author: mizuidekazuhiro
body:
### Motivation
- The fetch pipeline was saving navigation or whole-paper text instead of article bodies due to a longest-candidate selection and permissive fallbacks.  
- Notion metadata that used to be written (Source, Fetch/FullText status, Text Length, Image counts, etc.) stopped being populated.  
- The Playwright context variable was being shadowed by a dict (candidate) which caused `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'close'` and crashed runs.

### Description
- Reworked article extraction logic in `scripts/nikkei_fetch_articles_full.py` to restore prioritized candidate selection (JSON-LD, `#__NEXT_DATA__`, `article`, `main`, `.cmn-section`, `[data-track-article-body]`, explicit article-body classes) and removed `[class*="content"]` and `document.body.innerText` as primary body selectors, plus added `validate_article_body` and helper functions (`clean_article_text`, `article_body_quality_metrics`, `is_probably_navigation_text`) to reject navigation/paper-index content and short/noisy bodies; candidate diagnostics are written to `logs/nikkei_article_dom_candidates.jsonl`.  
- Fixed Playwright context handling by renaming browser context variable to `context`, using `candidate` for selector loop items, adding a safe `context` close in `finally` and robust route-handler error swallowing to prevent `dict.close()` regressions and route/close exceptions from crashing the run.  
- Restored schema-aware Notion metadata writes in `scripts/nikkei_save_articles_to_notion.py` by detecting existing DB properties, using typed setters (`title/rich_text/select/multi_select/number/checkbox/date/url`) and only updating properties that exist with compatible types, skipping mismatches without raising, and ensuring `Source`, `Fetch Status`, `Full Text Status`, `Text Length`, `Image Count`, `Has Image`, `Has Chart`, `Image URL`, and `Image Caption` are written when available while never writing rejected navigation text as the article body.  
- Extended scoring flow in `scripts/nikkei_score_articles.py` to derive grouped tag outputs (`country_tags`, `sector_tags`, `importance_tags`, `business_impact_areas`, `watch_themes`) from Notion Rules DB `RuleType`, and ensured `body_used_for_scoring` excludes navigation-like bodies.  
- Enhanced `scripts/nikkei_update_notion_scores.py` to page through Notion query results, prefer `page_id` when present, and conditionally update additional score-related properties (Business Impact Areas, Watch Themes, Country/Sector/Importance Tags, Negative Matches, Score Breakdown, Body Used For Scoring) only if those properties exist.  
- Small helpers and behavior: normalized Notion existing-URL keys to include `ng:<id>` variants for reliable page-id lookup; preserved saving of `title`, `url`, `issue_date`, and `edition` even when body extraction fails.

Files touched: `scripts/nikkei_fetch_articles_full.py`, `scripts/nikkei_save_articles_to_notion.py`, `scripts/nikkei_score_articles.py`, `scripts/nikkei_update_notion_scores.py`, `scripts/run_nikkei_paper_pipeline.py` (flow adjustments and integrations).  

### Testing
- Ran compilation checks with `python -m compileall scripts src` and targeted `python -m py_compile` on modified scripts, which succeeded.  
- Ran unit tests with `pytest -q` (full test suite), which passed (`112 passed`).  
- Also ran targeted tests `pytest -q tests/test_nikkei_fetch_articles_full.py tests/test_nikkei_save_articles_to_notion.py tests/test_nikkei_update_notion_scores.py`, which passed (`10 passed`).

body:
Similar movies on the detail page were capped at 8 with no way to paginate. This adds a "Daha fazla film gör" button that activates infinite scroll for subsequent pages.

## Hook (`useMovieDetail`)
- Removed `.slice(0, 8)` cap; initial load now returns full page 1 results
- Added `similarPage`, `similarTotalPages`, `loadingMoreSimilar` state

body: ## Summary PR #11 из дорожной карты после #10 — авторизация в NotebookLM прямо из панели вместо ручного `notebooklm login` локально + upload `storage_state.json`. ### Архитектура - Новый docker-compose-сервис **`browser`**: debian-slim с chromium + Xvfb + fluxbox + x11vnc + websockify + noVNC. CDP на `:9222` (только внутри docker-сети), noVNC на `:6080` (мапится наружу). - В панели — `BrowserSessionManager` (singleton, async-locked): connect_over_cdp → новый `BrowserContext` на `https://notebooklm.google.com` → следит за `page.url` и щёлкает статус `loading → pending → ready` когда видит NotebookLM origin. - Активная сессия в один момент времени **одна** на всю панель — второй юзер получит 409, пока первый не закончит / отменит / таймаутнётся (10 мин). Это потому что у нас один X-display в `browser`-контейнере, и иначе люди видели бы экраны друг друга. ### Endpoints (под `/api/google/notebooklm/auth`) - `POST /start` — стартует сессию, отдаёт `public_url` для iframe + статус - `GET /{id}` — поллинг, авто-флип в `ready` когда url совпал - `POST /{id}/save` — `context.storage_state()` → `users//notebooklm_storage.json` (туда же, куда писал ручной upload) - `POST /{id}/cancel` — снос сессии ### Frontend `/settings` → таб «Google» → блок NotebookLM расширен: кнопка «Авторизоваться через браузер», iframe на `public_url`, опрос каждые 2с, `Сохранить сессию` доступно когда статус `ready`. ### Тесты 6 router-тестов с Playwright-стабом (реальный браузер в CI не поднимается): - `start` возвращает метаданные сессии + `public_url` - поллер флипает в `ready` когда url совпал - `save` пишет storage_state.json и помечает `completed` - `save` 400-ит когда статус ≠ ready (нет полусохранённых файлов) - `cancel` сносит сессию - второй юзер получает 404 на сессию первого + 409 при попытке стартовать свою Всего 76 backend-тестов, ruff чисто, фронт билдится, `svelte-check` 0 errors. ### Deploy Обновил `DEPLOY.md` и `.env.example` с инструкциями по новому сервису и `PANEL_BROWSER_CDP_URL` / `PANEL_BROWSER_PUBLIC_URL`. Дефолтный `PANEL_BROWSER_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:6080` подходит для локальных тестов; на VPS его надо выставить на хостнейм/IP, иначе iframe в браузере юзера не сможет подключиться. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] `docker compose build && docker compose up -d` — оба контейнера (`parser-panel` и `parser-browser`) поднимаются, `docker compose ps` показывает их healthy - [ ] В `/settings` → Google → NotebookLM нажать «Авторизоваться через браузер» — должен появиться iframe с экраном Chromium на сервере - [ ] Залогиниться в Google в этом iframe; когда страница NotebookLM загрузится, статус должен переключиться на «NotebookLM открыта», после `Сохранить сессию` — пилл «авторизован» должен заиграть зелёным - [ ] Параллельно с админовской сессией зайти под другим юзером — кнопка «Авторизоваться» должна вернуть 409 «browser_busy» - [ ] Запустить parse-job с галкой NotebookLM — должна успешно использовать сохранённый `storage_state.json` ### Notes Yellow risk. Изменения нетривиальные: новый docker-сервис, async lifecycle для Playwright, кросс-пользовательская блокировка. CI прогоняет mock-тесты, но конечная проверка `connect_over_cdp` ↔ реальный chromium тестируется только end-to-end на VPS. Зависимость от PR #12 (data-loss safety fix) — мерджить лучше после него, чтобы база была чище. Конфликтов между ними нет. ## Related Issue

N/A — proactive tooling improvement.


## Changes

Codify the project's code conventions through tooling, and expose npm scripts that CI/CD can call directly in a follow-up.

- **Prettier** with `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` for deterministic Tailwind class ordering. Config: `printWidth: 100`, double quotes, semicolons, LF line endings, `trailingComma: "all"`.
- **commitlint** config (`@commitlint/config-conventional` with `i18n` type added) to validate PR titles. Workflow is not enabled in this PR — a follow-up PR will add it.
- **`.editorconfig`** and **`.gitattributes`** for IDE/Git consistency across contributors (especially Windows).
- **`.git-blame-ignore-revs`** so contributors can skip the bulk-format commit in `git blame`. The squash SHA will be appended in a follow-up PR (it cannot be known until this PR merges).
- **New npm scripts** in `package.json`: `format`, `format:check`, `typecheck`, `lint:fix`, `commitlint`.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** — added "Code Conventions", "Local Verification", and "git blame hygiene" sections. Fixed `dictionaries/` → `locales/` path typo.
- **PR template** — added checkboxes for `format:check`, `typecheck`, and Conventional Commits title. (This PR introduces the new template, so its checklist may differ from older PRs.)
- **CLAUDE.md** — listed the new npm scripts and added a pointer to CONTRIBUTING.md.
- **Bulk format pass** — applied `npm run format` to the whole codebase (31 files). Mostly Tailwind class reordering plus minor wrap/trailing-comma adjustments. No behavioral changes.

Wiring CI is intentionally left out of this PR. Once merged, two steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` complete the gate:

```yaml
- name: Format check
  run: npm run format:check

- name: Type check
  run: npm run typecheck
```


## How to Verify

1. npm install
2. npm run format:check → All matched files use Prettier code style!
3. npm run lint → passes with no warnings
4. npm run typecheck → passes (already strict: true)
5. npm run build → succeeds
6. Smoke-test commitlint:
```bash
echo "feat: bogus"  | npx commitlint   # passes
echo "weird: bogus" | npx commitlint   # fails (type-enum)
echo "i18n: add ja" | npx commitlint   # passes (validates the override)
```
7. Open any component (e.g. components/RepoCard.tsx) and confirm Tailwind classes are sorted by the plugin.


## Checklist

- [x] `npm run format:check` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run build` passes
- [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `i18n:`)

- `memberType`: 회원의 최초 활동 기수와 현재 활동 기수가 같으면 `YB`, 아니면 `OB`

- 예시: `16기, 17기` 트랙을 가진 회원이 현재 활동 기수 `17기`에 참여 중이면 `OB + activityStatus=true`

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["관리자: 활동 기수 변경"] --> B["active_generation 값 변경"]
    B --> C["승인 회원 + 트랙 조회"]

    K -->|REGISTERING / WAITING| L["요청 정보 반영 + WAITING 유지"]
    K -->|APPROVED| M["409 MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS"]
    K -->|REJECTED| N["403 ADMIN_REJECTED"]
```

- `./gradlew test`
- 승인 회원 동기화 단위 테스트 추가
- `memberType` / `activityStatus` 분리 정책 테스트 추가

author: kubestellar-hive[bot]
body:
Fixes #11856
Fixes #11857
Fixes #11859

## Problem

The `/enterprise/risk-matrix`, `/enterprise/risk-register`, and `/enterprise/risk-appetite` pages show a "Failed to fetch" error banner while simultaneously rendering `UnifiedDashboard` cards with misleading empty states ("No Score", "No Data", "No active alerts"). This creates conflicting UI signals — the user sees both an error AND content that implies the system is healthy.

## Root Cause

Each risk page renders two independent sections:
1. A `*Content` component with proper error/loading handling
2. A `UnifiedDashboard` component that renders cards regardless of the content fetch status

When the API fails, only the content component shows the error. The UnifiedDashboard cards still render their default empty states.

## Fix

1. **State coordination**: Content components now report their loading/error state to the parent via `onStateChange` callback
2. **Conditional rendering**: `UnifiedDashboard` is only rendered when content successfully loads (not during error or loading states)
3. **Enhanced error UX**: Error state now shows:
   - Descriptive title ("Unable to load risk matrix data")
   - Error details
   - Retry button to re-fetch data

## Testing

- When API fails → only error panel with retry button shown, no misleading cards
- When API succeeds → full dashboard renders normally with UnifiedDashboard cards
- Retry button triggers a fresh fetch cycle

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the project’s development tooling, documentation, and packaging workflow. The most significant changes are the addition of comprehensive code quality configurations, a major rewrite and expansion of the `README.md` for clarity and onboarding, and refinements to the release packaging process to support all sub-packages. Additionally, legacy CMake build files have been removed in favor of Conan-based workflows.

**Key changes:**

**1. Documentation and Onboarding Improvements**
- The `README.md` has been rewritten and greatly expanded to clarify the purpose and usage of the three header-only packages (`core`, `consumer`, `producer`). It now includes detailed quick start instructions, API examples, Conan/CMake usage, development workflow, troubleshooting, architecture, and performance sections.

**2. Code Quality Tooling**
- Added `.clang-format` to enforce consistent code style (LLVM-based, 4-space indent, Allman braces, etc.).
- Added `.clang-tidy` with a curated set of checks (bugprone, performance, modernize, readability, cppcoreguidelines) and disables noisy/conflicting checks. Custom options for member variable naming and initialization style are included.
- Added `.clangd` configuration to pin the toolchain, suppress known false positives, and fine-tune diagnostics for the codebase, including context-specific suppressions for Conan and test directories.

**3. Packaging and Release Workflow**
- Updated the GitHub Actions release workflow to export and package all sub-packages (`coderoast_ipc_core`, `coderoast_ipc_consumer`, `coderoast_ipc_producer`) into the Conan tarball, and clarified release notes to reflect this. author: ilyakislenko
body:
## Что меняется

Раньше у каждого урока внизу была подпись \"Раздел: X / + Назначить раздел\", и **она же** была редактором. Над уроком висел отдельный sticky header с тем же текстом. Двойная отрисовка названия + редактирование chapter'а только через урок (а не через секцию) = шум и боль когда нужно переименовать всю секцию.

Переделал по паттернам Udemy / Teachable / Notion:

- Из плоского \`course.videos\` строится массив \`ChapterRun[]\` — соседние уроки с одинаковым \`chapterTitle\` склеиваются в один run.
- Каждый run рендерит **один** \`ChapterHeaderRow\` — единственное место где название показано и редактируется.
- Click на header → inline-input. Enter / \"Сохранить\" коммитит, Escape отменяет.
- Save вызывает \`updatePlaylistVideo\` через \`Promise.all\` для всех уроков в run'е → переименовывает раздел целиком за один тап.
- Уроки без раздела попадают в псевдо-секцию \"Без раздела — нажмите, чтобы назначить\" (italic, muted). Клик и ввод названия превращает её в новую главу.

\`SortableLessonRow\` упростился:
- Снёс state \`editingChapter\` / \`chapterDraft\`.
- Снёс нижний div с \`Раздел: X\` / \`+ Назначить раздел\`.
- Убрал props \`showChapterHeader\` и \`onSetChapter\`.

\`handleSetChapter(video, value)\` (один-к-одному) → \`handleRenameChapter(videoIds[], value)\` (массовый) — отражает что теперь редактирование идёт на уровне run'а.

\`buildChapterRuns()\` — module-level helper, легко тестируется.

## Не делается в этом PR (намеренно)
- Кросс-секционное перетаскивание уроков (drag урока в чужую секцию + автонаследование chapterTitle от соседей) — отдельная задача. Сейчас drag меняет порядок, chapterTitle остаётся прежним.
- Bulk-endpoint на сервере для переименования. Сейчас 5 уроков = 5 PATCH'ей через Promise.all. Для типичного раздела (3-10 уроков) ок, batch добавим если будут жалобы на латентность.

## Test plan (всё прогнал в Playwright локально)
- [x] Открыть курс с разделами → один header per раздел, никаких \"Раздел: X\" под уроками.
- [x] Клик на \"КЕКСИК\" header → inline-input → переименовал в \"КЕКСИКИ\" → Enter → раздел стал \"КЕКСИКИ\".
- [ ] Курс без разделов → видна одна секция \"Без раздела — нажмите, чтобы назначить\". Клик → ввод имени → все уроки уехали под новый раздел.
- [ ] Drag-and-drop порядка в пределах раздела работает как раньше.

author: y-oga-819
body:
## 概要 (What)

ADR 0036 のシンプル世界観 (登録 → 上から順にやる) を TaskForm 1 画面で成立させる。`body` 欄追加 (ADR 0037) / 主観サイズの 7 段階 `task_size` 必須化 (ADR 0038) / `project` 任意化 (ADR 0039) を UI / gateway / e2e に同時に取り込む。

## 関連 Issue

Closes #170

## 背景 (Why)

[ADR 0036](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0036-simplify-task-registration-workflow.md) で確定した「default 経路は登録 → 上からやる」を実装に落とし込むタイミング。現状の TaskForm は次の 3 点で ADR の方針と乖離していた:

- `body` 入力欄が無く、AI 分解 (`buildDecomposePrompt`) に渡せる文脈が title だけ
- 見積もり入力が分単位 number input で、登録時の認知負荷が高い
- `project` 必須で、Inbox 的な「後で決める」運用が成立しない

これらを 1 画面で解消し、補正エンジン (ADR 0024〜0026) は `estimated_minutes` 軸のまま温存する (ADR 0038)。

派生 ADR: [0037](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0037-task-form-single-entry-with-body.md) / [0038](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0038-task-size-enum.md) / [0039](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0039-task-project-edit-and-cascade.md)。
DB / 型 / AI prompt 層は #169 (PR #175) で先行導入済み。

## Before → After (概念・フロー・メンタルモデル)

**Before:**
- 「タスク登録」の入力 IF が title / project / 分単位見積もり / 依存イベントの 4 軸
- 主観サイズと AI 推定が `estimated_minutes` 1 軸に潰れていて、Phase 4 で「ユーザーの見積もり傾向」と「AI 推定の精度」を別シグナルとして見られない
- project が必須で、Inbox 的に「後で決める」が成立せず、登録ミス時の手戻りは「削除 → 再登録」しかない
- AI 分解が登録経路で title しか文脈にできず、構造化された依頼 (例: 数百文字の手順 / 制約) を表現できない

**After:**
- 入力 IF は `title (必須)` / `body 任意` / `task_size 7 段階 (必須)` / `project 任意` / 依存イベント
- 主観サイズ (`task_size`) と AI 推定 (`estimated_minutes`) は別軸で並存。登録時は前者のみで、後者は AI 分解 / 補正の責務に倒す
- project は登録時任意。未指定なら `project_id=NULL` で入り、後から TaskDetailPanel 側で付け替えできる前提を作る (伝播 RPC 自体は #171 で実装)
- `body` を `buildDecomposePrompt` の文脈にできるので、構造化された依頼を AI 分解にそのまま流せる

## 追加したテスト (How verified)

- [x] `typecheck` / `lint` / `vitest run` (544 tests) すべて pass
- [x] TaskDetailPanel に `task_size` override の 8 ケース追加 (button → select / 値域 / null 戻し / blur / 同値選択時のスキップ)
- [x] e2e `task-crud.spec.ts` に「project 未指定 / body 空でも `project_id=NULL` / `body=''` で入る」ケース新規追加
- [x] e2e `task-crud.spec.ts` 既存「title / project / 見積もり」ケースを `task_size='1h'` / `body` 永続化 / `estimated_minutes=NULL` の検証に書き換え
- [x] e2e 全 task 作成経路 (10 ファイル) に `radio "30分"` クリックを差し込み、`プロジェクト (任意)` label 変更に追従

未カバー: e2e の TaskDetailPanel 側 `task_size` 編集経路 (今回は unit でカバー済 / dogfooding で詰める)。

## リリース前チェックリスト (When / Before merge)

- [x] DB migration 不要 (#169 / PR #175 で `tasks.task_size` 列は既に main にある)
- [x] 環境変数 / シークレット 追加なし
- [x] 既存タスク (`task_size IS NULL`) は引き続き読み書きでき、後方互換が保たれる
- [x] 既存ユーザーへの破壊的変更なし (登録 UI が変わるが、データ shape は #169 で既に整っている)

## このPRの範囲外 (Out of scope)

- TaskDetailPanel から `project_id` を編集する UI と、親 → 子 / 子 → 兄弟+親 への伝播 RPC ([ADR-0039](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0039-task-project-edit-and-cascade.md) の RPC 部分) — **#171 で別実装**
- 親共有タスク群のグルーピング操作 + 新規タスクの Top 直下挿入 ([ADR-0040](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0040-new-task-insert-position-top.md) / [ADR-0041](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-parent-shared-grouping-reorder.md)) — **#172 で別実装**
- `task_size` の Stack View 行カードへの badge 表示 (今は `estimated_minutes=NULL` の行は時間表示が出ない。dogfooding で違和感を観察してから別 issue 化判断)
- 「秘書から相談があります」モード ([#173](https://github.com/y-oga-819/kozutsumi/issues/173) / 将来構想)

Změny zavádí jednu kanonickou definici sdílenou napříč skilly i pravidly:

- **`skills/refactor-entry-point-to-action/SKILL.md`** — přebírá pravidlo do constraints.

author: xwiz
body:
## Doris

The events / process_connections / process_lineage / file_accesses / db_queries tables in 0001_events_pipeline.up.sql declared \`node_id\` between \`tenant_id\` and the timestamp column, but the DUPLICATE KEY (event_date, tenant_id, ts[, ...]) skipped node_id.

Doris requires KEY columns to be an ordered prefix of the schema. Prod was failing every controlplane startup with:

\`\`\`
KeyColumns[2] (starts from zero) is ts, but corresponding column is node_id in the previous columns declaration
\`\`\`

…and falling back to the mock engine for everything that hits Doris.

Verified live on the VPS: \`SHOW TABLES FROM controlone\` lists only \`doris_migrations\` (zero rows). None of the five tables ever existed; no data to lose.

Fix: reorder columns so each table's KEY columns come first; node_id and the rest of the payload follow. Writers all use named-column INSERTs, so the column reorder is safe.

## UI

\`NodeStatusBadge\` crashed the entire shell (\`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'healthy')\`) when the fleet endpoint responded without a \`totals\` field, which happened whenever Doris was in fallback. Default to all-zero totals when \`data?.totals\` is missing so the badge renders 0/0 instead of taking the rest of the app down.

body:
## Summary

Switches every customer-display query from the legacy `customer_regions`
snapshot (272 rows, frozen) to the `customers` master + `salespersons`
+ `regions` lookups. PR #12 worked around the mismatch with a banner;
this PR removes the mismatch.

No schema change in this PR — `customer_regions` stays on disk. A
follow-up PR can DROP it once we're confident no reader remains.

## What changes for the user

- Customer summary card no longer shows "(snapshot)" labels or the
  blue D1-pending banner. The values shown are the master record.
- Reassignments from PR #12 take effect immediately on the same page.
- Customers BSN-only (no `customers` row) now show a "ยังไม่มีใน
  master" badge on their summary so admins can see where the data
  is incomplete.
- The `/customers` region filter is a real dropdown of all 35 regions
  (code + name_th when set), driven by the master.
- New admin page `/regions` for filling in `regions.name_th` and
  `sort_order` (35 rows are still code-only from the migration-010
  seed).

## Backwards compatibility

- `?region=<code|name_th>` legacy URLs still work; the resolver maps
  them to `region_id`. If a legacy text doesn't resolve, the page
  flashes a warning rather than silently showing all customers.
- Mobile `/m/sales-trip` chips switched from `?region=<text>` to
  `?region_id=<int>`. Old bookmarks resolve via the same fallback.
- `customer_regions` is left in place — no caller reads it after this
  PR but the data is still recoverable.

## Hardening from code review (post-review fixes applied)

- Mobile sales-trip groups customers by `region_id` (FK), not by
  display name — eliminates the bug where two regions with identical
  `name_th` would merge into one section.
- Legacy `?region=` that fails to resolve now flashes a warning so
  the user understands why all customers showed up.
- Comment in app.py describes the regions_admin gate accurately.

WARNs left in code (not blocking, follow-up):
- `regions.sort_order` has no DB CHECK — admin can set negatives.
- `salesperson_orphan` returns SQL int (0/1); template usage is fine
  but JSON serialization should account for the encoding.

## Test plan

- [x] Smoke test all 4 query paths against live DB:
      - active sp + master → full name shown
      - orphan code (e.g. "21") → raw code + ⚠️ orphan badge
      - BSN-only (no master row) → fallback to NULL + missing-master badge
      - region.name_th NULL → falls back to code (e.g. "กท")
- [x] `?region_id=3` filters to 68 customers; legacy `?region=กท`
      resolves to the same 68 (compat verified).
- [x] All routes register and respond 302 to login.
- [ ] Browser verification:
      1. /customers — region dropdown shows code + name_th, filter works
      2. Click into a customer with master record → no banner, value
         matches reassign form
      3. Click into a BSN-only customer → "ยังไม่มีใน master" badge
      4. /m/sales-trip — region chips by code, filter works
      5. /regions (admin) — fill name_th for "กท" → "กรุงเทพฯ", save,
         verify it appears in /customers dropdown

author: tobias-eberle
body:
The previous output was five separate HTML files (topology, hotspots, staleness, duplication, type_distribution), each with its own table and chart, each pulling in Plotly's full ~3 MB JS bundle separately. A user opening the report folder didn't know where to start.

Now: one self-contained `dashboard.html`. The CSVs and the RAG JSONL still ship for downstream tooling, but the HTML story is one page, in one logical reading order:

  Hero          Status pill + run id + root path + finished-at.
  KPI strip     Files / Total size / Stale (5y+) / Duplication /
                RAG-ready (+ Errors when non-zero). CSS Grid with
                auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr) so it reflows on narrow
                windows.
  Topology      Treemap, full width — where the bytes live.
  Size hotspots Side-by-side depth-1 + depth-2 horizontal bars.
  Staleness     Cool-to-warm bucket bar (<1y green → 5y+ red).
  Duplication   Top-10 wasted-bytes bar + cluster sample paths.
  Types         MIME-category donut + top-extensions bar, side by side.
  RAG hand-off  Count + combined size + filename pointer to the JSONL.

Each section gets a one-sentence blurb explaining what the chart *means*, not what it *is*. Tables are stuffed under <details> so the page isn't a wall of HTML; click a row to expand.

Visual language:
- System font stack, calm muted palette (#fafafa background, #fff cards, #2563eb accent), tabular numbers, generous whitespace.
- _MIME_COLORS shared between Plotly traces and the CSS pill tags in the table — the donut, the treemap, and the inline category pills all line up.
- Staleness palette is a deliberate cool→warm gradient so the "5y+" bar looks the way users feel about it.

Plotly is inlined EXACTLY ONCE. The first chart uses include_plotlyjs="inline"; every subsequent chart uses include_plotlyjs=False and shares the global `Plotly` from the first load. Saves ~18 MB on a seven-chart page.
test_dashboard_inlines_plotly_only_once pins this; another test (test_dashboard_is_the_only_html) pins "no other *.html files".

Per-report modules are now CSV-only. share-analyzer report all still runs every registered report — produces dashboard.html plus the six CSVs and rag_candidates.jsonl. The old per-report HTML templates (_base.html.j2, topology.html.j2, …) are gone.

11 new tests (180 total): dashboard registered, run_all emits it, dashboard is the ONLY html, CSVs/JSONL still produced, self-contained (no CDN script tags), Plotly inlined at most once, every section heading present, every KPI label present, run metadata rendered, empty-share renders the empty-state copy without crashing, KPI total-bytes value matches `SUM(size)` from the index.

End-to-end smoke on a 66-file fixture share: dashboard.html is 4.6 MB (mostly the inlined Plotly bundle), six logical sections, zero CDN script tags, single window.PlotlyConfig declaration.

body:
## Summary

Adds two major features to ai-cli-runner:

1. **LLM cost calculation** via LiteLLM pricing data — auto-populates `cost_usd` on `AITokenUsage` when the CLI provider doesn't report it natively
2. **Model listing and validation** — discover available models per provider and validate model names

## Changes

### LLM Pricing (`llm_pricing.py`)
- `LLMPricingCache` with disk-based caching (`~/.cache/ai-cli-runner/litellm_pricing.json`)
- Respects `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, atomic writes (tmp + replace), directory mode `0o700`
- `load()` uses disk cache when fresh (<24h), `refresh()` forces network fetch
- Cost calculation with input/output/cache read/cache write token pricing
- Cursor model name resolution (routing suffix stripping, GPT/Claude/Gemini canonical key mapping)
- Background refresh with async start/stop (awaits cancelled tasks)
- Read-only `data` property via `MappingProxyType`

### Model Cache (`ai_models.py`)
- `AIModelCache` with TTL-based caching (1h)
- `list_models(provider)` — Claude/Gemini via LiteLLM data filtering, Cursor via `agent models` subprocess
- `is_valid_model(provider, model)` — True/False/None (None when cache empty)
- Process group isolation for Cursor subprocess (`start_new_session=True`)
- Parallel refresh via `asyncio.gather`

### Client Integration (`client.py`)
- Auto-populates `cost_usd` after JSON parsing when provider doesn't report it
- Uses primary model (highest output tokens) for Gemini multi-model pricing

### Gemini Multi-Model Improvements (`parsers.py`)
- Picks primary model for pricing instead of comma-joining names
- Deterministic tie-break (lexicographic)
- Documented as approximate pricing for multi-model responses

## New Dependencies
- `httpx` — HTTP client for fetching LiteLLM pricing data

## Testing
- 182 tests passing (ruff ✅, mypy ✅)
- Comprehensive tests for disk caching, cost calculation, model lookup, GPT resolver, client integration, model listing/validation
- Peer reviewed with Cursor (3 rounds)

Closes #17

body:
This PR adds test 6.2.19 for CSAF 2.0. 

Resolves #135 

Implementation has been extended to cover two different errors: 
a) the "written out" property (CVSS v2, v3.0, v3.1 `environmentalScore`, CVSS v4 `baseScore`) are set to non-zero
b) the calculated score, based on the vector, and extending by the JSON where the vector has fields empty / NotDefined, is non-zero

This allows us to cleanly cover some edge cases where property and calculation don't match, but also leads us to emit two errors on "regular" documents, i.e. where property and calculation are both non-zero.

author: sim590
body:
## Problem

When a focused floating window is moved to another workspace with `follow=true` (e.g. via `hy3:movetoworkspace <ws>,follow`), keyboard focus and active monitor do not reliably follow the window.

Two bugs combine to cause this:

**1. Wrong follow path when a tiled window exists on the origin workspace**

`getWorkspaceFocusedNode(origin)` returns the hy3 node of a tiled window on the origin workspace even though the focused window is floating (and has no hy3 node). The `if (node != nullptr)` branch in the follow block then calls `node->focus()` on that tiled window, stealing both keyboard focus and active monitor from the floating window we just moved.

**2. Monitor focus not explicitly updated**

`fullWindowFocus` and `monitor->changeWorkspace` do not call `rawMonitorFocus` directly. Monitor focus only updates as a side-effect of cursor warping via `simulateMouseMovement`, which is skipped when `misc:mouse_move_focuses_monitor = 0` or the cursor is already within the window bounds.

## Fix

- Introduce `moved_floating` to track whether the dispatched action moved a floating window. When true, skip the `node->focus()` path in the follow block even if `node != nullptr`.
- Call `fullWindowFocus` on the floating window to set keyboard focus with a keybind reason (hard focus), regardless of `input:follow_mouse`.
- Call `rawMonitorFocus` with the destination monitor explicitly so the active monitor is always correct, regardless of cursor position or `misc:mouse_move_focuses_monitor`.

## Reproduction

```
# hyprland.conf — bind mod+o to split-changemonitor
bind = $mod, o, split-changemonitor, +1
```

1. Open a floating terminal on monitor 1 and a tiled window on monitor 2
2. Focus the floating terminal
3. Press `mod+o` repeatedly — before this fix, focus would jump to the tiled window after the first move

## Summary

Complete rewrite of SlimSocial for Facebook from Flutter to native Android Kotlin, executed across 14 phased commits per the design spec and implementation plan in [`docs/superpowers/specs/`](docs/superpowers/specs/). The Flutter project under `SlimSocial_for_Facebook/` is **untouched** and keeps shipping; this PR adds a parallel `app/` Gradle module that will replace it once stable.

- **Native Kotlin + Jetpack Compose Material 3**, single Activity, manual DI — minSdk 24 / targetSdk 36
- **Two product flavors** (`full` for Play Store with Sentry + Play Billing + Play Review; `fdroid` with FOSS-only no-op stubs)
- **Feature parity** with the Flutter app: every existing CSS/JS rule ported verbatim (incl. ~6 KB dark-theme block, 23-language sponsor-keyword ad-blocker), all 22 legacy SharedPreferences keys preserved, all 41 app-link hosts replicated
- **Two-layer permission gate** ("total user control" — every permission off at first launch, WebView cannot bypass user toggles)
- **Render-process-gone recovery** ("Facebook stopped responding — Reload" inline overlay; no host crash on low-RAM devices)
- **In-app log viewer + Sentry** (full flavor only) with FB-session-cookie scrubbing
- **Custom CSS / JS / UA / proxy editor** with one-time JS-runs-in-your-session warning dialog
- **42 locales** ported from `assets/lang/*.json` to Android `res/values-<locale>/strings.xml`
- **426 unit + Robolectric tests** across both flavors, suite runs in ~22 s

author: melanieing
body:
… Slack

EPIC 3 lands as a single .github/workflows/ci.yml that covers tasks 3.0 through 3.6. The job graph is changes -> test -> build-scan-push -> notify, with the path-filter output driving a service matrix that flows through the rest.

What it does, by job:
- changes (R-B1-M2 path filter): dorny/paths-filter splits work by service. A small bash step folds the boolean outputs into a JSON array (services) and a flag (has-changes) so downstream jobs run only for the services that actually moved.
- test (R-B1-M2 unit-test gate): matrix over the changed services, setup-python 3.14 (matches Dockerfile FROM line), pip cache keyed on per-service requirements.txt, pytest with --tb=short. Failure here kills build-scan-push, so the build is gated on tests.
- build-scan-push (R-B1-O1, R-B1-M2, R-B2-M2, R-B2-M3, R-B2-O1): buildx + GHA cache-from/to per service for fast rebuilds; build with load:true so Trivy can scan the local image. Trivy then runs twice - once with severity=HIGH,CRITICAL and exit-code=1 as the gate, once full-report with exit-code=0 for the PR comment via marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment (sticky avoids comment spam on rebases). On main pushes only, build-push-action runs again with push:true (cache makes it almost free) to publish ghcr.io/<owner>/<service>:<sha> and :sha-<short>.
- notify (R-B1-M3 Slack): always() so failures notify too. Reads needs.<job>.result, paints success/failure with emoji + color, and posts to #deploy-status via slackapi/slack-github-action. Step is gated on env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL != '' so the workflow passes even before the secret is set (graceful onboarding).

Other touches:
- Re-enable github-actions ecosystem in .github/dependabot.yml now that the workflows directory has real .yml in it (closing the loop with troubleshooting/2026-05-04-dependabot-actions-no-workflows.md).
- Trivy stays on the post-incident 0.36.0 release tag with an inline note recommending SHA pin for production hardening.
- Concurrency group cancels in-flight runs on PR pushes but preserves main history.

Verification done in sandbox before commit:
- yaml.safe_load on ci.yml parses cleanly with 4 jobs, 3 triggers
- jsonschema validation against https://json.schemastore.org/github-workflow.json: pass
- jsonschema validation of dependabot.yml against https://json.schemastore.org/dependabot-2.0.json: pass (3 entries)
- actionlint v1.7.12 on ci.yml: clean (exit 0; checks unknown action keys, expression syntax, matrix shape, secrets context, job graph, embedded shell scripts)
- yamllint: 1 stylistic warning on 'on:' as YAML 1.1 truthy, which GHA accepts; intentionally not silenced.

End-to-end execution can only happen after merge to main; first real run will produce the metrics for task 3.2 (parallel vs serial build time) and the PR-comment screenshot for 3.5. BACKLOG marked accordingly (✅ for code, 🟡 for the post-merge measurement bits).

Per the agreed strategy A, this needs a PR + merge for Dependabot to keep tracking the new actions and for any subsequent push to trigger the pipeline.

author: atri-jar
body:
## What broke

drift-check has been failing on **every aurum-mcp PR opened after any aurum-android push to main**, even when the actual content (components, tokens, icons, codeConnect, changelog) is byte-identical. We ran into this twice today already (PR #6 and PR #8 both ate spurious drift failures + needed sync-first dance).

Cause: aurum-android's gallery rebuild updates three fields in the emitted manifest on every deploy regardless of content:

| Field | What it is | Why it changes |
|---|---|---|
| `aurum.sha` | Aurum git commit SHA at gallery deploy time | Every push to aurum-android main |
| `meta.generatedAt` | ISO timestamp from `generate.py` | Every gallery rebuild |
| `meta.manifestSha` | SHA-256 hash over manifest content (excluding itself) | Rolls up the two above |

The byte-exact comparison was tripping on these. Once branch protection made `drift` a hard required check, this turned into **mandatory two-PR friction** (sync first → then your real PR) on every aurum-mcp change after any aurum-android merge — even when content is identical.

## Industry-standard fix

Field exclusion at compare time. Same pattern as `kustomize` CI for k8s manifest drift, npm's package-lock churn detection, and similar config-as-code drift gates. Considered alternatives (annotated schemas, content-hashed everything, two-tier comparison) — overkill for our case.

```diff
- jq --sort-keys . data/manifest.json     > /tmp/local-canon.json
- jq --sort-keys . /tmp/live-manifest.json > /tmp/live-canon.json
+ SCRUB='del(.aurum.sha, .meta.generatedAt, .meta.manifestSha)'
+ jq --sort-keys "$SCRUB" data/manifest.json     > /tmp/local-canon.json
+ jq --sort-keys "$SCRUB" /tmp/live-manifest.json > /tmp/live-canon.json
```

## What's still gated

Real content drift in any of these still fails the diff and blocks the PR:
- `schemaVersion`
- `aurum.{library, version, platforms}`
- `meta.{figmaFileKey, galleryUrl}`
- `components`, `tokens`, `icons`, `codeConnect`, `changelog`

That's everything that affects MCP responses.

## Edge cases I checked

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Live URL 404 | Soft-skip with warning (existing behaviour) |
| Bundled has fewer components than live | Real content drift → fails ✓ |
| Schema later adds a new volatile field | Extend the `SCRUB` filter; `jq del()` is no-op on missing keys so it stays forward-safe |
| Manual hand-edit of bundled provenance fields | Passes drift but is harmless (provenance isn't load-bearing) |
| Numeric-formatting / whitespace | `--sort-keys` canonicalises both sides |

## Verified locally

- **Volatile-only diff** (the failing case): scrub passes ✓
- **Tampered `aurum.version`** (real content): scrub correctly detects version mismatch ✓

## Threat model

Scrubbing `aurum.sha` + `meta.manifestSha` means a malicious contributor could lie about which upstream commit a bundled manifest came from. They **cannot** lie about `aurum.version` (still in diff), schema version, or content. Acceptable for our internal-team threat model — the protection is right-sized for "accidental drift" not "malicious tampering". If the threat model ever changes (e.g. external contributors), revisit by signing the manifest at gallery deploy time.

## Test plan

- [x] Local volatile-only test passes
- [x] Local real-content tampering test fails (correctly)
- [ ] CI: PR's own `drift` check should pass (this PR doesn't change manifest content)
- [ ] After merge: confirm subsequent aurum-mcp PRs opened after aurum-android pushes to main no longer eat spurious drift failures

author: rc-int
body:
## Summary

After PR #4 the `review / code-review` check reports SUCCESS for Dependabot PRs (was SKIPPED), but consumer PRs are still BLOCKED on `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED` from branch protection's `required_approving_review_count: 1`. There's no human reviewer for machine-generated version bumps, so PRs sit blocked indefinitely (concrete repro: rc-international/leadminer#40).

This adds a reusable workflow that posts an APPROVE review as `valors-release-bot` for Dependabot PRs only. GitHub excludes `GITHUB_TOKEN` reviews from the approving-review-count, so the bot's app token (RELEASE_APP_ID / RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) is required. Consumer caller workflows must invoke this via `pull_request_target` (not `pull_request`) so org Actions secrets are available — Dependabot PRs under `pull_request` run with restricted secrets.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/dependabot-approve.yml` (new file)
  - Reusable workflow `on: workflow_call`, declares `RELEASE_APP_ID` + `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` as required secrets.
  - Single job `approve` gated `if: github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'` (defense-in-depth alongside caller-side guard).
  - Two steps: generate app token via `actions/create-github-app-token@v1`, then `jq | gh api repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews --method POST --input -` with `event: "APPROVE"`.
  - Mirrors the JSON-via-stdin pattern already used in `scripts/ci-review.ts` for the human-PR APPROVE path.

## Why pull_request_target is safe here

`pull_request_target` is normally risky because it runs with write permissions against the base repo. The risk only materialises if you check out the PR's HEAD and execute code from it (build, test, lint). This workflow does **neither** — it only generates an app token and calls the GitHub REST API. There's no path for PR-controlled code to run.

## Operator Deploy Steps

Reusable workflow consumed via `@main`. Deploy = merge to main. The workflow does nothing on its own until a consumer wires it in.

1. Merge this PR.
2. Open follow-up PR in `rc-international/leadminer` adding a `pull_request_target` job to `.github/workflows/code-review.yml` that calls `dependabot-approve.yml` for Dependabot.
3. After that lands, re-run the dependabot workflow on leadminer#40 (or push an empty commit to the dependabot branch) and observe the auto-APPROVE from `valors-release-bot`.
4. Verify leadminer#40 becomes mergeable.

## Expected Outcomes

- [ ] After consumer wiring lands, a Dependabot PR shows a review from `valors-release-bot[bot]` with state `APPROVED` and the canned body text.
- [ ] `gh pr view <N> --repo <consumer> --json reviewDecision --jq .reviewDecision` returns `APPROVED` (was `REVIEW_REQUIRED`).
- [ ] `gh pr view <N> --repo <consumer> --json mergeStateStatus --jq .mergeStateStatus` returns something other than `BLOCKED` once other gates pass.
- [ ] On a non-dependabot PR in any consumer, the new workflow's job shows as SKIPPED (job-level `if:` guard) and has no effect on review state.

## Verification gap

Reusable workflows triggered via `workflow_call` cannot be exercised pre-merge from a branch — consumer callers pin `@main`. Pre-merge I verified:

- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/dependabot-approve.yml'))"` → OK
- `jq -n '{event: "APPROVE", body: "..."}'` → produces well-formed JSON identical in shape to what `ci-review.ts` posts today
- The `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` invocation matches the existing `code-review.yml` byte-for-byte

Live end-to-end verification requires merge + the leadminer follow-up + a real Dependabot trigger. Calling the gap out explicitly per `pre-merge-deploy-verify`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/dependabot-approve.yml')); j=d['jobs']['approve']; assert 'dependabot[bot]' in j['if']; assert any(s.get('uses','').startswith('actions/create-github-app-token') for s in j['steps']); assert any('reviews' in s.get('run','') and 'APPROVE' in s.get('run','') for s in j['steps']); print('OK')"` → exits 0
- [ ] After merge + leadminer follow-up: `gh run list --repo rc-international/leadminer --workflow "Dependabot Auto-Approve" --branch dependabot/uv/uv-0889c57075 --limit 1 --json conclusion --jq '.[0].conclusion'` → `success`
- [ ] After merge + leadminer follow-up: `gh pr view 40 --repo rc-international/leadminer --json reviews --jq '.reviews[] | select(.author.login=="valors-release-bot") | .state'` → `APPROVED`
- [ ] After merge + leadminer follow-up: `gh pr view 40 --repo rc-international/leadminer --json reviewDecision --jq .reviewDecision` → `APPROVED`

author: thoriqmacto
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 of the approved 9-phase ShelfDrive plan: **Drive scan + ebook indexing**. Connected Drive accounts now actually populate the database with the user's PDFs / EPUBs / CHMs / DJVUs.

## Scope choice — SDK-free for now

Phases 2–3 already use Laravel's HTTP client for OAuth, and the Drive REST `files.list` is straightforward. I'm keeping Phase 4 SDK-free to avoid yet another `composer.lock` round-trip. **`google/apiclient` lands in Phase 8** alongside chunked resumable uploads, where the SDK genuinely earns its keep — its lock update will ship in that same commit. Listing files, paginating, and (Phase 7) Range-streaming media bytes are all simple HTTP calls that don't need a wrapper.

## Scope choice — full scan only

Incremental sync via `changes.list` is deferred to a small follow-up. The scheduler ticks every 15 min and dispatches a *full* scan if `last_full_scan_at` is older than `DRIVE_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`; the field is named `full` deliberately so the next phase can just slot in a separate `IncrementalSync` job that consumes `start_page_token`.

## API

- **Models** (`app/Models/`): `DriveFile`, `EbookCategory`, `SyncRun`. `DriveFile` carries format constants, `scopeVisible` (hides trashed + removed-from-library), `normalizeFormat($mime, $name)` for MIME + extension fallback (`application/octet-stream` from Drive uploads still gets classified by extension), and `ebookSearchQuery()` for the `q=` param.
- **`App\Services\Google\DriveClient`**: thin Drive REST client over `Http::withToken()`, auto-refreshes the bound account's access token (60s leeway), marks the row `revoked` on `invalid_grant`, retries once on a 401. Carries `getFileMedia($account, $fileId, ?$range)` with optional Range header — the Phase 7 streaming proxy will reuse it.
- **`App\Services\Google\FileLister`**: pages through ebook files as a `Generator`, so scan jobs stream-process huge libraries without holding every page in memory.
- **`App\Jobs\Drive\ScanDriveAccount`** (`ShouldQueue`): opens a `SyncRun`, iterates `FileLister`, upserts `DriveFile` rows by `(connected_account_id, drive_file_id)`, and on completion marks any previously-indexed-but-not-seen file `trashed=true` (we **never** call `DELETE` on Drive). Records `files_seen / added / updated / removed`, sets `last_full_scan_at` on success. Skips `revoked`/`error` accounts.
- **Controllers** (`auth:sanctum`):
  - `GET /api/v1/library` — paginated, owner-scoped; `q`, `format`, `account_id`, `per_page` filters; hides trashed + removed-from-library.
  - `GET /api/v1/sync` — last 50 `sync_runs` across all owned accounts.
  - `POST /api/v1/sync/{account}/run` — dispatches `ScanDriveAccount`; refuses login-purpose and non-active accounts (`422`); foreign returns `404`.
- **`routes/console.php`**: `shelfdrive:scan-due-accounts` runs every 15 min, picks `purpose=drive` + `status=active` accounts whose `last_full_scan_at` is older than `DRIVE_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, dispatches a scan. Skipped in `testing` so PHPUnit doesn't fan out into queue work.

## Web

- `(app)/sync/page.tsx` + `SyncClient.tsx`: SWR list of Drive accounts with **Scan now** button (state-tracked dispatch), and a recent-runs table with status pill + `seen / + / ~ / -` counters; polls every 5s while the page is open.
- Nav link added.

## Tests
- `tests/Feature/Library/ScanDriveAccountTest.php` — 4 cases:
  - PDF/EPUB/CHM/DJVU/other classification across paginated pages with `tests/Support/FakeDriveClient` bound via the container (no network).
  - `SyncRun` records correct `seen / added / updated / removed` counts; `last_full_scan_at` advances.
  - Second pass marks missing files `trashed=true` without calling Drive.
  - Revoked accounts are skipped (no `SyncRun` row, no `DriveFile` rows).
- `tests/Feature/Library/IndexTest.php` — 5 cases: 401, owner-scoping, name search, format filter, trashed/removed-from-library exclusion.
- `tests/Feature/Sync/SyncControllerTest.php` — 5 cases: 401, owner-scoped index, dispatch happy path, foreign `404`, refusal of login-purpose + revoked accounts (uses `Bus::fake`).

Locally: **`php artisan test` → 82 passed (271 assertions)**; web `lint` + `typecheck` + `build` all green.

## Test plan
- [ ] `cd apps/api && php artisan test` passes
- [ ] `npm run -w apps/web lint && npm run -w apps/web typecheck && npm run -w apps/web build` pass
- [ ] With a connected `purpose=drive` account containing real ebook files, `/sync` → **Scan now** dispatches and within seconds the runs table shows a row with `status=success` and a non-zero `seen` count
- [ ] `GET /api/v1/library?account_id={id}&format=pdf&q=...` returns paginated results and never includes a foreign user's rows
- [ ] Trashing a file at Drive and re-scanning marks the row `trashed=true` (verify it disappears from `/library`)
- [ ] Phase 1 / 2 / 3 surfaces still work (sign in, connect / disconnect drive accounts)

## Notes
- `google/apiclient` is **deferred to Phase 8** with the `composer.lock` update committed there.
- `App\Services\Google\DriveClient::getFileMedia` is implemented but unused in this PR — Phase 7 wires `LibraryStreamController` against it for the Range-aware proxy.
- The scheduled job is intentionally a no-op in `testing`. Production needs a queue worker (`php artisan queue:work`) plus the Laravel scheduler tick (`php artisan schedule:run`).

body:
## Summary

- Added 3 new CSS tokens (`--accent-on-dark`, `--page-bg`, `--red-on-dark`) to cover missing dark-context variants
- Normalized all hardcoded hex values to palette tokens across every screen

## What changed

| Was | Fixed to |
|---|---|
| `#5EEAD4` (×4 hardcoded) | `var(--accent-on-dark)` |
| `#4ADE80` step-done (random Tailwind green) | `var(--accent-on-dark)` |
| `#F87171`/`#FCA5A5` upload error | `var(--red-on-dark)` |
| `#EEF2FF`/`#3730A3` IFRS 16 badge (indigo, off-brand) | `var(--brand-lt)`/`var(--brand)` |
| `#F0FDF4`/`#166534` ASC 842 badge | `var(--green-lt)`/`var(--green)` |
| `#FFF7ED`/`#9A3412` "Both" badge | `var(--amber-lt)`/`var(--amber)` |
| `#FAFBFD` table hover ×2 | `var(--surface)` |
| `#F8FAFC` term row hover | `var(--surface)` |
| `#FFFBEB` flagged/missing bg ×2 | `var(--amber-lt)` |
| Toast borders (`#166534`, `#991B1B`) | `var(--green)`, `var(--red)`, `var(--brand)` |
| Disclaimer/modal inline hex literals | `var(--ink-2)`, `var(--ink-3)`, `var(--surface)`, `var(--border)` |

## Why

Every hardcoded color was either a duplicate of an existing token (written as a raw hex) or an off-palette value (random Tailwind colors) inconsistent with the Navy + Teal design system. This pass ensures a single source of truth in `:root` — changing any token now propagates everywhere.

author: alex-bako
body:
## Summary

v0.2 Slice 1 — the load-bearing tracer bullet for v0.2. Implements the `claim` Knowledge Object end-to-end so that a user can write prose plus a `::claim object.id … -- body ::` block, run `adoc check` / `adoc build`, and get HTML containing the claim plus an agent-JSON document containing the flat record. Missing required fields, malformed grammar, and unknown block types each produce specific diagnostics and block artifact emission.

Closes #28. Refs parent #4.

## What's new (user-visible behavior)

- New AgentDoc Source syntax for top-level typed blocks:
  ```
  ::claim billing.credits
  status: verified
  owner: team-billing
  --
  Body content here.
  ::
  ```
- Renders to a `<section class="claim" id="…">` block in `dist/docs.html`.
- Adds a flat record to `dist/docs.agent.json`'s `objects[]` array with `id`, `kind: "claim"`, `status`, `body`, `page_id`, `source_span: {path, line, column}`, `fields: {…}`, and empty `relations`.
- Five new `DiagnosticCode` variants on the public surface:

  | Variant | Wire string |
  |---|---|
  | `SchemaMissingField` | `schema.missing_field` |
  | `SchemaDuplicateField` | `schema.duplicate_field` |
  | `ParseUnknownBlockType` | `parse.unknown_block_type` |
  | `ParseMalformedField` | `parse.malformed_field` |
  | `ParseMalformedOpenFence` | `parse.malformed_open_fence` |

- Three new public artifact types (`AgentJsonObject`, `AgentJsonRelations`, `AgentJsonSourceSpan`), pinned by `tests/public_surface.rs`.

## Implementation map (per commit)

| Commit | Scope |
|---|---|
| `feat(adoc-core): add Claim aggregate and value objects` | `Claim` aggregate plus `ClaimStatus` / `ClaimBody` / `ClaimFields` value objects with constructor-enforced invariants; `Display` + `Error` for `ObjectIdError` |
| `feat(adoc-core): introduce KnowledgeObjectPending and KnowledgeObject in BlockAst` | Two new boxed `BlockAst` variants and the transient `ParsedClaim` shell |
| `feat(adoc-core): add diagnostic codes for claim parsing and schema` | Five new `DiagnosticCode` variants with `as_str` mappings, pinned by `public_surface.rs` |
| `feat(adoc-core): parse and resolve top-level ::claim blocks` | Strict column-1 parser for `::claim` open fences, fields, body, and `::` close; resolver stage that rebuilds aggregates between `validate_pages` and `assemble_workspace` |
| `feat(adoc-core): render and emit Claim Knowledge Objects` | HTML `<section class="claim">` markup + structured `AgentJsonObject` and friends; `lib.rs` re-exports |
| `test: integration coverage for claim end-to-end` | Core integration tests, CLI smoke tests, golden HTML / agent-JSON fixtures under `tests/fixtures/v0_2/`, and `insta` snapshot pins |

## Key decisions

- **Resolver as a dedicated pipeline stage**, not a `ValidationRule` impl. Preserves ADR-0007's read-only validation invariant; existing rules are untouched. The orchestrator stays a linear sequence of named domain operations.
- **`KnowledgeObjectPending` is internal and transient**: the renderer and agent-JSON emitter both `unreachable!()` on it. The resolver guarantees no Pending block survives.
- **`ParsedClaim` lives in `domain/ast.rs`** because `BlockAst` references it; everything stays `pub(crate)`.
- **`AgentJsonObject` is shaped for the v0.2 claim record today**. Future Knowledge Object kinds will evolve the wire format when those slices land; the field set was chosen to match `V0-DESIGN.md` and AC #4 of #4.
- **Strict open-fence rejection per D11**: `::claim foo.bar trailing` emits `parse.malformed_open_fence` and does **not** open a block — accumulated valid fields are not lost because the fence never opened.

## Test plan

178 tests, all green. Validation gates run before each commit:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --locked` (178 passed, was 122 before this slice)
- [x] `cargo build --workspace --locked`
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked`

End-to-end sanity:

- [x] `adoc check tests/fixtures/v0_2/claim_basic.adoc` → exit 0, `0 errors`
- [x] `adoc check tests/fixtures/v0_2/claim_missing_status.adoc` → exit 1, `error[schema.missing_field]` on stdout, no artifacts written
- [x] `adoc build tests/fixtures/v0_2/claim_basic.adoc --out dist` → byte-identical to `claim_basic.golden.html` and `claim_basic.golden.agent.json`
- [x] `insta` snapshots pin the exact `adoc check` stdout/stderr shape for both fixtures

## Acceptance criteria mapping (from #4)

- ✅ Top-level `::claim object.id` blocks parse with fields, body, source file, source span — parser commit + parser unit tests
- ✅ Claims require `status` and body — `ClaimError::MissingStatus`/`MissingBody` + resolver
- ✅ Valid claim renders to HTML with kind, ID, status, body — render commit + golden HTML
- ✅ Valid claim emitted as flat record in `docs.agent.json` — emit commit + golden agent-JSON
- ✅ Missing-required-field diagnostics block artifact writes — existing severity gate in `build_artifacts` + resolver
- ✅ Tests cover positive and negative fixtures — `tests/fixtures/v0_2/claim_basic.*` + `claim_missing_status.adoc`
- ✅ Domain naming aligns with CONTEXT.md glossary (AgentDoc Source, Knowledge Object, Object ID, Agent-Facing Artifact)

## Out of scope (deferred per #28 / #4 plan)

- HTML metadata footer for optional fields (Slice 2)
- Workspace `id.duplicate` detection (Slice 3)
- Verified-claim invariants — `status: verified` requires owner + verified_at + evidence (v0.3)
- Closed enum for `ClaimStatus` lifecycle vocabulary (v0.3)
- Inline grammar inside claim bodies — emphasis, code, links (v0.3+)
- Field-name vocabulary enforcement (later v0.x slice)
- Other Knowledge Object kinds — `decision`, `warning`, `glossary` (later v0.x slices)
- Relation parsing (v0.5)
- Nested typed blocks (out of scope for v0 entirely)

## ADR references

- ADR-0005 (single public compile API) — five new `DiagnosticCode` variants and three new artifact types are now part of the public surface, pinned by `tests/public_surface.rs`.
- ADR-0006 (internal hexagonal ports) — no port changes; resolver is a free function inside `infrastructure/validate/`.
- ADR-0007 (validation as a separate pass) — resolver runs as a dedicated stage; `ValidationRule` stays read-only.
- ADR-0008 (test taxonomy) — inline `#[cfg(test)]` for VOs / parser / resolver units; `tests/compile_workspace.rs` for orchestrator integration; CLI golden fixtures plus `insta` snapshots in `crates/adoc-cli/tests/`.
- ADR-0009 (tactical DDD layout) — `domain/knowledge_object/` populated for the first time.

author: sanchit-crl
body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #168951.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

---

Previously, the ?cluster= query parameter only routed the initial page request to the correct tenant. The SPA's subsequent API calls (like fetch("uiconfig")) used relative URLs without ?cluster= and fell back to the default tenant. This caused the login page to show the wrong tenant's configuration — notably missing the OIDC button when OIDC was only enabled on a non-default tenant.

This also broke the OIDC login flow for non-default tenants: the IdP callback to /oidc/v1/callback carried no tenant routing signal since IdP redirects strip query parameters and headers. Without a tenant cookie, the callback routed to the default tenant where HMAC state validation failed.

Fix: httpMux now persists ?cluster= as the tenant select cookie after confirming the tenant exists via getServer(). The cookie survives the IdP redirect, fixing both the uiconfig routing and OIDC callback routing. The tenant dropdown is updated to sync ?cluster= in the URL when switching tenants to prevent stale URL params from overriding the cookie.

The existing TestOIDCEnabled is updated to find the oidc_secret cookie by name rather than assuming cookie index, since the tenant cookie may now precede it in the response.

Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/18iisJDa8_zp4tFvVO8qnFaTFrHhFRFOkSDmq6-6OF7k

Fixes: #166296
Epic: CRDB-54682

Release note (bug fix): Fixed a bug where the DB Console login page did not show the OIDC login button when navigating with ?cluster=<tenant> to a tenant with OIDC enabled. OIDC login on non-default virtual clusters now works correctly.

Release justification: OIDC login fails on non-default virtual clusters because the IdP callback loses tenant routing after redirect. Customer-impacting. Fix is confined to HTTP mux cookie persistence and test updates

body:
## Summary

アルファベットなぞり書きで、小文字や例示単語の薄字ガイドが手書き練習用の4本線に対してやや合っていなかったため、実表示を Playwright で確認しながら小文字・単語・罫線高さ別に調整しました。

## Related Issue

Relates to #31

先行PR後の表示確認で見つかった、なぞり書き小文字の位置・サイズ調整のフォローアップです。

## Changes Made

- なぞり書きガイドに文字種別のクラスを付与し、小文字の短字・上伸び字・下伸び字・小文字単語・先頭大文字単語でフォントサイズと上下位置を調整しました。
- 罫線高さ `8mm / 10mm / 12mm` に合わせて、なぞり書きの1ページあたり文字数と横方向の繰り返し数を再計算するようにしました。

author: dmooney
body:
Fixes #620.

## Summary

- Adds `max_concurrent_sessions: usize` to `SessionConfig` in `parish-config` (default 50, overridable via `PARISH_MAX_SESSIONS` env var).
- `SessionRegistry` gains `active_count()`, `is_at_capacity(cap)`, and a `rejection_count: AtomicU64` field.
- `get_or_create_session` now returns `Result<(String, Arc<SessionEntry>, bool), CapacityExceededError>`. Only new-session creation is gated — returning visitors (cookie present, session in memory or restorable from DB) bypass the cap entirely.
- Both middleware paths (tower-sessions default + legacy killswitch) emit `503 Service Unavailable` with `Retry-After: 30` on `CapacityExceededError`.
- Auth handlers (`callback_google`, `logout`, `callback_google_tower`, `logout_tower`) propagate the same 503.
- `tracing::info!` events fire on new-session creation (current_session_count, capacity) and on rejection (current_session_count, capacity, rejection_count).
- Feature flag `admission-control` is default-on per CLAUDE.md rule #6 (`!is_disabled`).
- `docs/agent/architecture.md` gains a "Session capacity" subsection documenting the per-process budget formula, configuration, and mode-parity note.

## Mode parity

Admission control is HTTP-server-only by nature. CLI and Tauri have one session per process and do not call `is_at_capacity`. `SessionRegistry` exposes the method for trait coherence but it is not wired in non-server entry points.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`parish-server` lib): `active_count_reflects_in_memory_sessions`, `is_at_capacity_returns_false_below_cap_true_at_cap`, `rejection_count_not_incremented_below_cap`.
- **Integration** (`tests/admission_control.rs`): `no_cap_allows_unlimited_sessions`, `at_cap_new_visitor_gets_503_existing_visitor_allowed` (cap=2, verifies 503 + `Retry-After: 30` on third new visitor, returning visitor with cookie still admitted).

## Commands run

```sh
just check   # agent-check + fmt + clippy + tests + witness-scan + doc-paths
```

All 208 parish-server tests pass; no regressions.

## Configuration

| Source | Precedence |
|---|---|
| `PARISH_MAX_SESSIONS` env var | Highest |
| `[engine.session] max_concurrent_sessions` in `parish.toml` | Middle |
| Compiled default | 50 |

author: omar2003has-creator
body:
# Module 6 Week B: Applied Lab — Embeddings Comparison

## Description
This Pull Request completes the **Module 6 Week B Applied Lab**, where I implemented and compared three different text representation methods: **TF-IDF**, **GloVe**, and **DistilBERT**. The project involved building three distinct pipelines to transform raw BBC News articles into vector representations and analyzing how each method ranks semantic similarity.

## Technical Tasks Accomplished

### 1. TF-IDF Representation (Task 1)
- Implemented `build_tfidf(texts)` using scikit-learn's `TfidfVectorizer` to create a sparse matrix of text representations.
- Developed `compute_tfidf_similarity(tfidf_matrix)` to calculate pairwise cosine similarity.
- **Result:** Generated a matrix of shape (1000, 21166), capturing the statistical importance of keywords across the corpus.

### 2. GloVe Average Embeddings (Task 2)
- Implemented `load_glove(filepath)` to map words to 50-dimensional pre-trained vectors.
- Developed `text_to_glove(text, embeddings)` to compute the average vector of all words in a document while handling Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) words.
- **Result:** Successfully produced 50-dimensional document embeddings.

### 3. DistilBERT Contextual Embeddings (Task 3)
- Integrated the `distilbert-base-uncased` model using the Hugging Face `transformers` library.
- Implemented `extract_bert_embedding(text, tokenizer, model)` with a **Mean Pooling** strategy that accounts for the attention mask to generate high-quality 768-dimensional embeddings.
- **Result:** Captured deep semantic context for each of the 1,000 news snippets.

### 4. Comparison & Ranking (Task 4)
- Developed `compare_similarities` to rank the top-3 most similar documents for each method across 5 news categories (Politics, Sport, Tech, Business, and Entertainment).

## Analysis (Task 5)

### Agreement and Disagreement
- **Consistency:** Methods largely agreed on clear-cut categories like **Business** (Card Fraud) and **Tech** (Mobiles) where the vocabulary is highly specialized.
- **Keyword vs. Context:** In the "Entertainment" query regarding a TV ad controversy, **TF-IDF** stayed close to specific names (keyword overlap), while **DistilBERT** identified other articles about "media criticism" and "drama attacks," demonstrating a superior grasp of semantic meaning even when literal words differed.

### OOV (Out-of-Vocabulary) Observations
- **Missing Words:** The 50,000-word GloVe vocabulary missed several **Proper Nouns** (e.g., "Hoddle", "Blunkett") and domain-specific terms.
- **Impact:** Since GloVe averages only the known words, the resulting vectors for articles focused on specific individuals became more generic, leading to less precise similarity rankings compared to BERT, which handles subwords via its WordPiece tokenizer.

## Verification Results
Based on local execution:
- **Total Texts:** 1000
- **TF-IDF Matrix:** (1000, 21166)
- **GloVe Shape:** (50,)
- **BERT Shape:** (768,)

---

## Summary

Adds \`rain-metadata schema-check\` subcommand that compares the source subgraph schema (\`subgraph/schema.graphql\`) to the consumer crate's introspection snapshot (\`crates/metaboard/src/schema/metaboard.graphql\`) at the entity level: missing entities, missing fields, field-type mismatches. Exits non-zero on drift.

Wired in as a pre-deploy step in \`manual-subgraph-deploy.yml\`. If drift is detected, the workflow fails before \`subgraph-deploy\` runs — no Goldsky deploys, nothing to roll back.

## Demonstration

Run on this branch surfaces real drift between the deployed subgraph and the metaboard crate's snapshot:

\`\`\`
schema check failed with 3 mismatches:
  - field \`MetaV1.transaction\` is missing from consumer schema
  - field \`MetaV1.subject\` type mismatch: source \`Bytes!\` vs consumer \`BigInt!\`
  - entity \`Transaction\` is missing from consumer schema
\`\`\`

Smoke-tested end-to-end: triggered \`Subgraph manual deploy\` on this branch ([run 25311954053](https://github.com/rainlanguage/rain.metadata/actions/runs/25311954053)). Schema-check step failed; \`subgraph-deploy\` step was skipped. Zero Goldsky deploys.

## Closes

This PR adds the gate. It will block all further deploys until \`crates/metaboard/src/schema/metaboard.graphql\` is regenerated to match the live subgraph. Closes #58 on merge + snapshot regeneration.

## Test plan
- [x] \`cargo test -p rain-metadata\` — 5 new tests covering matching, missing entity, missing field, type mismatch, and the real divergence
- [x] Pre-deploy step verified to fail and skip deploy on this branch
- [ ] CI green (Rainix CI)

author: unbreakablemj
body:
## Summary

Adds the public `proxy::jump` submodule with the `[user@]host[:port]` parser and the `JumpHost` type. Re-opened on a clean rebase off main; previous PR #8 was auto-closed when its base branch (M13.2) was deleted by the squash-merge.

### New public surface

- `proxy::JumpHost { host, port, user, identity_files }`
- `proxy::parse_jump_chain(raw: &str) -> Result<Vec<JumpHost>, AnvilError>`
- `proxy::MAX_JUMP_HOPS` (= 8, matches OpenSSH `READCONF_MAX_DEPTH` per FR-57)

### Grammar

OpenSSH `-J` / `ProxyJump` syntax: `[user@]host[:port]`, comma-separated. Whitespace around commas is tolerated. The literal `none` (case-insensitive) is rejected with a clear `disable sentinel` error — callers that recognize it as the FR-59 disable sentinel should detect it before calling.

### Tests (16 new)

Single-hop bare, single-hop user@host:port, two-hop chain, whitespace tolerance, empty/whitespace-only string, trailing/double commas, empty user, empty host, invalid port, port out of range, `none` literal in three case variants, max-length chain accepted, length+1 rejected, struct `PartialEq` + `Clone` sanity. Total: 185 lib tests, 0 failures.

### Out of scope

- IPv6 literals (`[::1]:22`) — rare in ProxyJump strings, not exercised by the listed FRs.
- Per-hop `ssh_config` resolution — happens at the chain manager (M13.4) / dispatcher (M13.6) layer.

author: m-bonanno
body:
## What

Closes #372. Replaces the landing-page hero placeholder (soft-surface tile + centred brand glyph) with a real product screenshot — the Attendance heatmap on the Stats page, captured on iPhone 14 Pro Max against the Apex Grappling demo seed (#371).

## Why

#330 shipped the landing page with an explicit placeholder comment in `landing.component.html`:

> *Hero visual placeholder. A real screenshot of the dashboard on a phone goes here once we have the captures.*

Now we have:
- A populated demo academy (40 athletes / 4250 attendances / 377 payments — #371) so every chart renders rich.
- The new heatmap + bar charts merged in #369 / #370.
- 5 captures on iPhone 14 Pro Max sitting in `~/Downloads/`.

The heatmap is the most visually distinctive of the five — dense data, single-glance takeaway, immediately reads as "this product knows what it's doing." It carries the marketing arc on its own without needing a multi-screenshot carousel (explicitly out of scope per the issue body — revisit if conversion data justifies it).

## How

**Asset.** Source PNG 1290×2795 (306 KB) → `sharp` resize to 1024-wide → WebP `quality: 82, effort: 6` → **50 KB**. WebP is universally supported (Safari 14+, Chrome, Firefox, Edge); no PNG fallback needed for an MVP marketing surface. Lands at `client/public/assets/landing/stats-attendance-heatmap-iphone.webp`.

**Layout.** The inner white `landing__hero-visual-card` placeholder (sized for a 4rem brand-glyph) is dropped — the screenshot itself becomes the visual focus, framed by the soft-surface outer container. The outer container keeps its 4/5 (mobile) / 1/1 (desktop) aspect-ratio so the slot reserves a stable layout box (CLS budget, Doherty Threshold), and `box-shadow: var(--budojo-elevation-floating)` moves from the outer container to the screenshot itself so the elevation reads against the soft surface rather than the page background.

**i18n.** New `landing.hero.visualAlt` key in `en.json` + `it.json` (parity preserved). The screenshot is meaningful content (Norman § signifiers — "shows what the product looks like"), not pure decoration, so it carries a real `alt` rather than `aria-hidden`.

**Image attributes.**
- `width` / `height` set to the natural source dimensions (1024 × 2218) so the browser reserves layout space before the asset loads.
- `fetchpriority="high"` + `loading="eager"` because the image is above the fold on the marketing surface.

## Out of scope

- Multi-screenshot carousel / gallery — start with one strong capture; revisit if conversion data justifies it.
- Marketing copy rewrites in the hero block — copy stays as-is.
- Re-shooting on Android / non-iPhone devices.

## References

- Closes #372
- #330 — landing page initial implementation (the placeholder this PR replaces)
- #369 — Stats multi-section + heatmap (the captured screen)
- #371 — Apex Grappling demo seeder (the data behind the captures)

## Test plan

- [x] `./.claude/scripts/test-client.sh` — prettier + lint + vitest 476/476 green.
- [x] New vitest spec pins the swap: no `app-brand-glyph` inside the hero visual, the screenshot is present with expected `src` / dimensions / non-empty `alt`.
- [x] i18n parity check (`i18n-keys.spec.ts`) green — `landing.hero.visualAlt` lands in both `en.json` and `it.json`.
- [x] Asset reachable at `/assets/landing/stats-attendance-heatmap-iphone.webp` on the dev server (200 / 50 KB / `image/webp`).
- [ ] Cypress green in CI.
- [ ] Manual smoke: open `/` → hero card shows the heatmap screenshot with phone-ish proportions, no layout shift on load.

author: alexnetsov
body:
* feat: deploy Apple Pay domain-association file on install and on save

Apple Pay requires every storefront domain to serve a verification file at
/.well-known/apple-developer-merchantid-domain-association over HTTPS, per
https://docs.paypercut.io/docs/accept-payments/apple-pay. Previously merchants
had to drop the file via SFTP after install — easy to forget, and the existing
PayPerCut domain registration would stay in enabled:false until they did.

The plugin now writes the file automatically:
- install() places it before registering the order_info event.
- validate() re-runs the same routine on every settings save (idempotent
  fast path — no-op if the SHA256 on disk already matches).
- A "Refresh from PayPerCut CDN" button + six-state status panel under the
  Apple Pay toggle exposes ok / missing / mismatch_local / mismatch_remote /
  http_error / unreachable states, with the resolved local path and the
  storefront-side public URL for verification in a browser.

Source is hybrid: install() and the refresh AJAX endpoint try the
cdn.paypercut.io copy with a 3s timeout, and an inline base64 constant
(228 bytes, SHA256-pinned) provides an offline fallback. validate()'s save
path skips the CDN — the on-disk file is already correct in the common case,
and a network round-trip on every save is wasted work.

A permissive .htaccess is dropped into the created .well-known/ directory
for Apache hosts that block dotfile dirs by default. An existing .htaccess
(e.g. Let's Encrypt acme-challenge) is preserved.

uninstall() leaves the file in place — same policy as the existing DB-table
preservation. The 10 new language strings are translated across all 13
locales, reusing the wording from the v2/v3 sister plugins.

* fix: remove the sha256 check

author: smorand
body:
## User Story
Step 5 of the construction order in `specs/2026-05-03_21:03:22-agent-code-mvp.md` section 14.2: "Implement the anti-cheat tool wrapper: the layer that blocks writes to `tests/test_*.py` based on the current phase."

This is the single enforcement point that prevents the most common LLM agent failure mode: rather than fixing the production code that makes a test pass, the agent modifies the test until it passes. The spec marks this as non-negotiable; the reviewer agent and the PR creation gate rely on this invariant holding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC-1: A pure helper `is_test_locked_path(path)` returns True for `tests/test_*.py` at any depth and False for `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/testdata/**`, and any path outside `tests/`.
- [x] AC-2: An `AntiCheatGuard` wraps a `ToolRegistry` and tracks the active phase via `set_phase(name)` so the orchestrator can update it at phase boundaries.
- [x] AC-3: When the phase is `IMPLEMENTATION` and the call targets a write tool with a locked path, the guard returns `ToolResult(ok=False, ...)` WITHOUT invoking the wrapped tool.
- [x] AC-4: Intercepted tools: `write_file`, `edit_file`, `delete_file`, `move_file` (the latter checks BOTH `src` and `dst` so renames out of locked paths are also blocked).
- [x] AC-5: Other phases (`E2E_WRITING`, `PLANNING`, etc.) and read-only tools (`read_file`, `grep`, ...) are never blocked.
- [x] AC-6: Every block is recorded as a `BlockedCall` (frozen dataclass) for the audit trail; `AuditTrail.to_jsonl()` emits one JSON object per blocked call.

## Approach
- `src/tools/anti_cheat.py`: `is_test_locked_path` is a pure function on the path; the wrapper does not read file content. `AntiCheatGuard` holds a reference to the underlying registry and a mutable `_phase`. `set_phase` is the orchestrator's only mutation point. The block message tells the model exactly what is forbidden and what is allowed, so it can adjust strategy on the next iteration.
- The guard exposes `blocked_calls` as an immutable snapshot so the future implementation-loop PR can count blocks toward the "3 blocks in 10 iterations triggers an approach reset" rule (FR-008 step 4 in the spec).
- `AuditTrail` is a small JSONL emitter so blocks persist in `.agent_work/<ticket_id>/attempts.log` for forensic inspection by humans and the reviewer agent.

## E2E Tests
The MVP spec covers anti-cheat behavior in E2E-004, E2E-012, E2E-017, E2E-026, all run at the orchestrator level (deferred to the implementation loop PR). For this PR, 33 new pytest tests cover the wrapper's public surface:

- 4 parametrized tests on `is_test_locked_path` cover every lock and every allowed exception (including subdir conftests, testdata under any name, Windows separator normalization).
- 3 pass-through tests: no phase, planning, e2e_writing.
- 3 block tests parametrized over write_file/edit_file/delete_file with locked paths during IMPLEMENTATION.
- 2 move_file tests: blocks when `src` is locked, blocks when `dst` is locked.
- 3 allow tests during IMPLEMENTATION: conftest.py, testdata/**, src/**.
- Read tools are never blocked.
- BlockedCall accumulation order; set_phase(None) disables enforcement.
- AuditTrail JSONL round-trip; empty trail renders empty.
- BlockedCall immutability.

168 tests total (135 prior + 33 new), all green. Coverage 95.17%.

## Notable Decisions
- **Wrapper, not a decorator**: phases hold a guard reference, not the underlying registry. The guard exposes `call(tool_name, **kwargs)` with the same shape as the registry, so phases can be ported transparently when the orchestrator wires the guard.
- **Path inspection only**: the wrapper never reads file content. That keeps it cheap and side-effect-free; the cost is at most a `PurePosixPath` parse per call.
- **`move_file` blocks both `src` and `dst`**: a move out of `tests/test_foo.py` is functionally equivalent to deleting the test, so it is also a write that should be blocked. Tested explicitly.
- **Phase awareness via mutable state, not constructor**: a single guard instance lives across the run; the orchestrator updates the phase at boundaries. Simpler than reconstructing a guard per phase, and the `set_phase` API is small.
- **Read tools never intercepted**: even during IMPLEMENTATION, the agent must be able to read the test files to understand what it needs to make pass.
- **Block reason delivered to the model verbatim**: helps the model adjust strategy on its own without orchestrator intervention.
- **`is_test_locked_path` uses `parts[1:2] == ("testdata",)`** instead of `len(parts) >= 2 and parts[1] == "testdata"` to avoid a magic-value lint warning while keeping the intent clear.

## Out of Scope
- **Stagnation counter** (FR-008 step 4: 3 blocks in 10 iterations triggers an approach reset). The wrapper exposes `blocked_calls`; the actual counter and reset logic land with the implementation loop PR.
- **E2E commit SHA verification** (E2E-026 in the spec): a separate pre-PR check that the SHA of the E2E commit has not been altered. Independent from this wrapper; lives in the PR creation phase.
- **`apply_patch` interception**: the spec mentions unified-diff edits as a future tool. When it lands, the wrapper must parse the diff to extract target file paths. Tracked as a TODO in the module docstring.
- **`run_shell` interception**: not yet wired into the registry. When it is, the wrapper will inspect commands like `sed -i tests/test_*.py`. Today there is no escape hatch since `run_shell` cannot be reached via the registry.
- **Wiring the guard into the orchestrator** (where `set_phase` actually gets called between phases): a small follow-up PR.
