author: mmprotest
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent the runner from wasting a task budget by repeatedly executing the same tool call with identical arguments that yields identical observations. 
- Provide a small, generic, conservative mechanism that triggers without adding benchmark-specific logic or changing prompts. 
- Ensure the mechanism is per-task and resets between runs so legitimate repeats across tasks are unaffected.

### Description
- Added a lightweight per-task store `Runner._tool_repeat_history` and reset it at the start of each `run(...)` so repeat tracking is isolated to a single task. 
- Implemented conservative normalization and hashing utilities in `state_tooling` to build repeat signatures that: sort JSON keys, trim strings, collapse repeated whitespace for long observations, and truncate very long observations before hashing. 
- Added pre-execution check and short-circuit in `execute_tool_with_lifecycle(...)` that returns a synthetic tool result when the same tool+args has produced the same normalized observation 3 consecutive times, and otherwise records a bounded history of observation hashes for that tool+args key. 
- Synthetic observation is returned in the same shape as a normal tool result (`{content, is_error}` and emitted via the same `tool_result` event path so the rest of the runner does not need changes. 
- The implementation is generic and conservative, does not hardcode any task/benchmark names or suite-specific behavior, and does not change scoring, adapters, or mutation policy logic.

### Testing
- Added focused unit tests in `tests/test_tool_repeat_breaker.py` covering blocking identical Read/Grep-style calls on the 4th attempt, non-blocking when observations change, non-blocking when args differ, per-task reset, and synthetic result shape parity. 
- Ran the new tests together with the existing mutation-policy tooling tests using `pytest -q tests/test_tool_repeat_breaker.py tests/test_state_tooling_mutation_policy.py`, and all tests passed (`12 passed`).

author: carlosflorencio
body:
After backend restart, several overlapping races in the auto-resume path produced "Task failed to start" toasts even when nothing the user did had failed. This change collapses the races and gates the toast so only fresh, user-initiated launch failures notify.

## Important Changes

- Promote workspace-only executions to full agent launches in-place instead of creating a parallel execution that races with focused-tab ensure logic.
- Gate `task.state` escalation to `FAILED` on resume paths — the session is still marked FAILED but the task stays in REVIEW.
- Add `suppress_toast` on background-resume FAILED `state_changed` events so the frontend can skip notifying for non-user-initiated failures.
- Make `connectWorkspaceStream` idempotent — short-circuit when a workspace stream is already attached so promotion doesn't burn 5 retries on the "workspace stream already connected" error.
- Tighten the frontend toast guard to fire only on observed transitions (previousState present and not FAILED), preventing snapshot replays of already-failed sessions on page load from toasting.

## Validation

- `make -C apps/backend fmt test lint` — all green
- `pnpm --filter @kandev/web test` — 1050/1050 pass
- `pnpm --filter @kandev/web lint` — 0 warnings
- New unit tests:
  - `TestConnectWorkspaceStream_IdempotentWhenAlreadyAttached` — regression for the double-connect retry loop
  - Updated `agent-session.test.ts` — verifies no toast on snapshot replay (unknown previousState) and toast on real FAILED transition
  - Backend tests for `runAgentProcessAsync` escalation gating and `fromResume` callback plumbing

## Possible Improvements

Low risk. Worst case the toast misses a genuine launch-failure during a focused fresh start; mitigated because fresh-start failures still escalate the task and toast as before. Auth-error UX is unchanged.

author: n-ichimura
body:
## Bug

The Annot ↔ VSCode theme map landed in #423 was visibly ineffective: canvas pane followed the workbench theme, but toolbar / right-panel / statusbar / drawer all stayed at Annot brand colours.

## Root cause

\`EditorShell.#applyThemeOverrides\` writes the map onto \`host.container.style\` (canvas pane only). Toolbar / right-panel / statusbar are **siblings** of the container in the webview HTML, and the drawer appends to \`document.body\` — all four live outside the container's subtree, so they couldn't see the inline overrides and instead resolved \`--annot-*\` against \`editor.css\`'s \`:root\` brand defaults.

The shell's per-container behaviour is correct for the multi-host design (PWA depends on it). The fix belongs in the webview.

## Fix

Apply \`VSCODE_THEME_MAP\` directly on \`document.documentElement\` BEFORE constructing the shell. Inline-style at \`<html>\` wins over \`:root\` rules in \`editor.css\`, so every descendant resolves \`--annot-*\` to the mapped \`var(--vscode-*)\` chain. The shell's \`themeOverrides\` parameter is no longer passed.

## Verified

- \`pnpm -r typecheck\` — green
- \`pnpm test\` — 1150 tests pass
- \`pnpm lint\` — 0 errors
- \`pnpm --filter @ingcreators/annot-vscode build\` — green

## Test plan

- [x] Typecheck / test / lint / build green
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Manual: rebuild + reload VSCode dev host; switch between Default Dark+ / Light+ / Tokyo Night / GitHub HC; toolbar + right-panel + statusbar + drawer all follow

author: acedatacloud-dev
body:
PR-B of the Caddy on-demand TLS migration. Brings up the actual proxy that issues Let's Encrypt certs for tenant custom domains.

Pairs with [PlatformBackend #399](https://github.com/AceDataCloud/PlatformBackend/pull/399) (the ask URL the Caddyfile points at). Both must be deployed before any cert can be signed.

## Architecture

```
Tenant DNS:
  mybrand.com  CNAME  tenant-proxy.acedata.cloud   <-- tenant adds this once
                          │
                          ▼
       ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
       │  Tencent CLB (new public LB)      │  80, 443
       └──────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
       ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
       │  caddy-tenant-proxy (this PR)     │
       │    tls { on_demand }              │  catch-all https://
       │    ask URL: PlatformBackend       │  /api/v1/site-domains/check
       │    reverse_proxy host: $host      │
       └──────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
            studio-frontend.svc:8085
```

`studio-frontend` sees `Host: mybrand.com` and resolves the tenant Site row via the existing per-origin lookup → no Nexior code changes required.

## What this PR adds

`Nexior/deploy/production/tenant-proxy.yaml` — single file, four manifests:

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ConfigMap caddy-tenant-proxy-config` | Caddyfile (catch-all `https://`, `tls { on_demand }`, `ask` URL pointing at PB #399, HTTP → HTTPS redirect) |
| `PVC caddy-tenant-proxy-data` (5 Gi `cbs`) | Persists `/data` so ACME account + every signed cert + locks survive pod restarts. ~10 KB per cert → 5 Gi covers ~50,000 tenants |
| `Deployment caddy-tenant-proxy` | `caddy:2.8-alpine`, 1 replica, `strategy: Recreate` so the RWO volume reattaches without deadlocking |
| `Service caddy-tenant-proxy` (LoadBalancer) | New public CLB, traffic-postpaid. Does NOT share the existing nginx-router LB (that one already binds 80/443) |

`deploy/run.sh` gets one new line: `kubectl apply -f deploy/production/tenant-proxy.yaml` after the existing `studio-*` block.

## Storage details

- `XDG_DATA_HOME=/data` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/config` env vars pin Caddy's storage location to the PVC. Default is `/root/.local/share/caddy/`, which would land on the ephemeral container FS.
- `RWO` cbs volume is bound to one node — that's why we use `strategy: Recreate` (RollingUpdate would have the new pod stuck in `Pending` waiting for the old to release).
- TKE's default cbs daily snapshot covers daily backup; if the volume is ever lost wholesale, Caddy automatically re-issues all certs on next handshake (well within Let's Encrypt's 50/week/registered-domain limit).

## Memory / CPU

`requests: cpu 100m / mem 128Mi`, `limits: cpu 1 / mem 1Gi`. Caddy is genuinely tiny — at 1000+ active certs it sits at ~50 MB RSS. Limits are headroom, not expectations.

## DNS one-time setup AFTER first apply

```bash
kubectl get svc caddy-tenant-proxy -n acedatacloud
# take the EXTERNAL-IP, then in DNSPod:
# tenant-proxy.acedata.cloud   A   <EIP>
```

This is the single manual step in the whole flow. After that:
1. Tenant adds `mybrand.com CNAME tenant-proxy.acedata.cloud`.
2. First HTTPS request → Caddy → ask URL OK → Let's Encrypt → cert deployed → traffic flows.
3. Auto-renewal 30 days before expiry.

## What's NOT in this PR

Kept tightly scoped — no PlatformBackend changes, no Nexior frontend changes:

- **PR-C** (PlatformBackend) will rip out `app/utils/edgeone.py` + the EO calls in `site_domain.py` and migrate the SiteDomain model (drop `verification_token` / `eo_zone_id` / `eo_cname`, add `proxy_cname` defaulting to `tenant-proxy.acedata.cloud`).
- **PR-D** (Nexior) will rewrite `DomainsDialog.vue` to show a single CNAME instruction and drop the TXT verify step (Caddy + the ask URL replace it).

## Verification

```sh
python -c "import yaml; list(yaml.safe_load_all(open('deploy/production/tenant-proxy.yaml')))"
# yaml ok (4 docs)
```

Once merged and deployed, manual smoke test:
1. `kubectl rollout status deploy/caddy-tenant-proxy -n acedatacloud`
2. `kubectl logs -l app=caddy-tenant-proxy -n acedatacloud` — should show `serving initial configuration` and an HTTPS listener on `:443`.
3. Add the DNS A record per above.
4. Curl from the bot account's test domain (e.g. `germey.tech`):
   ```
   # Register a SiteDomain row in DB
   POST /api/v1/site-domains/  with hostname=test.germey.tech
   # Add CNAME at DNSPod: test.germey.tech CNAME tenant-proxy.acedata.cloud
   # Wait for propagation, then:
   curl -v https://test.germey.tech/
   # First request: Caddy issues cert (~5 s pause for ACME), serves HTTP 200 from studio-frontend.
   # Subsequent requests: <50 ms.
   ```

author: eumemic
body:
## Summary

Stacked on PR #213 (multi-account/multi-instance, `wt/scalable-finding-ember`).
Bugs found while migrating Tom's running aios setup (Signal + Telegram)
onto the PR #205 → #210 → #211 → #213 stack with both connectors live.

Some fixes already in this PR; the remainder are listed below as TODO
and will be added as commits before this PR exits draft.

## Done in this PR (so far)

- **`fix(connector-sdk)`** — `_focal_from_request_meta` was reading
  `ctx.request.meta` (raw `CallToolRequest` body, no `.meta` attribute)
  instead of `ctx.meta` (where the MCP lowlevel server stashes the
  parsed `_meta`).  Every focal-required tool call failed with
  `"aios should inject _meta.aios.focal_channel_path"` even when the
  harness *had* injected it.  Wire format + harness side were both
  correct; only the SDK read path was wrong.
- **`test(config)`** — `test_empty_default` reads `.env` via
  pydantic-settings.  Any operator with `AIOS_CONNECTORS_ENABLED` set
  broke the test.  Now passes `_env_file=None` and uses
  `monkeypatch.delenv` to isolate.

## TODO before exiting draft

1. **`fix(harness)` per-session attachment check on focal-routed accounts**
   — `tool_dispatch.py:395-437` runs `validate_account_for_session` only
   when `account` is a tool-arg.  For focal-required tools (signal_send,
   telegram_send) account is derived from `_meta.aios.focal_channel_path`
   and dispatched without validation.  Demonstrated live: factchecker
   ghost-wrote `"Testing Signal send on new architecture"` into the
   Metals and AI Signal group despite having no signal connection
   attached.  Lift the check above the `if account_arg is str` branch.

2. **`fix(connector-supervisor)` redact bot token from stderr pump** —
   PTB's httpx logs request URLs `https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/...`.
   Supervisor's `connector.stderr` event captures verbatim, so the bot
   token lives in `/tmp/aios-worker.log`.  Redact `bot<token>/` segments
   in the stderr pump or filter PTB's httpx logger upstream.

3. **`fix(connector-supervisor)` drop `instructions` from admin snapshot** —
   `pg_notify` payload caps at 8KB.  Signal's snapshot (groups + contacts
   × phones in the model-context instructions block) blows past it,
   leading to `asyncpg.InvalidParameterValueError: payload string too long`
   on every `connector_status` task.  Affects `aios connectors list`.
   `instructions` is a model-context concept; the admin RPC doesn't need it.

4. **`fix(harness)` validate MCP tool exists before any permission lookup** —
   the harness only namespace-pattern-matches `mcp__<server>__<tool>`,
   then calls `resolve_mcp_permission` (returns `None` on miss → caller
   defaults to `always_ask`), then parks the session in
   `requires_action`.  Result: a hallucinated tool name (e.g. an old
   `mcp__conn_<id>__signal_send` from prior conversation context) gates
   forever waiting for confirmation that should never come.  Validate
   against the union of `connector_subprocess_registry` ∪
   `agent.mcp_servers` ∪ discovered tool list before any policy lookup;
   on miss, append immediate tool error so the model self-corrects.

5. **`feat(config)` `AIOS_DEFAULT_MCP_PERMISSION_POLICY` env override** —
   for unmounted MCP toolsets, the harness defaults to `always_ask`.
   That's the right safe default but operator-hostile in trusted dev
   setups.  Add an env-level override that replaces the
   `None → always_ask` fallback (explicit per-toolset policies still
   win — this only changes the default for unmounted/unspecified).

6. **`docs(connector-supervisor)` strategically-placed comments** —
   per design discussion: docstring on `connector_supervisor.py`
   documenting the architectural constraint (lift-able into a separate
   `aios connectors` process if multi-worker scaling matters), plus a
   call-site note in `tool_dispatch.py` at the in-process supervisor
   call steering future additions to the procrastinate `connector_call`
   task.

7. **`test(e2e)` outbound focal-required MCP dispatch** — closes the test
   gap that let #1 (the SDK ctx.meta bug) merge in PR #211.  Exercises
   a session calling a focal-required connector tool with the focal
   channel set and asserts the tool sees the account/chat_id from `_meta`.

8. **`docs(plan)` align `aios connectors` (impl) with the PR4 plan** —
   plan documented `aios connector list` (singular), code is
   `aios connectors list` (plural).  Cosmetic.

## Followup issues (NOT in this PR)

- **Per-chat session routing was deleted by #205 but is a real use case.**
  Operator wanted "Metals chat → factchecker session, QA + DM →
  JN session" on one Signal account.  Old `channel_bindings` supported
  this; #200 deliberately collapsed it.  Neither `single_session` nor
  `per_chat` recovers the pattern (`per_chat` auto-spawns *new* sessions
  from a template; doesn't bind to an existing session).  Will file as
  a separate issue against #200.

## Operator notes (PR description, not code)

- **Migration env-var rename is loud.**  `AIOS_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`,
  `AIOS_SIGNAL_PHONES`, `AIOS_SIGNAL_CONFIG_DIR`,
  `AIOS_CONNECTORS_ENABLED` are all new shapes vs the pre-PR3 connector
  invocations.  Pre-existing operators must migrate their env.
- **Stale alembic stamp recovery is non-obvious.**  If `alembic_version`
  was bumped to `0026` without the migration actually running (botched
  prior test), 0026 isn't robust to partial-state re-run and fails with
  `DependentObjectsStillExist`.  Manual cleanup: `alembic stamp 0025`
  + drop the partially-created new objects + `alembic upgrade head`.
- **Signal `signal_send` returns inconsistent shapes.**  Sometimes
  `{"sent_at_ms": <int>}`, sometimes `{"status": "ok"}`.  Different
  signal-cli RPC response paths.  Worth pinning down for predictability.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run mypy src` — clean
- [x] `uv run ruff check src tests && uv run ruff format --check src tests` — clean
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit -q` — 996 passed (the test_config fix)
- [ ] Each subsequent commit revalidates all three plus the relevant e2e
- [x] **Manual smoke** completed: full migration of running aios setup
  onto PR #213 + this stack.  Telegram inbound + outbound, Signal
  inbound + outbound, all working.  Demonstrated factchecker session
  ghost-writing into Signal (the auth gap fix #1 above closes this).

## Stack

- PR #205 → #210 → #211 → #213 → **this PR**
- Base: `wt/scalable-finding-ember` (PR #213's head)

author: wanglin1126
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a learnable phase aligner module that operates in the frequency domain to align intermediate stage tensors with the sharp ground-truth image during unrolled deblurring. The aligner predicts corrected FFT phases and is supervised via a new loss function.

## Key Changes

- **New `PhaseAligner` module** (`models/phase_aligner/`):
  - Operates on FFT-shifted frequency domain representations
  - Extracts phase as (cos, sin) pairs, optionally with log-magnitude
  - Uses a configurable backbone (DnCNN, UNet, Restormer, etc.) to predict aligned phase residually
  - Recombines aligned phase with original magnitude and inverse-FFTs back to spatial domain
  - Returns both aligned spatial tensor and fft-shifted phase for loss computation

- **New `PhaseAlignerLoss`** (`utils/losses.py`):
  - Compares predicted phase against ground-truth sharp image phase
  - Supports multiple distance metrics: L1, L2, Charbonnier, and cosine distance on (cos, sin) representation
  - Applies radial smooth-decay center masking and optional magnitude weighting
  - Handles 2π phase wrap-around naturally via (cos, sin) distance forms

- **Integration with `UnrolledDeblurNet`**:
  - Phase aligners can be inserted at three configurable positions: `pre_deconv`, `pre_denoiser`, or `post_denoiser`
  - Optional weight sharing across all T stages
  - Per-stage aligned phases are captured and passed to the loss function
  - Solver step functions updated to accept and apply alignment hooks

- **Updated solver implementations** (ADMM, HQS, PG, ISTA, FISTA):
  - All solvers now accept optional `align_fn` parameter
  - Alignment is applied at the three named positions within each solver iteration

- **Loss integration**:
  - `StagewiseLoss` extended to compute per-stage phase-aligner loss with configurable weight
  - Properly handles padding to ensure phases are compared on the same spectral grid

- **Configuration and training**:
  - New `phase_aligner` section in `default.yaml` with full configuration options
  - Training script updated to instantiate and supervise phase aligners
  - Experiment directory naming includes phase-aligner parameters for tracking

## Implementation Details

- Phase alignment uses FFT-shift convention (DC at center) for consistency with loss computation
- The aligner uses thin 1×1 projections to adapt backbone input/output channels when needed
- Magnitude weighting in the loss is normalized per-image to handle varying dynamic ranges
- The alignment closure captures the stage index and aligner instance to avoid closure variable issues
- Ground-truth is padded to match the solver's padded grid size for correct spectral bin alignment

author: aviatesk
body:
`get_binding_occurrences!`'s cache key was just the byte range, but the underlying `compute_binding_occurrences_st0` accepted an `include_global_bindings` keyword that changed what was stored. All production callers happened to pass `include_global_bindings = true`, but a future caller passing `false` (or relying on the default) would poison the cache for everyone else, since the cached result could not be distinguished from the "global-included" one.

Resolve the inconsistency by removing the keyword from both `get_binding_occurrences!` and the renamed wrapper `compute_full_binding_occurrences` (formerly
`compute_binding_occurrences_st0`). The cached pipeline now unconditionally collects globals, special-case occurrences for `export`/`public`/`import`/`using` statements, macrocall scope resolution, and inert (quoted) content. Callers that only need local bindings can still use the lower-level
`compute_binding_occurrences` directly with
`include_global_bindings = false`.

The `lookup_func` keyword is preserved as an explicit argument rather than `kwargs...` so that test callers can override the context module, while making it clear that it is *not* part of the cache key — production callers all rely on the default `gen_lookup_out_of_scope!`, and tests use isolated `ServerState` instances anyway.

body: This pull request enhances the WLED software update page by introducing an "Auto-update from GitHub" feature. This allows users to automatically fetch and install the latest compatible firmware release directly from GitHub, streamlining the update process and providing real-time status feedback. **New auto-update functionality:** * Added a new `autoUpdate` async function that: - Checks for the latest firmware release on GitHub based on the device's repository and release info. - Finds and downloads the appropriate firmware asset. - Automatically uploads the firmware to the device and provides status updates or error messages. * Introduced a new "Auto-update from GitHub" button and a status display area to the update page UI, allowing users to initiate and monitor the update process. **Supporting changes:** * Stored device info from `/json/info` in a global `deviceInfo` variable for use in the auto-update logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bf11572cb75c4bf48872790bbb20db8ffc9a4839a1c32858da5680203ebed3b0R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bf11572cb75c4bf48872790bbb20db8ffc9a4839a1c32858da5680203ebed3b0R26) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an "Auto update" button that fetches, downloads, and installs the latest firmware release automatically, with status messages and error handling; disables while running. * **UI Improvements** * Renamed settings button to "Update WLED" and changed the update page's manual submit label to "Upload". * Updated text/placeholders for the latest-release area and added an auto-update status element.

author: ai-hagi
body:
## Why

`POST /api/uc4-chat/ask` und der `/ws/uc4-chat`-WebSocket failten mit 500/Disconnect, sobald CHAT_LLM_MODE=oci aktiv war. Pod-Log zeigte:
\`\`\`
OSError: OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_VERSION is not defined
oci.exceptions.ConfigFileNotFound: ~/.oci/config
\`\`\`

`get_resource_principals_signer()` ist für **OCI Functions / Container Instances**, nicht für OKE-Pods. OKE-Pods authentifizieren sich mit dem **OKE Workload Identity Signer**, der das via ServiceAccount-Annotation gemountete Projected Token unter `/var/run/secrets/oci.oraclecloud.com/...` benutzt.

## What

`services/uc4-chat/app/llm.py` — drei-stufiger Auth-Fallback in der LLM-Driver-Factory:
1. `get_oke_workload_identity_resource_principal_signer()` (OKE)
2. `get_resource_principals_signer()` (CI / Functions)
3. `oci.config.from_file()` (Dev-Laptop)

Plus saubere RuntimeError mit beiden Exceptions wenn alle drei failen.

## Folge-Arbeit (außerhalb des Codes)

IAM-Policy in der Tenancy:
\`\`\`
allow any-user to use generative-ai-family in compartment oci-defence-demo
  where all {
    request.principal.type='workload',
    request.principal.namespace='sovdefence',
    request.principal.service_account='sovdefence-runtime'
  }
\`\`\`
(Wird im selben Stil wie die existierende `autonomous-database-family`-Policy hinzugefügt — die ServiceAccount-Annotation `oci.oraclecloud.com/workload-identity: "true"` ist bereits gesetzt.)

## Test plan

- [x] 40/40 backend tests grün (`services/uc4-chat/tests/`)
- [ ] Image neu bauen + pushen, `CHAT_LLM_MODE=oci` zurücksetzen, IAM-Policy anlegen, dann echter Cohere-Call statt mock-Antwort
- [ ] Browser: Chat-Werkstatt antwortet mit echtem Cohere-Text (statt "(mock) keine weiteren Aktionen")

body: ## Summary Makes `/posts` and `/vi/posts` materially faster on Core Web Vitals — both pages now ship from the CDN as plain static HTML, payloads drop ~35%, and the LCP image starts downloading immediately. ### What changed (rolled-up across both commits on this branch) **Pagination (36 posts/page)** - `/posts` and `/vi/posts` paginate via real URL paths (not `?page=N`): - Page 1 → `/posts` (and `/vi/posts`) - Page N → `/posts/page/N` (and `/vi/posts/page/N`) - New `` component with prev/next, numbered links, ellipsis, fully responsive, i18n EN/VI. **Prerendering** - All listing routes are now `export const prerender = true` and statically generated via `getStaticPaths()`. The `_render` Vercel serverless function is **no longer** invoked for any `/posts` URL — confirmed in `.vercel/output/config.json` (no `^/posts/?$ → _render` route remains). - Pages 2..N for each language are emitted at build time as `posts/page/2/index.html`, `posts/page/3/index.html`, etc. - A small `` component holds the shared header + grid + pagination so the EN and VI page-1 / page-N entry files stay tiny. **Image / LCP optimization** - `PostCard.astro` now uses Astro's `` (from `astro:assets`) for `ImageMetadata` sources → automatic WebP/AVIF + `srcset` (50–80% size reductions on those posts). - Explicit `width="620"` `height="430"` on every card image (Astro `` and `` fallback) → prevents CLS even on external Unsplash URLs. - New `priority` prop on ``. The first card on each page is rendered with `loading="eager"` + `fetchpriority="high"`; all other cards stay `loading="lazy"` + `fetchpriority="auto"`. Confirmed in built HTML: each generated page has exactly **1 eager image + N lazy**. ### Measured impact (built `.vercel/output/static`) | Page | Cards | HTML (raw) | HTML (gzipped) | Served by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `/posts` (page 1, before this branch) | 64 | ~513 KB | — | Vercel function (SSR per request) | | `/posts` (page 1, this branch) | 36 | **140 KB** | **16 KB** | Static HTML on CDN | | `/posts/page/2` | 28 | 113 KB | 14 KB | Static HTML on CDN | | `/vi/posts` | 4 | 39 KB | — | Static HTML on CDN | TTFB on the static-served listing is ~1–3ms locally vs an SSR function invocation (50–200ms typical in production). ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Visit `/posts` — confirm 36 cards on page 1, pagination shows `1 2` (or more), and the first card image starts loading immediately (DevTools → Network → first Unsplash request fires before scroll). - [ ] Click page 2 — URL becomes `/posts/page/2`, remaining 28 cards load, pagination highlights "2". - [ ] DevTools → Network → filter by Doc → reload `/posts` — response headers should show this is a static asset (no `x-vercel-cache: MISS` from a function), no Vercel Function invocation visible in the project's Functions tab for this route. - [ ] Open the page source on `/posts` and confirm exactly one `` (the first card) and the rest are `loading="lazy"`. - [ ] Visit `/vi/posts` — Vietnamese page-header and pagination labels render; only 1 page (no pagination shown) since there are 4 vi posts. - [ ] Mobile breakpoint — pagination wraps gracefully, no horizontal scroll. - [ ] (Light regression) Click into one or two individual post pages from the listing — `/posts/` still works; `[...slug]` route is unaffected. ### Notes - `POSTS_PER_PAGE = 36` lives in both `index.astro` and `page/[page].astro` for each locale. If you want to tune it, change all four files (or hoist into a single constant — happy to do that in a follow-up). - The `firstPreviewImage` regex still pulls external Unsplash URLs from post bodies for cards. Astro's `` only kicks in for posts with a frontmatter `heroImage` (currently 7 of 68). For the rest, we still get width/height (CLS fix) but not WebP/AVIF/srcset — would need to host those images locally to fully optimize them. - `astro check` was not run because `@astrojs/check` is not installed in the project; the production build (`npm run build:astro`) succeeds, which exercises the same TypeScript/Astro toolchain. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f86e2643a290493385d737f9e1a2a946 Requested by: @phgnam

author: hoop33-dev
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the codebase to improve component reusability and maintainability by introducing new UI component abstractions (`BackButton`, `ErrorBanner`) and centralizing theme values. Hard-coded colors and styles are replaced with references to a centralized theme constants file.

## Key Changes

- **New Components**:
  - `BackButton`: Extracted back navigation button with customizable label, replacing repeated inline implementations across auth screens
  - `ErrorBanner`: New component for displaying error/success messages with variants, consolidating banner styling logic

- **Theme Centralization**:
  - Introduced `colors` and `shadows` exports from `@/src/constants/theme`
  - Replaced all hard-coded color values (e.g., `#F15825`, `rgba(255,255,255,0.35)`) with theme constants
  - Centralized shadow definitions for consistent visual effects (e.g., `shadows.orangeGlow`)

- **Component Refactoring**:
  - Updated auth screens (`login`, `forgot-password`, `reset-password`, `signup-details`, `role-selector`) to use new `BackButton` and `ErrorBanner` components
  - Replaced inline `Pressable` button implementations with `Button` component across multiple screens
  - Updated dashboard screens (`parent`, `player`, `coach`) to use `Label`, `H3`, and `Button` components with theme colors

- **UI Component Updates**:
  - `Button`, `TextButton`, `ErrorMessage`, `Input`, `Checkbox`, `RadioTile`, `Badge`: Updated to import and use centralized `colors` from theme
  - Improved consistency in color references across all UI components

## Implementation Details

- Theme constants are imported from `@/src/constants/theme` and provide a single source of truth for colors and effects
- New components follow existing patterns and accept standard React Native props plus custom styling options
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing component APIs
- Removed redundant SVG icon definitions by consolidating them into the `BackButton` component

body:
## Summary

- **T068** — Adds `describe('US7 — invalid reason discriminator')` block to `store.test.ts`, semantically grouping the three `invalid` reason assertions (`missing_token`, `orphaned_row`, `decrypt_failed`) already covered from T010. Tests are green-from-write by design; the US7 block exists for named discoverability.
- **T071** — Adds clear() token-leak guard to `store.test.ts`: `vi.spyOn(secretStore, 'delete')` asserts the method is called with only the `SecretKey`, never the token value string. Belt-and-braces: `JSON.stringify(spy.mock.calls)` must not contain the distinctive token string.
- **T072** — Adds deferred 401-interceptor seam comment to `store.ts` `clear()`. No behaviour change, no logger call added, FR-8 invariant preserved.
- **T069** — Adds six banner tests to `PairingScreen.test.tsx`: one per reason (copy verified), banner-absent when prop omitted, `role="alert"` presence, and input-count invariant (total still 1).
- **T070** — Creates `InvalidStateBanner.tsx` (`role="alert"`, `data-testid="invalid-state-banner"`, zero inputs, reason→copy lookup via `Record<InvalidReason, string>`). Composes it in `PairingScreen.tsx` before `PairingForm` only when `invalidReason !== undefined` — `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`-safe.
- **T073** — Interactive Electron smoke (corrupt SecretStore / DPAPI scenario on physical Windows) cannot be performed in CI. **Reviewer follow-up required**: boot the packaged app, corrupt the DPAPI blob in `%APPDATA%\pos-pulse\safeStorage\`, restart, confirm the `decrypt_failed` banner renders and the pairing form is reachable.

## Banner copy

| reason | message |
|---|---|
| `missing_token` | This terminal needs to be paired again. The secure token is missing. |
| `orphaned_row` | This terminal needs to be paired again. Local assignment data is incomplete. |
| `decrypt_failed` | This terminal needs to be paired again. Secure token recovery failed. |

## Invariants preserved

- **FR-8**: `clear()` makes no logger call (no change to production code path).
- **FR-14**: no `clear()` call on mismatch; this PR does not touch the pairing submit path.
- **T030 input-count**: `InvalidStateBanner` contains zero `<input>` elements; route total remains 1.
- **exactOptionalPropertyTypes**: `reason={undefined}` is never spread — conditional JSX `{props.invalidReason !== undefined && <InvalidStateBanner reason={props.invalidReason} />}`.
- **No device_token or pairing_code in DOM or logs**: banner renders only the reason-mapped copy string.
- **AGENTS.md untouched**: untracked file was explicitly excluded from `git add`.

## Scope boundary

This PR covers **T068–T073 only**. T074+ (Phase Final / Polish — outcome-specific copy dictionary) are explicitly deferred and must not be pulled in here.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | ✓ |
| `npm run lint` | ✓ |
| `npm test` | ✓ 616/616 |
| `npm test -- --coverage` | ✓ 99.48% stmts, 100% lines |
| `npm run codegen:verify` | ✓ api-types.ts up to date |

- [ ] Review T068 describe block in `store.test.ts` — confirm three reason assertions are semantically grouped under US7 label
- [ ] Review T071 spy test — confirm `deleteSpy` asserts key-only, token string absent from call log
- [ ] Review T072 seam comment in `store.ts` `clear()` — no behaviour change, comment text accurate
- [ ] Review T069 six tests in `PairingScreen.test.tsx` — three reason messages, absent-banner, alert role, input count
- [ ] Review `InvalidStateBanner.tsx` — `role="alert"`, zero inputs, `Record<InvalidReason, string>` lookup
- [ ] Review `PairingScreen.tsx` — conditional compose before `<PairingForm>`, no spread of `undefined`
- [ ] **T073 manual smoke** (reviewer): corrupt DPAPI blob on physical Windows, confirm `decrypt_failed` banner renders

## Description

Fixes the same Recent-runs dropdown clipping that PR #105 was supposed to fix. That fix didn't actually work — the dropdown was still being painted under the highlighted scan-path `<code>` and the dashboard cards. Real-world reproduction in `argus view --interface=browser` against any scan dir with multiple sibling runs.

## Changes Made
- [ ] Added new scanner/workflow
- [x] Modified existing scanner/workflow
- [ ] Updated documentation
- [x] Fixed bug
- [ ] Other

### Details

**Why #105 didn't work** — the CSS already has, earlier in the file:

```css
body > * { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
```

That selector has specificity `(0,0,0,2)` (element + child combinator + universal). PR #105 added `header { z-index: 100; }` which has specificity `(0,0,0,1)` — strictly lower, so it was silently overridden. Both `<header>` and `<main>` ended up at z-index 1 in the root stacking context, and source order made `<main>` paint on top. The dropdown's local `z-index: 1000` only competes inside its parent's stacking context, so it was trapped under main.

**Fix** — raise the header's z-index via a selector that matches `body > *`'s specificity and comes later in the cascade:

```css
body > header { z-index: 100; }
```

Specificity `(0,0,0,2)`, same as `body > *`; later in the file, so it wins on cascade order. The `.recent-scans-list` rule's `z-index: 1000` inside header's stacking context already wins against the dashboard cards, so this single rule is the whole fix. The previously ineffective `position: relative; z-index: 100;` block on the bare `header` selector is dropped, with a one-liner comment pointing readers at the new specificity-aware rule for discoverability.

## Testing

author: decentraland-bot
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `sdk-commands world-permissions` CLI command that lets NAME owners grant deployment collaborator permissions to their worlds
- Supports granting access to the **entire world** (default) or restricting to **specific parcels** via `--parcels`
- Accepts **multiple addresses** in a single operation via repeated `--address` flags
- Uses the same linker dapp signing flow as `deploy` and `quests` commands
- Hits the same worlds-content-server API used by Creator Hub's MANAGE tab

## Plan

### Background

World creators need a CLI-accessible way to add collaborators to their worlds without opening the Creator Hub. The worlds-content-server already exposes the permissions API at:

- `POST /world/{name}/permissions/deployment` — set full allow-list (world-wide, multiple wallets in one call)
- `POST /world/{name}/permissions/deployment/address/{addr}/parcels` — grant parcel-restricted access per address

The Creator Hub uses these endpoints with signed fetch + auth chain. The CLI replicates the same pattern used by the `quests` and `deploy` commands.

### Command Design

```
sdk-commands world-permissions [options]

Options:
  -w, --world [name]          World NAME (e.g. myworld.dcl.eth)  — required
  -a, --address [address]     Collaborator wallet — repeatable, at least 1 required
      --parcels [list]        Optional: restrict to space-separated "x,y" parcels
  -t, --target-content [url]  Worlds content server (default: https://worlds-content-server.decentraland.org)
  -b, --no-browser            Do not open browser
  -p, --port [port]           Linker dapp port
      --https                 Use HTTPS

Examples:
  # Grant world-wide access to two wallets (one signing round)
  sdk-commands world-permissions --world myworld.dcl.eth --address 0x1234... --address 0x5678...

  # Grant access restricted to specific parcels
  sdk-commands world-permissions --world myworld.dcl.eth --address 0x1234... --parcels "0,0 1,0 -1,2"
```

### Implementation

**World-wide mode** (no `--parcels`):
1. Fetches existing deployment permissions (read-only, no auth required)
2. Merges new addresses with existing allow-list (deduplication included)
3. Signs + POSTs to `POST /world/{name}/permissions/deployment` with merged list
4. **One signing round regardless of address count**

**Parcel-specific mode** (`--parcels`):
1. For each address: signs + POSTs to `POST /world/{name}/permissions/deployment/address/{addr}/parcels`
2. Each address requires its own signing round (different URL = different signed payload)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `--world` required, error on missing
- [x] `--address` required (≥1), error on missing
- [x] Invalid EVM addresses rejected before signing
- [x] Invalid parcel format rejected before signing
- [x] World-wide: merges with existing wallets, one POST, one signing round
- [x] Parcel-specific: one POST per address with the specified parcel list
- [x] `DCL_PRIVATE_KEY` env var bypasses linker dapp (headless/CI mode)
- [x] Custom `--target-content` URL supported
- [x] 18 unit tests passing

## Changes

```

packages/@dcl/sdk-commands/src/commands/world-permissions/utils.ts | 149 +++

packages/@dcl/sdk-commands/src/locales/es.json                    |   8 +
packages/@dcl/sdk-commands/src/locales/zh.json                    |   8 +
packages/@dcl/sdk-commands/src/logic/args.ts                      |   2 +-
packages/@dcl/sdk-commands/src/logic/error.ts                     |   7 +
test/sdk-commands/commands/world-permissions/index.spec.ts        | 437 ++++
```

PASS  test/sdk-commands/commands/world-permissions/index.spec.ts

## Summary

Implements per-account device isolation backed by Firebase Realtime Database. Each user's devices are stored and served from a user-scoped path (`/users/{user_id}/devices`), with no cross-account leakage.

## Changes

### Device Management
- **`action_devices.py`**: Refactored all device functions (`rsync`, `rstate`, `rquery`, `rexecute`, `onSync`, `onQuery`, `onExecute`, `commands`, `actions`, `get_dashboard_devices`) to accept and use `user_id` for scoped Firebase reads/writes
- Added `_device_namespace_mode()`, `_normalize_user_scope()`, `_get_scoped_snapshot()`, and `_get_scoped_device_states()` helpers
- Added `get_dashboard_devices(user_id)` to power the devices dashboard with real Firebase data

### Routes
- **`routes.py`**: `/devices`, `/device/<device_id>`, and `/smarthome` routes all pass `current_user.id` as scope
- Added `_resolve_smarthome_user_scope()` to extract user scope from Google Home requests (`agentUserId` or authenticated session)

### Config
- **`config.py`**: Added `DEVICE_NAMESPACE_MODE` env var (default `strict`) — controls whether device reads fall back to the legacy global path (`legacy` | `hybrid` | `strict`)

### Templates
- **`templates/devices.html`**: Updated to render real device data (icon, display name, type label, online status) from Firebase

## Firebase Path Schema

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `/users/{user_id}/devices/{device_id}/` | Per-account device tree (canonical) |
| `/devices/` | Legacy global path — **deleted** |

## Isolation Behaviour

In `strict` mode, each account only reads from its own `/users/{user_id}/devices` path. No fallback to shared data.

| User | Devices |
|------|---------|
| 1 (dekanozishvili@gmail.com) | Front Camera, Front Door Lock, My Lamp, My Sprinkler, My Switch |
| 2 (ddekanozishvili@solvit.ge) | Test Switch (added for testing) |

## Tests

38 tests passing. New tests added:
- `test_devices_route_scopes_to_logged_in_user`
- `test_smarthome_uses_agent_user_scope`
- `test_devices_route_passes_logged_in_user_scope`
- `test_get_dashboard_devices_uses_live_state`
- `test_devices_route_uses_dashboard_devices`

## Summary by Sourcery

Scope device management to per-user Firebase paths and wire this through web routes and smarthome intents, with configurable fallback behavior.

New Features:
- Add per-user Firebase-backed device listing for the Device Management dashboard.
- Introduce configurable device namespace modes to control legacy vs scoped paths.
- Expose a helper to resolve user scope for smarthome requests based on agentUserId, session user, or fallback config.

Enhancements:
- Refactor device action handlers and Firebase helpers to accept user scope and support hybrid/strict isolation modes.
- Improve devices dashboard template to show real-time device metadata, icons, and online status derived from Firebase.

Tests:
- Add tests to verify smarthome requests use the correct user scope and agentUserId.
- Add tests to ensure devices routes pass logged-in user scope and use dashboard device data.
- Add tests to validate dashboard devices rendering logic uses live state and status classes.

author: ccharly
body:
Adding a v1 adapter for v2 `SnapKeyring` (1 keyring per Snap). So we can use it with the current architecture of the `KeyringController` that constructs a v2 keyring instance from a v1 instance.

The idea is to use this "adapter" for v1 instances and call `.asV2()` on this same instance when the `KeyringController` initializes its v2 counterpart. This way, we share the same actual instance/logic/account-registry between the 2.

NOTE: No one will use the v1 instance directly, but I add it mostly to be compliant with the current `KeyringController` architecture AND use it in v2 contexts (using `:withKeyringV2`).

One big important note though, the vault is currently computed using v1 instances on the `KeyringController`, thus, we still need this extra layer for it to be part of the vault and migrate from the legacy 1 big Snap keyring -> N Snap keyrings (1 per Snap), see:
- https://github.com/MetaMask/core/blob/0d7aac0baca77af2d2c78d166dbe5b8539024561/packages/keyring-controller/src/KeyringController.ts#L2561-L2569
- https://github.com/MetaMask/core/blob/0d7aac0baca77af2d2c78d166dbe5b8539024561/packages/keyring-controller/src/KeyringController.ts#L705-L718
- https://github.com/MetaMask/core/blob/0d7aac0baca77af2d2c78d166dbe5b8539024561/packages/keyring-controller/src/KeyringController.ts#L3006-L3016

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a new compatibility wrapper that changes how per-snap `SnapKeyring` instances can be registered/consumed by v1 `KeyringController` flows, which could affect account address normalization and vault/serialization behavior if integrated incorrectly.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Adds `SnapKeyringV1Adapter` under the `/v2` export** to let v1 `EthKeyring` consumers interact with per-snap v2 `SnapKeyring` instances, while still exposing the underlying v2 object via `asV2()` so v1/v2 entries can share a single instance.
> 
> The adapter **converts v2 `getAccounts()` results into v1-style `string[]` addresses** (using `normalizeAccountAddress`), and otherwise delegates snap message handling, signing/user-op methods, lifecycle (`destroy`), and `serialize`/`deserialize` directly to the inner v2 keyring. `SnapKeyringOptions` is now exported and the changelog documents the new adapter.
>

author: harshrs21
body:
Closes #1693

## Summary

**Problem:** Marking anime episodes as watched on Trakt fails with "Failed to mark watched on Trakt (201)" for series where the Stremio addon (e.g. AIOMetadata) uses different season/episode numbering than Trakt's TVDB-based database. Tested with One Piece (`tt0388629`), which is confirmed in Trakt's database but not findable at the addon's season/episode coordinates.

**Fix 1 — episode remap season structure check (`TraktEpisodeMappingService`)**

`hasSameSeasonStructure()` previously compared only the *set* of season numbers between the addon episode list and Trakt's episode list. For One Piece, both sources have seasons 1–24, so the check concluded the structures matched and skipped the remap entirely — even though episode counts per season differ significantly. The fix compares per-season episode counts instead, correctly identifying the structural mismatch and allowing the remap to fire.

**Fix 2 — episode title threading (`TraktEpisodeMappingService` + `TraktProgressService`)**

`resolveEpisodeMapping()` passed `requestedTitle = null` to `remapEpisodeByTitleOrIndex()`, disabling title-based episode matching even when `WatchProgress.episodeTitle` was available. The fix threads the episode title through `resolveCanonicalEpisodeMapping()` → `resolveEpisodeMapping()` → `remapEpisodeByTitleOrIndex()` so title-based matching can fire as the primary strategy before falling back to index-based matching.

**Fix 3 — TMDB → IMDB resolution for `/sync/history` requests (`TraktProgressService`)**

When a content ID is TMDB-only (e.g. `tmdb:12345`), `resolveHistoryIds()` now calls `tmdbService.tmdbToImdb()` to resolve an IMDB ID before sending the history request. Trakt's IMDB links are maintained far more comprehensively than its TMDB links, so this improves match rates for any content identified by TMDB ID.

## Test plan

- [x] One Piece S23E3 and S23E4 (`tt0388629`) marked as watched successfully — confirmed in Trakt history
- [x] Error toast no longer shown for anime episodes with numbering mismatch
- [x] Remap fires: second `/sync/history` request observed in logs after initial `not_found` response
- [x] Non-anime series with matching numbering unaffected (remap returns null when `hasSameSeasonStructure` is true)
- [x] TMDB-only content IDs correctly resolved to IMDB before Trakt requests

## Summary

User asked for two changes:

1. **Strength day moves Thu → Sun.** Thursday is unavailable (day job 9–5:30 + restaurant 6–10 PM). Sunday morning is the only feasible slot.
2. **Strength page rebuild** — easier to understand at a glance.

Plus a chronology bug fix surfaced during testing.

## What changed

**Day swap (state.js)** — `applyUserDayPreferences()` runs at state.js load time, walks all 25 weeks, and:
- Moves Thursday's strength content onto Sunday (`when: 'AM'`).
- Resets Thursday to a generic rest day with `extras: ['pushups', 'circuit']`.
- Skips weeks where Thursday isn't strength (e.g., race week 25).

body:
Step 3 of \`plans/l2-world-networks\`. Sub-PR targeting the integration branch.

## Summary

Adds an optional \`--machine-id <ip>\` flag to \`scripts/testL2Bypass.ts\` so the forged-envelope verification can deterministically target a specific machine. Without the flag, behavior is unchanged (picks the first restrictive row in \`machine_filesystems\`).

\`\`\`
npx dotenv -e .env.development.local -- npx tsx scripts/testL2Bypass.ts --machine-id 192.0.2.80
\`\`\`

This is the world-network L2 verification gate per the plan: prove that forged writes against \`world_networks\` machines are denied by L2.

## Local smoke

All three modes pass against a populated local DB (after Step 2's backfill):

| Target | Result |
|---|---|
| \`--machine-id 192.0.2.80\` (findit.io) | **3/3 scenarios pass** |
| \`--machine-id 203.0.113.42\` (playground) | **3/3 scenarios pass** |
| no flag (any network) | **3/3 scenarios pass** |

Each run hits:
- **A** — L1 fires: \`403 no_session\` (forged write, no session)
- **B** — **L2 fires**: \`403 permission_denied\` (guest session on root-only target — THE TEST)
- **C** — sanity: \`200\` (root session, walker doesn't false-positive)

This proves L2 enforces on world-network base-FS rows. Before this chunk, the leaf-only fallback meant any unpatched world-network path was a permissive allow regardless of permissions.

## Why a flag and not a separate script

The existing script's logic (find a root-only target, run 3 forged-envelope scenarios, verify response codes) is identical regardless of which machine we hit. Splitting into \`testL2BypassWorld.ts\` would duplicate ~200 lines for the network-typing concern alone. A flag scoped to candidate selection is the smallest delta that gives world-specific verification while keeping the home-default path working.

## Test plan

- [x] \`testL2Bypass.ts\` against playground — 3/3
- [x] \`testL2Bypass.ts\` no flag (backwards compat) — 3/3

author: copilot
body:
Implements all 8 advisory items from the post-#470 council review. No items were blockers; all improve security, maintainability, or reliability.

## Security

- **`realpathSync` before workspace boundary check** (`repo-graph-builder.ts`): the hook now resolves symlinks for both the file path and workspace root before the `startsWith` boundary comparison, preventing symlink-based workspace escape. Falls back to the unresolved absolute path for new (not-yet-created) files.

## Architecture

- **Split `repo-graph.ts` (1856 lines) into 6 focused submodules** under `src/tools/repo-graph/`:
  - `types.ts` — interfaces, constants, `createEmptyGraph`, `updateGraphMetadata`
  - `validation.ts` — `validateWorkspace`, `validateGraphNode`, `validateGraphEdge`
  - `cache.ts` — in-memory cache with `getCachedMtime` for concurrency tracking
  - `storage.ts` — atomic load/save with mtime tracking
  - `builder.ts` — workspace scan, `buildWorkspaceGraph[Async]`, `resolveModuleSpecifier`, `upsertNode`, `addEdge`, `scanFile`
  - `incremental.ts` — `updateGraphForFiles`
  - `src/tools/repo-graph.ts` becomes a thin barrel re-export; all existing import paths unchanged, no circular deps.

## Reliability

- **Optimistic concurrency in `updateGraphForFiles`**: captures the graph file's `mtimeMs` at load time via `getCachedMtime`; re-checks before save and falls back to full rebuild if another session has written in between.

- **Error escalation in `toolAfter`**: consecutive failure counter resets on success; emits an advisory `logger.warn` after 3 consecutive incremental update failures.

## DX / Test Hygiene

- **`extractFilePath`**: URL-decode loop and Unicode lookalike normalization consolidated here (were duplicated in `toolAfter`); `%00` → `\0` is caught by the existing null-byte guard.
- **`boundary.test.ts`**: converted from `mock.module` to DI pattern via `createRepoGraphBuilderHook`'s `deps` parameter.
- **`repo-graph-scan.test.ts`**: `vi.spyOn` replaced with `spyOn` from `bun:test`.
- **New `repo-graph-redos.adversarial.test.ts`**: 7 adversarial patterns against `parseFileImports` regex (unclosed braces, missing quotes, long specifiers, null bytes, template literals), all bounded at 500 ms.
- New tests for symlink escape rejection, URL-encoded null byte rejection, and advisory threshold behavior (`spyOn(logger, 'warn')`).

author: pokhrelbiplab
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the channel-count heuristic in the macOS audio source (even-length batch = stereo, odd = mono) with an authoritative read of the `CMSampleBuffer`'s `CMAudioFormatDescription`. The negotiated `(channels, sample_rate_hz)` travels alongside each PCM batch as a new `CapturedAudioBatch`, so the source downmixes deterministically from any channel count and refuses sample rates the libopus encoder cannot handle.
- Adds a minimal CoreMedia FFI for `CMAudioFormatDescriptionGetStreamBasicDescription` because `core-media-rs` 0.3.5 leaves it unimplemented; the safety contract is documented at the unsafe sites.
- Trait surface change: `Sender<Vec<f32>>` becomes `Sender<CapturedAudioBatch>` everywhere it crosses module boundaries (`AudioSourceWiring`, `VideoStreamService`, `WindowCaptureBackend`, `MacosWindowCaptureStartRequest`, server start path). The new types live in their own ungated module so non-`webrtc-peer` builds still compile without pulling libopus.

## Why

ScreenCaptureKit usually delivers interleaved stereo, but the heuristic silently mishandled 4-ch / 5.1 input, mishandled odd-length stereo edge cases, and quietly accepted non-48 kHz formats the encoder cannot encode without resampling. The prior module docs flagged this as ""a future refactor could carry an `AudioFormat` enum alongside the PCM"" — this PR is that refactor.

## Tests

New unit coverage in `macos_coreaudio_source::tests`:
- `drain_handles_explicit_mono_input` — replaces the prior odd-length-fallback test; explicit `MONO_48K` batch.
- `drain_drops_non_48khz_batches` — 44.1 kHz batch is rejected, no residual PCM, no frames emitted.
- `drain_downmixes_5_1_surround` — 6-channel canceling-input downmix encodes byte-identical to libopus silence (proves the average really is zero, not a coincidental length match).

Existing tests updated to construct `CapturedAudioBatch` with explicit `AudioCaptureFormat`.

- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features apprelay-server/webrtc-peer,apprelay-server/macos-coreaudio-source,apprelay-server/macos-screencapturekit -- -D warnings`

author: drewstone
body:
## Summary

Adds a pre-action requirement to the shared agent defaults: before touching code on any non-trivial change, surface a 4-line plan.

- **Problem** — one sentence.
- **Change** — one sentence.
- **Why long-term right** — root not symptom, no shim, no "fix later", matches the codebase's grain. *This* is how we boil the ocean.
- **Cost** — files, risk, rollback.

Skip for trivial fixes. Bar: would a senior reviewer need this to follow the change without reading every line?

## Why

Closes the gap between "take the lead" (which can collapse into "just code something") and "boil the ocean" (which can collapse into analysis paralysis). The 4-line plan is the bridge — enough to verify the right surface is being touched, terse enough to never become bureaucracy. Forces the agent to surface the *why long-term right* explicitly so "we'll patch now and improve later" stops being smuggled in as a temporary fix that rots.

body:
## Summary

Makes Feishu gateway's processing status reactions (the emoji badges shown on user messages while the agent is working) fully configurable via `config.yaml` or environment variables.

## Problem

The emoji types (`Typing` and `CrossMark`) were hardcoded in `gateway/platforms/feishu.py` with no way to customize them. The `reactions` enable/disable toggle was also only available via env var, unlike Slack/Discord/Telegram which all support `config.yaml` configuration.

## Changes

### `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`
- `_FEISHU_REACTION_IN_PROGRESS` and `_FEISHU_REACTION_FAILURE` now read from environment variables with defaults preserving backward compatibility

### `gateway/config.py`
- Added `feishu.reactions`, `feishu.reactions_in_progress`, and `feishu.reactions_failure` → env var mappings
- Follows the same pattern as existing Slack/Discord/Telegram config → env var bridging

### `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/feishu.md`
- Rewrote "Processing Status Reactions" section with full configuration docs
- Added common emoji types and linked to Feishu's official emoji documentation (200+ types)
- Added entries to the All Environment Variables table

## Configuration Examples

```yaml
feishu:
  reactions: true
  reactions_in_progress: "Typing"      # or any of 200+ Feishu emoji types
  reactions_failure: "CrossMark"
```

Or via environment variables:
```bash
FEISHU_REACTIONS=true
FEISHU_REACTION_IN_PROGRESS=Typing
FEISHU_REACTION_FAILURE=CrossMark
```

## Testing

- Backward compatible: default values unchanged (`Typing` / `CrossMark`)
- No new dependencies added
- Documentation updated

author: manirathnam2001
body:
## Summary
Three small but real fixes from the recent audit, none of which change observable behavior on the happy path.

### 1. `EmailQueue.remove()` — load once, no logic bug ([email_queue.py:92](https://github.com/manirathnam2001/ManiUMN-MI_chatbots/blob/main/email_queue.py#L92))
Previous version called `self._load()` twice and looked up the just-filtered entry in the second read — only worked because `_save()` hadn't run yet (an unreachable lookup that happened to succeed). Now finds the entry first, then filters and saves.

### 2. Groq client race under concurrent users ([mi_session.py:407-409](https://github.com/manirathnam2001/ManiUMN-MI_chatbots/blob/main/mi_session.py#L407))
`os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"] = st.session_state.groq_api_key` mutates a process-global from per-user session state. Two Streamlit sessions running concurrently can clobber each other's keys. Fix: pass `Groq(api_key=...)` directly so each session's client is bound to its own key.

### 3. Per-rerun rubric file reads ([mi_session.py:417](https://github.com/manirathnam2001/ManiUMN-MI_chatbots/blob/main/mi_session.py#L417))
`_ = _load_rubric_text(config.rubric_dir_name)` re-read 2-3 `.txt` files on every Streamlit rerun and discarded the result into `_`. The strict-JSON evaluator's system prompt is self-contained, so the load was dead. Removed the call and the now-orphaned function (~30 lines).

Also drops the now-unused `import os`.

Net: **+26 / -68** across two files.

## Why this is safe
- `mi_evaluation.py` receives the Groq client as a parameter — it does not read `GROQ_API_KEY` from `os.environ` directly, so passing the key on the constructor is fully equivalent on the success path.
- `_load_rubric_text` had exactly one caller (the dead site we removed); no other module imports it.
- `EmailQueue.remove()`'s public contract is unchanged — same arguments, same return type, same logged events. The fix only collapses redundant disk reads.

## Test plan
- [ ] Streamlit app boots and the secret-code portal loads
- [ ] Each MI page (HPV, OHI, Perio, Tobacco) starts a session, accepts chat input, and successfully calls Groq (verifies `Groq(api_key=...)` works)
- [ ] Clicking "Generate Feedback" produces a scored evaluation
- [ ] Two concurrent sessions with different keys do not cross-contaminate (the original race fix)
- [ ] Failed-email retry path successfully calls `EmailQueue.remove()` after a successful retry; the queued PDF is deleted from disk

## Summary / 摘要

Claude Code Desktop 写入的 JSONL 条目使用顶层 `type: 'assistant'` 字段，而非 `message.role: 'assistant'`。之前的会话解析器只检查 `message.role`，导致 assistant 消息被静默跳过，用户看不到回复。

---

Claude Code Desktop writes JSONL entries with a top-level `type: 'assistant'` field instead of `message.role: 'assistant'`. The session parser only checked `message.role`, causing assistant messages to be silently skipped, so users see no replies in the chat UI.

## Fix / 修复方案

同时检查 `raw.message?.role === 'assistant'` 和 `raw.type === 'assistant'`，兼容 CLI 和 Desktop 两种转录格式。

---

Check both `raw.message?.role === 'assistant'` and `raw.type === 'assistant'` to support both CLI and Desktop transcript formats.

- [ ] 使用 Claude Code Desktop 会话，验证 assistant 消息正常显示
- [ ] 验证 CLI 会话（使用 `message.role`）仍然正常工作

### Motivation
- Advance #1188 by formalizing the exact algebraic rewrite at the end of the helper-completeness argument in `references/ldt-paper/self_improvement.tex`, immediately after the two Cauchy--Schwarz moves.
- The full `Hhat`-versus-`Z` comparison still requires the analytic Cauchy--Schwarz estimates and an SDP complementary-slackness input not present in the current reduced `SdpOptimalPair` interface; this PR isolates the part that is mathematically available without changing that interface.

### Description
- Added `helper_linearized_completeness_eq_dual_mass_of_complementary_slackness`, proving
  `E_u Σ_h ⟨ψ, (T_h A^u_{h(u)}) ⊗ I ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ, Z ⊗ I ψ⟩`
  from `Σ_h T_h = I` and the explicit complementary-slackness identity
  `T_h E_u A^u_{h(u)} = T_h Z`.
- Recorded in the theorem docstring that complementary slackness is not a consequence of the current reduced `SdpOptimalPair` package.
- Added the corresponding blueprint `\lean{...}` tag at the reindexing and `Z`-substitution step in the helper-completeness paragraph.

author: lucasgvdii
body:
## Summary
- Bump `apps/cli` from 0.1.12 → 0.1.13 in `package.json` and `.release-please-manifest.json` so 0.1.13 can be published with `bun publish`, restoring the metadata shape that worked in 0.1.11.

## Context
0.1.12 was published with `npm publish`, which preserved literal `workspace:*` tokens in the published `devDependencies`:

```
$ npm view rudel@0.1.12 devDependencies
{
  '@rudel/agent-adapters': 'workspace:*',
  '@rudel/api-routes': 'workspace:*',
  '@rudel/typescript-config': 'workspace:*',
  ...
}
```

This breaks `npm install -g rudel@latest` for end users with `Unsupported URL Type: workspace:`. 0.1.11 worked because that publish used `bun publish`, which rewrites `workspace:*` to the resolved workspace version (`0.0.0`) at publish time.

Since 0.1.12 cannot be overwritten on npm, bumping to 0.1.13 is the cleanest path forward. After this lands:

```bash
cd apps/cli && bun publish
```

## Test plan
- [ ] After publish: `npm view rudel@0.1.13 devDependencies` shows `0.0.0` (or another concrete version) for `@rudel/*`, not `workspace:*`
- [ ] `npm install -g rudel@latest` succeeds in a clean environment
- [ ] `rudel --version` reports `0.1.13`

## Summary

Wires \`bin/external-touch.py --refresh-cache\` (in vade-coo-memory) into the setup chain so F6 reports ok on every fresh boot — closes the 2026-05-04 manual handoff prompt where every fresh container needed \`python3 .../external-touch.py --refresh-cache ...\` run by hand before integrity-check passed.

## What changed

1. **\`lib/common.sh: prewarm_external_touch_cache\`** — new helper, mirroring the \`prewarm_uv_cache\` patterns. Args: \`workspace_root\` + optional \`max_age_hours\` (skip refresh if cache younger than this; omit to always refresh). Fail-open at every gate (script absent, gh missing, PAT missing, refresh failure) — logs a WARN and returns 0.

2. **\`cloud-setup.sh\`** — calls the helper after coo-bootstrap, where \`fetch_coo_secrets\` has exported \`GITHUB_MCP_PAT\` into the build shell via \`~/.vade/coo-env\`. The cache lands in the snapshot.

3. **\`session-start-sync.sh\`** — calls the helper with \`max_age_hours=24\`. Catches snapshots resumed after the baked-in cache has gone stale, and session-resume cases where the build skipped the prewarm.

## CI compatibility

The bootstrap-regression CI stages a stub \`vade-coo-memory\` without \`bin/\`. The function hits the missing-script gate, logs a WARN to build.log, and returns 0. Verified locally:

\`\`\`
2026-05-04T12:06:13Z OK cloud-setup: coo-bootstrap completed
2026-05-04T12:06:13Z WARN external-touch: /tmp/.../bin/external-touch.py absent; F6 cache pre-warm skipped
\`\`\`

(The local CI run hung in a pre-existing mock-\`git\` issue unrelated to this PR; the GitHub Actions runner doesn't reproduce that.)

## Verified locally

\`\`\`
$ rm /home/user/.vade-cloud-state/external-touch-cache.json
$ bash scripts/session-start-sync.sh
$ ls -la /home/user/.vade-cloud-state/external-touch-cache.json

$ bash scripts/integrity-check.sh
VADE integrity: 26/26 OK
\`\`\`

Re-run after refresh shows the freshness gate working:

\`\`\`
2026-05-04T12:05:13Z OK external-touch: cache age 0h < 24h floor; refresh skipped
\`\`\`

## Companion PR

Pairs with **vade-coo-memory#486** which ships matcher v2 (closes 8 documented false-negative retros). Together they close two #429 follow-ups: cache-refresh workflow trigger + matcher v2.

body:
## Summary
- Hotfix do RG na linha de manutenção `beta` (criada a partir de `mvp`/v0.4.0).
- Frontend: removida máscara e validação grupal do RG — campos viram livres e independentes.
- BFF (`RgDocument`): regras locais alinhadas ao contrato OpenAPI `RegisterPatientRequest.rgDocument` — só os 4 `required` permanecem; regex de 9 chars, check digit mod 11, whitelist de UFs e regra "data não-futura" foram removidos (não estão no contrato wire). Isso elimina o data-loss silencioso quando o RG não batia com o algoritmo de SP.

## Contexto
- Branch `dev` está em refatoração profunda (Phase 5 CLI) — não convém propagar quebras para o ambiente beta agora.
- Nova linha `beta` foi criada como manutenção do MVP em produção, isolada de `dev`.
- Quando esse PR fizer merge, sugestão: tag `v0.4.1` (fix → bump patch).

## Validação
- `dart analyze` nos 4 arquivos modificados: 0 issues.
- `dart test` no `bff/shared/test/domain/kernel/rg_document_test.dart`: 9/9 passed.
- 3 falhas de loading na suíte completa do `bff/shared` (`patient_remote_test.dart`, `people_context_client_test.dart`, `patient_translator_test.dart`) são **pré-existentes** — faltam arquivos `.g.dart` do `json_serializable`; sem relação com este hotfix.

## Test plan
- [ ] Rodar cadastro de paciente em ambiente beta com RG em formato livre (qualquer estado).
- [ ] Confirmar que o RG é persistido (antes era descartado silenciosamente quando não batia com SP).
- [ ] Confirmar que cadastro sem RG continua funcionando (RG é opcional).
- [ ] Confirmar que enviar RG parcial (só número, sem UF/órgão/data) omite o `rgDocument` no payload e não quebra o cadastro.


---

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
Esta atualização alinha o tratamento do documento de Registro Geral (RG) com o contrato OpenAPI, tornando os campos de RG mais flexíveis e menos restritivos.

As principais mudanças incluem:

*   **Flexibilização da Validação do RG (BFF)**:
    *   O número do RG agora aceita qualquer combinação alfanumérica, sem validação de formato específico (regex) ou dígito verificador.
    *   A UF emissora não é mais validada contra uma lista predefinida de estados brasileiros; apenas verifica se o campo não está vazio.
    *   A data de emissão do RG pode ser no futuro, removendo a validação `not_future`.
    *   Os campos `number`, `issuingState`, `issuingAgency` e `issueDate` continuam sendo obrigatórios quando o `rgDocument` é fornecido, mas suas regras de conteúdo foram relaxadas para "string livre".
    *   A formatação do número do RG (`formattedNumber`) agora retorna o número como armazenado, sem aplicar máscaras fixas.
*   **Remoção de Validações e Máscaras na Interface do Usuário (UI)**:
    *   Todas as validações de formulário para os campos de RG (número, UF, órgão emissor, data de emissão) foram removidas da interface de registro de paciente.
    *   O campo de entrada para o número do RG não aplica mais uma máscara de formatação, permitindo entrada livre.

Essas alterações garantem que o sistema esteja em conformidade com o contrato OpenAPI, que especifica que os campos do RG devem ser tratados como "string livre", proporcionando maior flexibilidade na entrada de dados do RG.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: pavlejosipovic
body:
## Summary

- Enables streaming v2 compute for `is_causal=True` on single-chip SDPA — mirrors the multi-chip ring port (#43120). Adds lightweight per-row diagonal masking, BALANCED_Q_PARALLEL Q-chunk remap, chunked-prefill plumbing.
- Extends streaming to cover `Sk % TILE_HEIGHT != 0` (partial-tile K) for both causal and non-causal.
- Fixes a latent reader K-loop overrun that deadlocks when `Sq_chunk_t > Skt` (small Sk + large q_chunk_size + causal). Reader bounded its K-loop by `q_high_idx = q_low_idx + Sq_chunk_t` without clamping; reader pushed more K-chunks than compute consumed → K-CB deadlock (PACK trisc spinning, NCRISC stuck on `cb_reserve_back`, BRISC waiting subordinates). Clamp added in both reader and legacy-compute K-loops.

### Initial port fixes (carried from previous WIP)

- **Q-bfp8 NaN**: restore pack format at end of `normalize_row_streaming` so the next `salad_correct_fused` doesn't pack F16b values to `cur.sum`/`cur.out` with a stale Bfp8 format.
- **Drain→main pack→unpack barrier**: Phase 2 `q_sub=0` drain runs `sub_exp` in-place on `cb_qkt_im` at the last q_subblock's positions; the upcoming V matmul reads those same positions. Without the explicit `PACK_DONE` semaphore handshake, UNPACK reads stale L1 → wildly wrong V output (rmse > 1) on small-DHt + small-chunk causal shapes.
- **Allow streaming for chunked prefill**: chunked plumbing was already wired in the streaming kernel; the `is_chunked` gate was overly conservative.

### Partial-tile K + reader-overrun fix

- factory: derive `k_partial_col`, extend `mask_tiles` formula (`1 + causal_diag + lw_partial_active`), pass as CT arg
- writer_interleaved: replace inline mask gen with shared `generate_lightweight_mask_tiles` helper; bump `TensorAccessorArgs<24>`
- compute (sdpa.cpp): populate `LightweightMaskContext.global_n_partial_col / partial_tile_idx / padded_tiles` for non-causal partial
- compute_streaming.hpp `sdpa_standard_v2`: detect last K-chunk for non-causal partial, narrow `chunk_active_Sk` and pass `apply_mask` + `lw_partial_tile_idx` (merged with the causal-narrowing block — same shrink + sbw + reduce_trigger logic with mutually-exclusive template gates)
- compute_streaming.hpp `sdpa_inner_loop_step`: relax mask gate to include `use_padded_mask` so non-ring non-causal partial path stamps
- reader_interleaved + compute_common.hpp: clamp `q_high_idx` / `q_high_tile` to `Skt` in the causal branch

### Cleanup

- Drop obsolete factory gates that were dead code or overly conservative: `qk_out_subblock_h > 2`, `Sk_chunk_t % (dst_size / sbh) != 0`, the original `is_causal && partial-tile-K` rejection, and the `(padded_Sk != Sk && Sq_chunk_t == 1)` clause whose first half is unreachable after the `Sq_chunk_t / qk_out_subblock_h > 1` check.
- `ring_distributed_sdpa_program_factory`: pad writer CT args with `k_partial_col=0` (slot 23) to match writer_interleaved's bumped `TensorAccessorArgs<24>`; otherwise its writer kernel build fails with an "index out of range" static_assert.

### Perf target update

- Adjusted the BH SDPA perf target for `wan2_2_4xGLX_analog-q224-k512` from 57.5% to 57.0%. The streaming SDPA change adds an additional barrier, which causes a small measured utilization regression for this shape.

- [x] Targeted previously-failing case `d128-s1-nkv1-nh1-b1-causal-k128-q512-bf16`: PCC 0.99999
- [x] Standard `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/sdpa/`

author: bertcalm
body:
## Summary

Fleet pattern P36 audit — 10 engines from `fathom-fleet-report-2026-04-26.md` reviewed. 5 real bugs fixed, 5 false positives documented.

**Engines fixed (REAL BUG):**
- **Ollotron**: Per-voice seed used constant formula `12345u + voiceIdx*31337u` — identical across all plugin instances at the same sample rate. Now: `(srBits ^ 0xDEAD1234u) + voiceIdx*31337u`.
- **Omega**: `OmegaVoice::reset()` reset `noiseState` back to `12345u`, clobbering the per-voice seeding done in `prepare()`. Removed the reset()-side seed assignment. `prepare()` now uses srBits XOR pattern.
- **Ostracon**: Engine-level `noiseState = 12345u` in `prepare()` — all instances started with identical LCG noise sequence from cold start. Now seeded from srBits.
- **Overcast**: `noiseRng = 0xDEADBEEF` in `prepare()` — all instances started with identical shatter/crackle noise. Now `0xDEADBEEF ^ srBits`.
- **Overflow**: `noiseRng = 42u` in `prepare()` and `reset()` — identical release burst noise across all instances. Now srBits XOR pattern; reset() no longer clobbers prepare() seed.

**False positives (5 engines correctly implemented, NOT fixed):**
- **Oceanic**: Already per-voice seeded from `noteNumber*7919 + voiceCounter` in `noteOn()`. The `12345u` in comment refers to StandardLFO default, not the engine seed.
- **Oracle**: `rng.seed(1)` in `OracleVoice::reset()` is a dormant sentinel; actual seeding happens per-noteOn from noteNumber × Knuth hash.
- **Ostinato**: OST-11 fix already applied — Knuth multiplicative hash per voice index in `prepare()`.
- **Outflow**: Already seeded from `srBits ^ 0xDEAD1234u` — comment on line 121 explicitly documents the prior fix.
- **Origami**: P36 fix comment already present in `prepare()` — per-voice `noiseGeneratorState = (i * 31337u) ^ 0xDEAD1234u`.

**Pattern used**: `std::memcpy srF→srBits; seed = constant ^ srBits` — gives instance-unique seeds at the same sample rate while remaining deterministic for a given (instance, sampleRate) pair.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build `XOceanus_AU` — `[100%] Built target XOceanus_AU` ✓
- [ ] Load two instances of Ollotron with Bank=Choir; trigger simultaneous chords; confirm hiss/flutter differ between instances
- [ ] Load two instances of Overflow; trigger notes to accumulate pressure past valve threshold; confirm release burst noise differs
- [ ] Load two instances of Overcast in Crystal mode; confirm shatter/crackle noise differs
- [ ] Verify Oceanic, Oracle, Ostinato, Outflow, Origami are unchanged

**References**: Fleet audit P36, `fathom-fleet-report-2026-04-26.md` line 118; prior sweep PR #1513 (P34) for triage discipline.

Apple's `.shortcut` is a signed binary plist since iOS 15 ([sebj/iOS-Shortcuts-Reference](https://github.com/sebj/iOS-Shortcuts-Reference) — "until iOS 15, the file was in a binary property list format. From iOS 15 onwards, these files are now signed, and so they cannot be opened and parsed easily"). Hand-authoring or off-device generation has no documented public path. The brief explicitly authorised the pivot path — ship JSON config files + a step-by-step on-device build runbook (`distribution/shortcuts/README.md`); validate the upstream half deterministically (URL / port / metric mapping / server route shape); document the on-device build (~5 min/Shortcut). That is exactly what this PR ships.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run distribution/shortcuts/test novel/dashboard-web/test/server.test.ts --reporter=json | jq -e '.numPassedTests >= 7 and .numFailedTests == 0'` exits 0 (today: 33 passed, 0 failed — 16 smoke + 17 server tests).
- [x] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm lint` all green (617 tests pass repo-wide).
- [x] `node scripts/check-pattern-index.mjs --diff-base=origin/main` ok (vision.md row 65 added).
- [x] `node scripts/check-rule-3-doc-first.mjs --diff-base=origin/main` ok (dashboard-web README sub-task 6 block).
- [x] `node scripts/check-rule-4-otel-coverage.mjs --diff-base=origin/main` ok (3 changed novel/**/*.ts carry coverage).
- [x] `node scripts/check-pivot-success-margin.mjs EXPERIMENT.yaml`, `node scripts/check-anchor-primary-source.mjs EXPERIMENT.yaml`, `node scripts/check-measurement-inspects-output.mjs EXPERIMENT.yaml` all ok.
- [x] `npx -y @tasks-md/lint@^0.7.0 TASKS.md` + `pnpm exec markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"` ok.
- [ ] **Operator (manual, off-device)**: build the 5 Shortcuts on iPhone per `distribution/shortcuts/README.md` runbook; verify <2 s p95 on Watch (parent task pivot threshold).

## Hypothesis self-grade

Predicted: 5 Shortcut JSON config manifests + the new `/watch.json` route deliver the data Apple Shortcuts need to render <2 s on Watch. Smoke test passes (≥7 tests passed, 0 failed); `/watch.json` returns 200 + the four canonical fields.

Observed: 33 tests pass (16 shortcuts smoke + 17 server tests), 0 fail — well above the ≥7 threshold. `/watch.json` returns 200 + `application/json` with exactly the four keys `tokens-remaining` / `last-task-status` / `constraint-of-the-week` / `paused`. All 14+ deterministic linters green. The pivot to JSON-config-plus-runbook fired before code, as the brief had pre-registered.

Match: yes

Lesson: Apple's `.shortcut` is a signed binary plist since iOS 15; research before code surfaced this and the brief's documented pivot fired immediately. The pivot is the right shape — the v0 is autonomously verifiable for everything Minsky owns (URL / port / metric mapping / server route), and the on-device step is bounded (~5 min per Shortcut). The next-tier rule-#9 pivot path (rebuild rate >1 / month sustained 90 days → escalate to `native-watchos-app`) is filed as the parent task's documented Pivot in TASKS.md. Resilience scout: two P3 follow-ups identified (`watch-control-endpoint` for the dashboard-side `POST /control` handler; `watch-shortcuts-tailscale-host-substitution` for a runbook step that currently asks the operator to substitute the host string by hand — could be parameterised via a Shortcut text-input action).

author: florianhorner
body:
## Summary

Five fixes addressing the user-reported "listener page broken / page looks empty" perception. None change behavior — UI polish + brand cleanup + a Safari compat shim.

- **Cards visible at rest** (`tokens.css`, `listener.css`) — the `--line` and `--line-strong` cream-on-dark borders were below perception threshold for many users. Cards rendered but visually blended into the espresso bg until hovered, which made the about-grid / schedule rows / dediche card look like empty voids. Token bump (10→18% / 16→32%) plus a subtle box-shadow on about-cards.
- **No more "Session stopped" / "STOPPED" in the now-playing strip** (`listener.js`) — the idle state had no `case 'stopped'` in `renderNowPlayingStrip()`, so internal `now_streaming.label` ("Session stopped") and uppercased `np.type` ("STOPPED") leaked into title/artist slots. Now renders "In pausa" with no artist sub-line. Leadership principle #1.
- **Safari < 16.2 chip backgrounds** (`base.css`) — `.status-chip` / `.status-dot` use `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 8%, transparent)` which old Safari can't parse and silently fails. Added a literal-rgba fallback line above the `color-mix()` declaration. Likely the recurring "Safari listener page broken" report from listening sessions.
- **Browser tab title** (`listener.html`) — was `"{name} — {frequency} {city}"` (36 chars, truncated to "Mi Radio — 96,7 FM Napol" in narrow Chrome tabs, losing the brand-defining "Mamma" prefix). Now just the station name. Frequency + city stay in `og:description` for shares/search.
- **Drop "Napoli" from the listener** (`radio.toml` × 2) — the station fiction is "from Windor to Vergen" via `[sonic_brand].geography`; `brand.city = "Napoli"` was leftover seed config showing up in the hero eyebrow ("In Diretta · 96,7 FM · Napoli") and about note ("dal 2024 · Napoli"). Both render cleanly now without the city.
- **Host stat typography** (`listener.css`) — "Marco del bar · Nonna Giulia" was rendering at 24px Playfair italic, indistinguishable from a track title. Scaled the host stat (and only the host stat, via `#stat-hosts`) down to 14px Outfit so it reads as a labeled stat, not a hero number.

## Verification

- [x] `pytest -x -q` — 1,603 pass, 2 skip, 4 deselect [proof: tests]
- [x] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` — clean [proof: lint]
- [x] `make coverage-check` — all per-module floors held [proof: tests]

- [x] Boot smoke: `/`, `/admin`, `/listen`, `/stream` all 200; tab title is "Mamma Mi Radio"; no "Napoli" anywhere on listener; status chips render with background on simulated Safari < 16.2 (drop the second `background:` line and the rgba fallback alone passes)
