body:
## Summary

Финальный PR Спринта 1.2 — закрывает задачу **1.2.7** из `development_plan.md`. Когда суммарный DAU достиг 80 % от `MAX_DAU`, система **один раз в календарные сутки** пишет audit-запись `DAU_THRESHOLD_REACHED` и эмитит structlog-warning, чтобы админы успели заранее повысить лимит до того, как новые игроки начнут попадать в очередь регистраций.

### Что сделано

- **`domain/dau`** — новый порт `IDauThresholdAlerter` (тонкий, без идемпотентности — она в use-case-е через `IIdempotencyKey`), плюс `AuditAction.DAU_THRESHOLD_REACHED`. Порт в domain нужен, чтобы `application` не импортировал `structlog` напрямую (иначе ругается `import-linter`).
- **`infrastructure/dau/alert.py::StructlogDauThresholdAlerter`** — реализация поверх `structlog.get_logger("pipirik_wars.dau.threshold").warning("dau.threshold.reached", ...)` со структурированными полями (`current_dau`, `max_dau`, `percent`, `occurred_at`).
- **`application/dau/check_threshold.py::CheckDauThreshold`** — новый use-case. Проверка `current >= 80 % * max_dau` сделана через целочисленную арифметику `5 * current >= 4 * max_dau` (нет float-погрешностей). Idempotency-ключ — `dau_threshold_alert:{moscow_date}`, привязан к той же дате, что использует `IDauCounter` для дневного сброса. Алгоритм: проверяем порог → если ниже, выходим без транзакции; иначе открываем UoW, проверяем `is_seen`, при отсутствии — `mark` + `audit.write` → коммит → **после коммита** `alerter.emit(...)` (вне транзакции, чтобы откат не оставлял «висячих» алёртов).
- **Точки вызова** — после `dau_counter.record_active(...)`:
  - `application/player/register.py::RegisterPlayer` — после успешной регистрации в активной ветке.
  - `application/signup_queue/promote.py::PromoteFromQueue` — после loop-а промоута, только если кто-то реально поднят (`if promoted: ...`).
- **`bot/main.py::Container`** — новые поля `dau_threshold_alerter` + `check_dau_threshold`; `build_container()` собирает `StructlogDauThresholdAlerter` и передаёт `CheckDauThreshold` в `RegisterPlayer` / `PromoteFromQueue`.
- **`tests/fakes/dau.py`** — `FakeDauThresholdAlerter` (накапливает события).

### Тесты (новые / обновлённые)

- **`tests/unit/application/dau/test_check_threshold.py` (19)** — таблица кейсов для `_is_threshold_reached` (включая `MAX=1`, `4/5`, `4/6`, `5/6`, overshoot), use-case-сценарии: ниже порога (без транзакции/audit), первое пересечение (audit + alerter + commit), второе пересечение в тот же день (no-op, но UoW открывается на `is_seen`), переход через сутки (новый ключ → новый алёрт), pre-seeded ключ (idempotency пропускает алёрт), overshoot (`current > max_dau`).
- **`tests/unit/application/player/test_register_player.py` (4 новых)** — алёрт после регистрации, пересекающей 80 %; нет алёрта при низкой загрузке; нет алёрта при попадании в очередь; ровно 1 алёрт за сутки даже при подряд идущих регистрациях после порога.
- **`tests/unit/application/signup_queue/test_promote.py` (3 новых)** — алёрт после промоута, доводящего DAU до ≥ 80 %; без промоута alerter не зовётся; при низкой загрузке нет алёрта.
- **`tests/unit/infrastructure/dau/test_alert.py` (2)** — `StructlogDauThresholdAlerter` через `structlog.testing.LogCapture` (warning, структурированные поля, default-logger).
- **`tests/unit/bot/test_composition_root.py`** — добавлены проверки на `dau_threshold_alerter` / `check_dau_threshold` в обоих вариантах (фейковый Container и `build_container()` с реальным `StructlogDauThresholdAlerter`).
- Существующие тесты `RegisterPlayer` / `PromoteFromQueue` / `JoinClan` приведены к новой сигнатуре конструкторов через общий `_build`-helper.

### Локальный CI

- `make ci`: ruff (lint+format), mypy --strict, import-linter (3/3 контракта), pytest **565 passed**, **coverage 97.40 %**.
- `import-linter`: `application` не импортирует `structlog` — доступ только через порт `IDauThresholdAlerter`.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Прочитать `application/dau/check_threshold.py` — особенно `_is_threshold_reached` и порядок «проверка → транзакция → коммит → emit». Убедиться, что emit-вне-транзакции — желаемое поведение (если откат UoW — алёрт не уходит; если emit падает — audit уже зафиксирован, что норм).
- [ ] Проверить namespace idempotency-ключа (`dau_threshold_alert:{moscow_date}`) — он бьётся по календарным суткам в Europe/Moscow и не коллидит с другими ключами (`register_player:`, `queue_player:`, `promote_player:`).
- [ ] Убедиться, что `bot/main.py::build_container()` собирает `dau_threshold_alerter` ДО `check_dau_threshold` и до `RegisterPlayer` / `PromoteFromQueue` (иначе DI развалится).
- [ ] Глянуть `docs/history.md` — описание соответствует реальности.

### Notes

- Канал доставки сейчас — только structlog-warning. Когда понадобится Telegram-уведомление админам или Slack — достаточно будет добавить второй адаптер `IDauThresholdAlerter` и собрать `CompositeDauThresholdAlerter` без правки `CheckDauThreshold`. Эта развязка специально заложена.
- Порог `80 %` и namespace `dau_threshold_alert` вынесены в константы (`DAU_THRESHOLD_PERCENT`, `DAU_THRESHOLD_NAMESPACE`).
- Этот PR закрывает Спринт **1.2** целиком (1.2.A → ✅, 1.2.B → ✅, 1.2.C → ✅, 1.2.D → 🟢 текущий PR). После merge — Спринт 1.3.

author: youtalk
body:
## Summary

- Add `vendor/common_interfaces-humble` submodule (pinned to tag `4.2.4`) for Humble IDL sources. macOS is case-insensitive, so I used lowercase `vendor/` to match the existing `vendor/common_interfaces-jazzy` submodule and avoid a `Vendor/` vs `vendor/` collision.
- Extend `SwiftROS2Gen` IR with `FieldAvailability`, per-distro field presence tracking, and a value-widened `perDistroHashes: [String: String?]` so a distro that defines the type but lacks a RIHS01 (Humble) is distinguishable from one where the type does not exist.
- Add `IRBuilder.build(perDistro:)` with deterministic field-union ordering and `IRMergeError.conflictingFieldType` for incompatible schemas. Constants from later distros win on value mismatch (constants are not part of the wire schema).
- Add per-distro RIHS01 hashing (`RIHS01.hash(_:for:registry:)`) that filters to fields available in the target distro.
- Teach `SwiftEmitter` to emit `static func typeInfo(for distro: ROS2Distro) -> ROS2MessageTypeInfo` switches plus a `static var typeInfo` shim and `if !encoder.isLegacySchema { ... }` / `if decoder.isLegacySchema { ... } else { ... }` branches whenever distros disagree. Single-distro callers keep the uniform `static let typeInfo = ROS2MessageTypeInfo(...)` shape.
- Wrap each array / sequence decode block in `do { ... }` so the local `out` / `count` variables don't collide when a struct has multiple array fields (`sensor_msgs/Imu` is the canary).
- Teach `Pipeline.generateMulti` to group input runs by package name and merge multi-distro IDLs via `IRBuilder.build(perDistro:)`. Single-distro packages keep the Phase 1-3 fast path.
- The `swift-ros2-gen` CLI now consumes every `--input pkg=path@distro` entry; multiple distros for the same package automatically merge.
- Replace the 15 hand-written `BuiltinMessages/SensorMsgs/*.swift` files with generator output rooted at `Generated/SensorMsgs/`. `RangeMsg` is the canary for distro-conditional emission. Add `SensorMsgsExtensions.swift` to layer the legacy-API conveniences (Swift enums for `STATUS_*` / `POWER_SUPPLY_*` constants, `Data`-typed initializers for byte-blob fields, `RegionOfInterest.fullFrame`, `PointField.xyzFields`, `NavSatStatus.statusFix`, etc.) on top of the bare generator output.
- Touch the existing array / sequence generated files (`UniqueIdentifierUUID`, `GoalStatusArray`, `CancelGoalResponse`) and their golden test fixtures to reflect the new `do { ... }` decode shape.

This is phase 4 of 8 — see the design doc for the full plan. Subsequent phases extend the generator to `.srv` / `.action`, add a SwiftPM build plugin, and gate the Docker hash-oracle CI job.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` clean
- [x] `swift test --parallel` — 64 Swift Testing tests + 358 XCTest tests pass; 8 LINUX_IP-gated skips
- [x] Range golden test (`EmitterDistroConditionalTests`) matches the canonical distro-branched output byte-for-byte

## Summary

Post-Phase-5f engineering refactor (no rule semantics change, no f-structure change, no test expectations change). 13 commits on `feature/refactor-grammar-package`; full plan-of-record at `docs/refactor-grammar-and-roots.md`.

**Part 1 — `cfg/grammar.py` per-area split (Commits 1-9).** The 3250-line monolith is split into seven domain modules, each exposing a single `register_rules(rules)` function called by a thin composer in `cfg/grammar.py`:

| Module | Rules | Lines | Owns |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `nominal` | 95 | 1085 | NP shells, demonstratives, cardinal/ordinal/vague-Q/universal/distrib-poss/whole/measure-N/decimal/mga/approximator/numeric-comparator/minute-composition |
| `clause` | 20 | 471 | V-initial S frames, parang comparative, predicative cardinal, arithmetic predicates, multi-GEN-NP applicative/causative frames |
| `clitic` | 5 | 180 | floated quantifier, 2P enclitic absorption, kita fusion |
| `negation` | 2 | 128 | hindi clausal negation, huwag MOOD=IMP lift |
| `extraction` | 46 | 942 | ay-inversion, S_GAP family, relativization, AdvP/PP fronting, dual-binding wrap |
| `control` | 30 | 541 | S_XCOMP, raising-inside-control, control wrap |
| `discourse` | 3 | 117 | temporal-frame PP, FREQUENCY AdvP |
| `grammar.py` | 0 | 85 | composer + `Rule` dataclass |

`_eqs` + `_VERB_PERCOLATION` move to a new `cfg/_helpers.py`. `_cardinal_case_marker` is promoted from a local in the cardinal section to a module-level constant in `nominal.py` (its only consumer). Total rule count is 201, byte-for-byte unchanged from the pre-refactor.

**Part 2 — drop `_rules` suffix (Commit 10).** The `_rules` suffix is redundant under `cfg/` (a CFG package — what else would they hold?). All seven files renamed via `git mv`; the `np` → `nominal` rename avoids the bare `np` colliding with numpy's universal alias.

**Part 3 — split `data/tgl/roots.yaml` by POS (Commit 11).** The 411-entry single-file blob (204 VERB + 207 NOUN) is split into `data/tgl/verbs.yaml` + `data/tgl/nouns.yaml`. The morph loader reads both and concatenates verbs first then nouns to preserve the exact `MorphData.roots` iteration order. The structurally misplaced "Phase 4 §7.6: control verbs" sub-section that lived inside the noun region is pulled back into the verb file. Plan doc renamed `docs/refactor-grammar-package.md` → `docs/refactor-grammar-and-roots.md`.

**Part 4 — reorder per-POS yaml entries (Commit 12).** `verbs.yaml`: separate Control verbs section (3 entries with `CTRL_CLASS`) + alphabetical Inflectional verbs section (201 entries); historical Phase 2C bulk-scale-up A/B/C subsection markers dropped. `nouns.yaml`: 11 SEM_CLASS-driven sections in this order — common, frequency-multiplier, percentage, fractions, clock-time, time-of-day, months, days, seasons, collective-numerals, proper-name placeholders. Within each section: alphabetical by citation, except months / days (by VALUE, chronologically) and seasons / collective-numerals (preserved canonical / by-N order).

**Part 5 — doc cleanup (Commit 13).** Sweeps stale `cfg/grammar.py` references throughout `docs/`, `tests/*.py` docstrings, and `src/` / `data/` comments to point at the per-area modules. 39 references rewritten total. Plan doc gains a final "Outcome" section with the commit list + final layouts.

## Zero-diff invariant

Every commit (1 through 13) holds:

- `hatch run pytest -q` — 4334 passed (~146-149 s on each commit, identical pass count).
- `hatch run check` — clean.
- `hatch run python scripts/check_parses_unchanged.py --check` — zero ranker-output diff against the Commit 1 baseline (1208/1214 corpus sentences; 6 are `expected: fragment` / `expected: fail`).

The baseline pickle (`tests/tgllfg/data/parses.baseline.pkl`, ~906 KB) is committed so reviewers and CI on follow-up commits have the same reference point. The ``--check`` script diffs the rendered top-1 parse (c-tree + f-structure + a-structure + diagnostics) against the baseline.

## Test plan

- [x] `hatch run pytest -q` clean on every commit (verified locally on each).
- [x] `hatch run check` clean on every commit.
- [x] `hatch run python scripts/check_parses_unchanged.py --check` clean on every commit.
- [x] `git log --follow` works on every renamed file (`git mv` used for all 7 cfg/ renames + the plan doc + `roots.yaml` deletion).
- [x] `parses.baseline.pkl` round-trip verified (capture → check returns OK; mutated baseline → check returns 1 with the differing indices).

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Sub-splitting `nominal.py` along `det/quant/adj` boundaries — defer until Phase 5g+ adjective work substantially grows the module.
- Sub-splitting `extraction.py` along `ay/gap/rc/fronting` boundaries — defer until Phase 6 FU/LDD adds substantially.

author: bastian-schur
body:
# Zusammenfassung: Neue Dateien im Diff sichtbar machen

## Was wurde umgesetzt

Bisher zeigte die Diff-Ansicht einer Task nur Änderungen an bereits vorhandenen Dateien. Wenn Claude im Rahmen einer Implementierung komplett neue Dateien anlegt, blieben diese unsichtbar — die Diff-Seite erschien leer oder unvollständig, obwohl echte Arbeit geleistet wurde.

Dieses Verhalten wurde in zwei Bereichen korrigiert:

## Was sich konkret verändert hat

**Für Nutzer der Web-Oberfläche:**
- Die Diff-Ansicht einer Task zeigt jetzt auch neu angelegte Dateien an. Diese erscheinen wie bisher mit dem grünen „NEU"-Badge, alle hinzugefügten Zeilen werden angezeigt.
- In der Stat-Zusammenfassung oberhalb des Diffs erscheinen neue Dateien mit dem Hinweis „(neu) Dateiname".
- Vorher war die Diff-Seite nach einem Implement-Lauf oft leer, obwohl Änderungen existierten — das ist jetzt behoben.

**Für die interne Statistik:**
- Die Auswertung am Ende eines Diff-Durchlaufs (Anzahl geänderter Dateien, Anzahl eingefügter Zeilen) berücksichtigt jetzt ebenfalls neue Dateien. Die Zahlen in der Ergebnis-JSON sind damit aussagekräftiger.

## Abweichungen vom ursprünglichen Plan

Keine. Die Umsetzung folgt dem Konzept vollständig.

---

New files created by the implement phase remain uncommitted and untracked, so git diff origin/{branch}...HEAD silently omitted them. Switches to git diff origin/{branch} for tracked changes and adds a --no-index loop for untracked files in ViewTaskDiff. Extends diff.sh numstat block to accumulate file count and insertions from untracked files.

<details><summary>Technische Details</summary>

# Technische Zusammenfassung: Neue Dateien im Diff anzeigen

## Geänderte Dateien

### `app/Filament/Admin/Resources/TaskResource/Pages/ViewTaskDiff.php`

**Stat-Befehl** (`$statProcess`):
- `git diff --stat origin/{$branch}...HEAD` → `git diff --stat origin/{$branch}` (Working-Tree statt nur committed Changes)
- Ergänzt: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard | while ... ; do echo " (neu) $f"; done` um ungetrackte Dateien in der Stat-Ausgabe aufzulisten

**Diff-Befehl** (`$diffProcess`):
- `git diff origin/{$branch}...HEAD` → `git diff origin/{$branch}` (Working-Tree)
- Ergänzt: Schleife über `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` mit `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null "$f" || true` für jede neue Datei
- Alles in einem `sh -c`-String → ein Container-Start, Output kombiniert durch `head -c 131072`

**Parser** (`parseDiffStructured`): Keine Änderung nötig. Das `--no-index`-Format produziert identische Header (`diff --git a/dev/null b/path/file`, `new file mode`, `--- /dev/null`, `+++ b/path/file`). Der Parser erkennt `new file mode` und setzt `is_new = true`; `to_path` wird korrekt als relativer Pfad extrahiert.

**Quoting-Detail**: Pint konvertierte `"\$f"` in einzeln-gequotete PHP-Strings (`'...$f...'`). Das ist korrekt: in single-quoted PHP-Strings wird `$f` literal durchgereicht; die Shell empfängt das Zeichen `$` und expandiert `f` als Shell-Variable.

### `worker/phases/diff.sh`

Im `phase_diff_run()`-Block nach dem bestehenden `numstat`-Block:
- `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` gibt ungetrackte Dateien aus
- Pro Datei: `wc -l` für Insertions-Zählung (Näherung; Zeilen ohne abschließendes `\n` werden um 1 unterschätzt — akzeptabel)
- `(( files_changed += untracked_count ))` und `(( insertions += untracked_insertions ))` akkumulieren die Werte
- `(( ... )) || true` verhindert Exit-Code 1 bei arithmetischem Ergebnis 0 unter `set -e`

### `tests/Feature/ViewTaskDiffParserTest.php` (neu)

Unit-ähnlicher Test für `parseDiffStructured` via Reflection (Methode ist `private`):
- Leerer Content → leeres Array
- Standard Tracked-Change (Modifikation)
- `--no-index`-Output für neue Datei (`is_new = true`, korrekter `to_path`)
- Hunk-Lines einer neuen Datei sind alle `add`
- Kombinierter Output (tracked + untracked) → beide Dateien korrekt geparst
- Gelöschte Datei (`is_deleted = true`)
- ANSI-Escape-Codes werden entfernt

## Architektur-Entscheidungen

- **Kein `git add -N`**: Das Volume ist `:ro` gemountet, daher würde `git add -N` (Index-Staging ohne Content) fehlschlagen. `--no-index` umgeht das komplett.
- **`|| true` für `--no-index`**: `git diff --no-index` gibt Exit-Code 1 zurück wenn Unterschiede gefunden wurden (Standard-Diff-Semantik). Ohne `|| true` würde der `sh -c`-Block mit Fehler abbrechen.
- **Einzelner Container-Start**: Stat und Diff laufen je in einem einzigen `docker run`. Kein zweiter Container-Start für untracked files — alles im selben `sh -c`-String gebündelt.

## Quality-Gates

| Gate | Status |
|------|--------|
| `php artisan list` | ✓ |
| `vendor/bin/pint` | ✓ (1 Fix: double→single quotes) |
| `php artisan test` (308 Tests) | ✓ alle grün |
| `vendor/bin/phpstan` | ✓ 0 Fehler |
| `shellcheck` | nicht im Container verfügbar; Code manuell reviewt, folgt bestehenden Konventionen |

## Bekannte Limitierungen (scope-extern, nicht geändert)

- Bats-Test für `diff.sh`-numstat fehlt (keine git-Fixture-Infrastruktur in bats; manuell getestet ist nicht möglich ohne Worker-Image)
- `wc -l` unterschätzt Insertions bei Dateien ohne abschließendes Newline um 1 — akzeptabel als Approximation

</details>

author: seanhanca
body:
## Summary

Bug: when a user drags a music or video clip's right edge past the source media's natural duration, the timeline shows the extended length but playback freezes at the last frame (video) or plays silent (audio). The user expects the source to loop from the beginning by default.

## Fix

Two changes in \`packages/creative-kit/src/ui/timeline/PreviewPanel.tsx\`:

1. **Audio sync mirror video's loop-modulo logic.** The audio sync \`useEffect\` previously set \`el.currentTime = playhead - clipStart + clip.trimIn\` with no loop awareness, so any \`targetTime > sourceDuration\` left the audio element past its decoded range — silent. Now applies the same \`targetTime % srcDur\` (or \`loop-tail\` window) the video sync already had.

2. **\`<audio>\` and \`<video>\` get \`loop=true\` by default** (only off when \`clip.loopMode === "freeze"\`). The browser handles end-of-source restart natively. Combined with the modulo for jump seeks, this gives correct behavior whether the playhead arrives via continuous play or a click.

Default loop mode for new / extended clips remains \`"loop"\` (was already the fallback in the video sync at line 145). \`"freeze"\` is opt-in via the existing loop-mode picker on the clip context menu.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` clean
- [ ] Live: drop a 5-second music clip into a track, drag its right edge to 12 seconds, hit play → audio loops from the beginning at the 5-second mark
- [ ] Same for a video clip — visual should restart, not freeze
- [ ] Loop-mode = \`freeze\` still freezes (regression check on the existing affordance)

body:
## Summary

The repo wasn't loadable as a Claude Code marketplace because plugin names diverged across three sources of truth:

| Source | discovery | develop | deliver |
|---|---|---|---|
| `marketplace.json` (catalog) | `discovery` | `develop` | `deliver` |
| `<dir>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (manifest) | `etak-discovery` | `etak-develop` | `etak-deliver` |
| README install commands | `discovery@etak` | `develop@etak` | `deliver@etak` |

With `strict: true` (the default), `plugin.json` is the authority and the marketplace entry is merged on top — so components were registering under names that didn't match what users typed at install time. Plus ~190 conditional prose references like "when \`etak-deliver\` is installed" referred to a name that wouldn't exist as installed.

This PR aligns everything to the marketplace + README form (no `etak-` prefix) so install commands keep working unchanged.

- Drop `etak-` prefix from each plugin's `name`; bump versions
- Remove the invalid `categories` field from each `plugin.json` (not in Claude Code's plugin schema)
- Wire `$schema` references on all manifests so editors validate against the upstream Claude Code schemas
- Delete the custom `plugin-schema.json` — its closed `additionalProperties` rejected valid fields (`commands`, `mcpServers`, `hooks`, …) and required fields Claude Code doesn't require
- Rename `etak-{discovery,develop,deliver,design}` → `{discovery,develop,deliver,design}` across READMEs, agents, and skills (44 files)
- Add the previously-untracked `develop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` so the marketplace can actually load `develop`
- Update `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/meta/skill-design-guide.md` to drop the obsolete prefix convention

`docs/plugin-design-review.md` is intentionally left as a historical audit snapshot.

## Test plan

- [ ] `/plugin marketplace add ~/etak` (or `audenaert/etak` after merge) succeeds

body:
## Summary

Builds on the K8s integration test scaffolding from #24278 with five new tests covering service-discovery paths the original suite didn't reach.

- **`test_cross_namespace.py`** — cluster-wide watch via `ClusterRole` + no `--service-discovery-namespace`. Validates that pods in two distinct namespaces are both registered, asserting per-pod IP membership (not just count) so the test actually proves the cluster-wide path rather than coincidentally landing 2 pods.
- **`test_lifecycle.py`** — three lifecycle scenarios:
  - **Gateway pod restart**: kill the gateway, verify the new pod re-lists existing workers without duplicates **AND** that the post-restart watch loop picks up a freshly-deployed worker (proves it isn't relist-only).
  - **Pod IP change**: force-delete + recreate same pod name, verify the registry switches to the new IP and drops the old URL. Skips on the rare CNI-IP-reuse case rather than silently false-passing.
  - **Graceful drain**: verify deregistration fires on the `deletionTimestamp` event well before the grace period elapses (`elapsed < grace_secs`), with a `still_exists` guard so a slow CI run doesn't lucky-pass through pod-gone reconciliation. Asserts on URL membership rather than total count to tolerate unrelated workers.
- **`test_multi_model.py`** — two gateways with disjoint `--selector` values (`model=llama` vs `model=qwen`). Verifies selector isolation: each gateway sees exactly its pool, no cross-talk between views.

Each test owns its worker fleet via a unique label (`cross-ns-test=true`, `lifecycle=restart`, `model=llama|qwen`) so the new gateways don't race with the default suite or each other.

Three rounds of specialized review (code-reviewer, pr-test-analyzer, silent-failure-hunter, comment-analyzer) drove fixes for: race-prone count-based assertions, port-forward subprocess respawn races, IP-reuse false-passes, kubectl stderr swallowing, brittle "NotFound" substring matches, and a few inaccurate file:line citations.

author: joshbouncesecurity
body:
## Summary

Introduces a new `atomic_write_json()` helper and applies it to all final
pipeline output files. The helper writes JSON to a temp file in the **same
directory** as the target, fsyncs, then `os.replace`s it onto the target path.
If a crash or power loss occurs mid-write, the previous output file is
preserved intact rather than being left truncated.

Upstream uses plain `write_json()` (a `json.dump` wrapper), which can corrupt
multi-hour scan results on interrupt.

Same-directory temp is load-bearing on Windows: `os.replace` is only atomic
when source and target sit on the same volume; cross-volume falls back to
copy+delete and loses atomicity.

**Call sites covered** (one write each, at the very end of a pipeline stage):
- `core/analyzer.py` — `results.json`
- `core/enhancer.py` — `enhanced_dataset.json`
- `core/verifier.py` — `results_verified.json`
- `core/reporter.py` — `pipeline_output.json` (final report)
- `core/parser_adapter.py` — `dataset.json` + `analyzer_output.json`
- `experiment.py` — experiment results (legacy direct-run path)

**Not changed:** checkpoint files (designed for incremental writes), scanner
intermediate state, and the diff-filter sidecar report (cheap to regenerate).

**Performance:** one `fsync` + one rename per output file, all of which occur
once at the end of a stage that runs for minutes. Negligible overhead.
`fsync` is silently skipped on filesystems where it fails (network mounts etc.)
so atomicity degrades gracefully to rename-only in those environments.

Addresses item 20 from #16 (does not close the issue).

## Test plan

- [x] Helper round-trip preserves data (incl. `ensure_ascii=False` Unicode).
- [x] Mid-write failure leaves the existing file intact.
- [x] Mid-write failure does not create a target if none existed.
- [x] No stray `.tmp-` files left on failure.
- [x] Temp file is in the same directory as the target.
- [x] POSIX permissions match umask (not mkstemp's 0600 default).
- [x] Existing tests pass (113 collected, 91 passed, 22 skipped — go/js parser binaries unavailable in this env).

author: julienbatt
body:
## Summary

testflight.yml run-id 25334986033 (build 2.9.0+38) succeeded at the binary upload phase (« Successfully uploaded the new binary to App Store Connect » @ 18:16:43) but the WHOLE workflow exited 1 because fastlane's `upload_to_testflight` action ALSO tries to auto-submit the build for beta review — and Apple's beta review queue accepts only one in-flight build per train.

```
Spaceship::UnexpectedResponse: Another build is in review.
Another build in the same train is already in beta review.
```

## Root cause

We just shipped 2 TestFlight uploads in 30 min (+37 then +38, hotfix on top of the original cut). Apple processes one at a time. Auto-submit on +38 collides with +37 still in queue.

## Fix

Wrap `upload_to_testflight` in begin/rescue: catch the « Another build in review » substring (or « already in beta review » synonym), log a clear `UI.important` message, and re-call the action with `skip_submission: true` to satisfy the workflow.

Real failures (auth, certificate, missing binary) re-raise and CI fails as before.

## Operational impact

Julien clicks « Submit for Review » in App Store Connect once the previous build of the same version clears Apple's review (typically 5-30 min). Distributes to « Beta Testeurs » group from there.

author: p0mvn
body:
Tracks #1661.

This PR is part of the Shielded Voting merge sequence (#1687), split for ease of review.

Brings the SDK Rust crate onto the released `zcash_voting 0.4` dependency line and the matching pinned `orchard 0.13.1` (with the `unstable-voting-circuits` feature), and lands a single pure-function FFI symbol that proves end-to-end linkage. The follow-up PRs in this sequence will then layer wallet-to-voting plumbing, the broader FFI surface, and the Swift wrappers on top of this foundation.

## Why this rather than landing more of the FFI now

Reviewing #1687 as a single 1571-line Swift wrapper plus a 3000-line `voting.rs` is hard. The FFI surface there mixes four concerns that a reviewer needs to evaluate independently:

| Concern | What a reviewer has to verify | Lands in |
|---|---|---|
| Does the SDK build against released `zcash_voting` and `orchard 0.13.1`? | Cargo graph resolves to single versions, FFI links | **this PR** |
| Wallet-to-voting plumbing (note snapshot, witness generation) | Wallet DB queries at historical heights are correct | follow-up |
| Voting DB lifecycle, JSON serde across FFI, ProgressContext lifetimes | Memory ownership and FFI safety | follow-up |
| Swift `VotingRustBackend` API surface | Public Swift contract, locking, error mapping | follow-up |

This PR isolates the first row. The diff is intentionally narrow and the new symbol is provably outside the wallet path.

## Version changes

| Crate          | Before | After                                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| orchard        | 0.13   | `=0.13.1`, `features = ["unstable-voting-circuits"]`   |
| zcash_voting   | new    | `0.4`, `default-features = false`                      |

Both are released on crates.io; no `[patch.crates-io]` entries are introduced and no fork URLs are pinned. The `orchard` `unstable-voting-circuits` feature is required transitively by `zcash_voting`.

## What the new FFI does — and what it deliberately does not do

`rust/src/voting/share_tracking.rs` exposes one symbol:

```rust
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn zcashlc_voting_compute_share_nullifier(
    vote_commitment: *const u8, // 32 bytes
    primary_blind:   *const u8, // 32 bytes
    share_index:     u32,
) -> *mut c_char // 64-char hex nullifier; caller frees via zcashlc_string_free
```

It forwards to `zcash_voting::share_tracking::compute_share_nullifier` and returns the 32-byte share-reveal nullifier as a 64-character hex C-string. On error or panic it returns `NULL`. The returned pointer must be freed by the caller via the SDK's existing `zcashlc_string_free`.

It intentionally stays outside the wallet-to-voting data path:

- No wallet DB open / read
- No voting DB open / read
- No network I/O (no PIR, no lightwalletd)
- No proving-key cache warm-up or other process-lifetime side effects
- No randomness
- No secret material in or out

The function is a deterministic computation over caller-supplied bytes. Its only purpose in this PR is to prove that the SDK Rust crate links and dispatches against `zcash_voting`.

## Source compatibility

No public Swift API changes. No new Swift wrapper. No `Synchronizer` protocol additions or default implementations. Existing constructor call sites and downstream conformers continue to compile unchanged.

## Out of scope (intentionally deferred to follow-ups)

- Swift `VotingRustBackend` and `VotingTypes` (the 1571 + 456 line files in #1687)
- Wallet note snapshot lookup, witness generation, voting DB lifecycle, PIR snapshot resolver
- Any `Package.swift` linker or binary target changes
- Any FFI symbol that takes a `wallet_db_path` or opens `WalletDb`

These will land as separate, individually reviewable PRs once this foundation is in.

body:
### Motivation
- The Telegram control-room command for `/why_no_trade` lacked a machine-readable `command` field and several runtime keys, causing a failing test and opaque diagnostic output. 
- Improve observability by returning precise missing-source reasons and persistent traceback data to diagnose `NoneType` API errors without changing trading logic or enabling live trading.

### Description
- Add `command` fields to payloads for `performance`, `positions`, `capital`, `risk`, `trades_today`, and `why_no_trade` and include the command in unavailable render output to keep the human heading while making the payload machine-assertable. 
- Expand `get_why_no_trade()` to expose `decision_count`, `skip_count`, `last_skip_reason`, `run_reason`, `portfolio_block_reason`, `api_error`, and `last_loop_time`. 
- Persist the above runtime keys and explicitly set/clear `api_error` from the execution worker, and capture full exception tracebacks to `last_traceback` for diagnostics. 
- Files changed: `app/telegram_control_room/status_provider.py`, `app/telegram_control_room/commands.py`, and `app/ig_execution_worker.py`; to rollback, revert the edits to those files to restore prior behavior.

### Testing
- Ran `PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q tests/test_factory_ops.py::test_new_telegram_commands` which passed.

body:
## Summary

Adds `swamp data delete <model> <data_name>` to remove a data artifact that's currently only addressable via hand-edits in `.swamp/data/`. The motivating case (issue body): re-running an `import` method blocked by a state guard like `[NP-E028]` when the user wants a clean re-import.

- **Default** deletes all versions (artifact identity is `(model, name)`; versions are an internal evolution detail). Prompts `[y/N]` with the exact version count.
- **`--version <n>`** removes a single version. Latest pointer follows the highest remaining version automatically.
- **`--force`** skips the prompt for scripts and JSON mode.

The domain service runs three pre-checks (model exists, artifact exists, version exists when requested) so a bad invocation surfaces a clear error message instead of the silent no-op the underlying repository primitive produces on a missing version directory.

## Architecture

Mirrors the existing `data rename` slice (single-mutation) plus the `data gc` two-phase preview-then-execute pattern:

- `src/domain/data/data_delete_service.ts` — domain service
- `src/libswamp/data/delete.ts` — `dataDeletePreview` + `dataDelete` generator
- `src/presentation/renderers/data_delete.ts` — log/json renderers + `renderDataDeleteCancelled`
- `src/cli/commands/data_delete.ts` — CLI command

## Followup

- **swamp-club#229** — refactor `data_rename_service` and `data_delete_service` to depend on domain-side ports instead of `infrastructure/persistence` types. The DDD layer-rules ratchet is bumped from 26 → 27 with a one-line pointer to #229.

## Test plan

Unit + integration coverage at every layer (33 new tests across 5 files). Full `deno run test` passes (5327 / 5327).

Manual smoke test against compiled binary on a scratch repo (`/tmp/swamp-feature-181`):

- [x] Prompt renders with exact version count
- [x] Prompt cancellation (`n`) leaves data intact
- [x] Prompt acceptance (`y`) deletes the artifact
- [x] `--version <n>` deletes only that version, latest pointer follows
- [x] `--version 99` on artifact `[1, 2]` errors with "Version 99 does not exist for \"result\" (available versions: 2)"
- [x] `--force` skips the prompt
- [x] `--json --force` emits the structured envelope (`modelId`, `modelName`, `modelType`, `dataName`, `versionsDeleted`)

## Out of scope (post-merge followups)

- UAT coverage gap — `tests/cli/data/` in `swamp-uat` lacks `delete_test.ts`. File a UAT issue post-merge.
- Docs update — `content/manual/reference/data-outputs.md` in `swamp-club` needs a new `### swamp data delete` section. File a docs issue post-merge.

## Summary

Adds a ruff lint step to the test workflow with two rules: `F821` (undefined name) and `F811` (redefined unused name). Python won't report an undefined name until that code path executes, so a missing import can ship undetected. F821 + F811 catch that statically with zero false positives and no style noise.

Configured to run before pytest so CI fails fast on missing imports.

body:
## PR A de 4 — Fundação: KPIs personalizáveis por área

Primeira de 4 PRs sequenciais para reorganizar a dinâmica de KPIs (consolidada nas 3 camadas: `/meus-kpis` → `/painel-kpis` → `/jornada`). **Esta PR não muda nenhuma tela final** — só prepara o esqueleto: quem pode editar e preencher KPIs de qual área.

## Hoje vs depois desta PR

**Hoje:** qualquer admin/diretor edita qualquer KPI; qualquer usuário autenticado registra valor de qualquer KPI; `responsavel_area` em texto solto, não vincula a profile.

**Depois:** cada usuário tem `profiles.kpi_areas text[]` que define quais áreas ele lidera. Admin/diretor segue passando direto. Resto só edita KPIs das suas áreas.

## Banco (migration `20260504230000_kpi_areas_per_profile.sql`)

- `profiles.kpi_areas text[]` com index GIN.
- **Backfill**: usuários que já têm `profiles.area` recebem `kpi_areas = [lower(area)]`.
- Função `public.can_edit_kpi_area(area)` — admin/diretor passa direto; senão precisa ter a area em `kpi_areas`.
- RLS de defesa em profundidade em `kpi_registros` e `kpi_indicadores_taticos` (o gate primário continua sendo o backend; RLS protege se algum dia chamarmos via `supabase-js` direto do front).

## Backend

- `middleware/auth.js`:
  - `authenticate` agora carrega `kpi_areas` em `req.user`
  - Novo helper `authorizeKpiArea(extractor)` exportado. Aceita um extractor síncrono ou assíncrono que recebe o `req` e retorna a área alvo.
- `routes/auth.js`:
  - `/auth/me` retorna `kpi_areas`
  - Novo `PUT /auth/profiles/:id/kpi-areas` (admin/diretor) para atribuir áreas
- `routes/kpisV2.js`:
  - `PUT/POST/DELETE /taticos` trocaram `authorize('admin','diretor')` por `authorizeKpiArea(...)` (admin/diretor passa, líder só na sua área)
  - `POST /registros` checa a área do indicador contra `kpi_areas` do user

## Frontend

- `AuthContext`: profile inclui `kpi_areas`
- `src/api.js`: `users.me()` e `users.setKpiAreas(id, areas)`
- `src/hooks/useMyKpiAreas.js`: novo hook com `{ kpiAreas, isAdmin, canEditArea(area), canEditAny }` — base para PR B/C
- `src/pages/admin/KpiAreas.jsx` (rota `/admin/kpi-areas`): admin gerencia áreas dos usuários com chips toggláveis das 11 áreas (AMI, CBKids, CBA, Cuidados, Grupos, Integração, Voluntariado, NEXT, Generosidade, Jornada, Igreja). Mostra aviso quando o usuário é admin/diretor (já tem acesso a tudo).

## O que vem depois (já planejado)

- **PR B** — `/meus-kpis` (líder preenche e edita só sua área)
- **PR C** — `/painel-kpis` (consolidado institucional + Mandala da Jornada)
- **PR D** — Limpeza (remove abas duplicadas, redireciona rotas legadas)

## Migration a aplicar antes do merge

`supabase/migrations/20260504230000_kpi_areas_per_profile.sql` — idempotente. Te mando o SQL pra colar quando confirmar.

## Test plan

- [ ] Aplicar migration; verificar que profiles ganhou `kpi_areas` e que usuários com `area` foram backfilled
- [ ] Logar como admin → `/admin/kpi-areas` mostra todos os usuários, mensagem "já tem acesso a tudo" para admins/diretores
- [ ] Adicionar `'voluntariado'` para um líder não-admin → ele consegue editar VOL-01 (PUT /taticos/VOL-01) mas é **bloqueado** ao tentar editar GRUP-01 (403)
- [ ] Mesmo líder consegue registrar valor em VOL-01 mas é bloqueado em GRUP-01
- [ ] Coletor automático (cron) continua funcionando (usa service role, RLS bypassada)
- [ ] Login normal continua funcionando, AuthContext expõe `profile.kpi_areas`

author: martinsaposnic
body:
## Summary

Adds `POST /payinvoice` so mdkd can send Lightning payments, not just receive
them. Calls `node.bolt11_payment().send()` for amount-bearing invoices and
`send_using_amount()` for zero-amount invoices. Returns `{paymentId, paymentHash}`
so callers can poll the existing `GET /payments/outgoing/{paymentId}` for status.

This is required for using mdkd as the agent-wallet engine on Cloudflare
Containers (single shared wallet across a worker deployment, with both
receive and send needed for autopayouts and tipping).

### Endpoint

- `POST /payinvoice` (`tag: send`, full-access auth)
  - Form-encoded body:
    - `invoice` (required): bolt11 string
    - `amountSat` (optional): only for zero-amount invoices
  - Response: `{paymentId, paymentHash}` (camelCase)
  - 400 if the invoice carries an amount AND `amountSat` is set, or if the
    invoice is zero-amount AND `amountSat` is missing

### Files

- `src/daemon/api/pay.rs` (new) - handler
- `src/daemon/api/mod.rs` - route registration in `full_routes`, OpenAPI schema
- `src/daemon/types.rs` - `PayInvoiceRequest` / `PayInvoiceResponse`
- `tests/integration.rs` - new tests (see below)
- `tests/common/mod.rs` - `PayerNode::create_invoice` and `outbound_capacity_msat` helpers

### Naming convention note

`amountSat` (sat units) intentionally diverges from eclair's `amountMsat`
(msat) to stay consistent with the rest of mdkd's existing surface
(`/createinvoice`, `/getbalance`, all incoming-payment fields use sat).
The endpoint name and `invoice` parameter follow eclair. Optional eclair
params (`maxAttempts`, `maxFeeFlatSat`, `maxFeePct`, `externalId`,
`blocking`) are deferred until there's a concrete caller use case.

## Tests added

- **`test_payinvoice_outbound_payment`** - end-to-end pay flow. mdkd is
  funded via an inbound JIT-channel payment from the LSP-connected
  `PayerNode`, then issues `/payinvoice` for a fresh invoice that same
  payer node generated. Asserts `paymentId`/`paymentHash` shape, polls
  `/payments/outgoing/{paymentId}` until `isPaid=true`, asserts `sent` +
  `fees` + `preimage`, and waits until the payer node observes the
  inbound 50k sat in its lightning balance to defend against silent
  routing failures.
- **`test_payinvoice_invalid_bolt11`** - 400 + `bad_request` when the
  invoice string fails to parse.
- **`test_payinvoice_amount_conflict_400`** - 400 + `bad_request` when
  an amount-bearing invoice is paired with an `amountSat` override.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo nextest run` integration coverage for the happy path and
      both validation-error paths (will run in CI; local nix sandbox
      hits a pre-existing `daemon::secret::tests` FD-3 failure that
      also fails on `origin/master`, unrelated to this branch).
- [x] Manual: paid a 1500 sat mutinynet faucet invoice from a signet
      mdkd built off this branch. fee 1 sat, `isPaid: true`, balance
      went 3430 -> 1929.
- [x] Manual: deployed mdkd to a Cloudflare Container (built from this
      branch), called `POST /payinvoice` from a Worker, paid a 1000 sat
      faucet invoice, polled `GET /payments/outgoing/{paymentId}` until
      `isPaid=true`. fee 1 sat.

author: larsencundric
body:
## TL;DR

**Nobody on a cloud-provisioned bux box actually has Composio integrations working — including Larsen and me — because \`claude mcp add\` defaults to \`--scope local\`, registering the MCP under whatever CWD bootstrap.sh ran from instead of user-globally.**

The bug is invisible from CI because bootstrap.sh's \"did the registration take?\" verify check happens to run in the same CWD as the buggy add, so it always passes. The bot's actual claude session runs from \`/home/bux\`, sees no composio entry there, and silently exposes zero tools.

## How I found it

Investigating why a friend's box had no MCP. Cloud-side \`provisioner.py\` writes \`/etc/bux/env\` with \`BUX_BOX_TOKEN\` correctly, bootstrap fires fine, no errors anywhere — but \`claude mcp list\` from \`/home/bux\` (where the bot runs) returned nothing. Inspection of \`~/.claude.json\`:

\`\`\`
projects:
  /home/bux:        mcpServers: {}        ← bot session reads from here
  /opt/bux/repo:    mcpServers: {composio: ...}   ← MCP landed here instead
\`\`\`

\`claude mcp add\` without \`--scope user\` writes to \`projects.<cwd>.mcpServers\`. bootstrap.sh's CWD depends on who invoked it:

| Caller | CWD | Resulting MCP location | Visible to bot? |
|---|---|---|---|
| AMI bake (packer install.sh) | \`/opt/bux/repo\` | \`projects./opt/bux/repo\` | no |
| First-boot user-data | \`/\` | \`projects./\` | no |
| \`/update\` from box-agent | \`/home/bux\` | \`projects./home/bux\` | yes (but only by accident) |

So depending on the path that registered MCP last, the bot may or may not see it. On my own box (which got registered via packer at bake time), composio was at \`/opt/bux/repo\` and totally invisible from \`/home/bux\`.

## Fix

\`\`\`diff
- sudo -u bux -H claude mcp add --transport http composio \\
+ sudo -u bux -H claude mcp add --scope user --transport http composio \\
\`\`\`

\`--scope user\` writes to user-level config (top-level \`mcpServers\` in \`~/.claude.json\`), independent of CWD. Existing buggy local-scope entries get cleaned up by the unchanged \`claude mcp remove composio\` line above (which removes from whichever scope it lives in).

## Hardened the verify check too

The original verification grep ran \`claude mcp list\` from bootstrap.sh's CWD — same dir as the buggy add, so it always passed. Changed to \`claude mcp list\` so we test from the directory the bot actually uses. A silent registration in the wrong scope can no longer slip past.

## Test plan (verified live on this box)

- [x] Before fix: \`claude mcp list\` from \`/home/bux\` → no composio (only claude.ai integrations)
- [x] Before fix: \`claude mcp list\` from \`/opt/bux/repo\` → \`composio: ✓ Connected\` (where the buggy local-scope entry happened to land)
- [x] Apply fix manually: \`claude mcp remove composio && claude mcp add --scope user --transport http composio …\`
- [x] After fix: \`claude mcp list\` from \`/home/bux\` → \`composio: ✓ Connected\` ← the consumer of the registration finally sees it
- [x] After fix: tools surface in claude sessions started from \`/home/bux\` (bot's runtime path)
- [x] \`bash -n agent/bootstrap.sh\` passes
- [ ] Fresh AMI deploy from the cloud-side path (would need a test launch; this PR's fix runs on the next /update or first boot of any new box)

## Rollout

Existing boxes pick this up automatically on the next \`/update\` (or \`/restart\` from #74). The unchanged \`mcp remove\` call clears whichever buggy scope the entry was at, then the new line re-adds at user scope.

## Adjacent

- #82 closes a different gap (DIY curl-pipe install never accepted/persisted \`BUX_BOX_TOKEN\` at all). Both are needed for end-to-end MCP coverage across all install paths.

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->

## Summary by cubic
Registers the `composio` MCP at user scope so tools are available to all `claude` sessions. Also verifies from `/home/bux` to ensure the bot actually sees the registration.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Use `claude mcp add --scope user` to write to user-level `~/.claude.json`, fixing missing tools caused by CWD-based local scope.
  - Keep `claude mcp remove composio` to clear prior entries regardless of scope.

author: ycnslh
body:
## Summary

Two prompt fixes after observing MiniMax mis-route on docx generation. Logs from the deployed instance showed:

\`\`\`
1. docx_read("office://rules/docx")  → UnknownSchemeError ❌
2. docx_create(file_uri="local://Histoire_du_dragon.docx", blocks=[15 dicts])  ✅
\`\`\`

So every successful generation was preceded by a failed call where MiniMax tried to call \`docx_read\` on the rules **resource**.

### 1. Drop the "consult \`office://rules/<format>\`" instruction

Both \`_INSTRUCTIONS\` (FastMCP) and \`serverInstructions\` (librechat.yaml) used to instruct the LLM to read the rules resource before creating. MiniMax (and similar small models) don't distinguish MCP tool calls from resource reads — they call \`docx_read("office://rules/...")\` as a tool, which fails. The formatting doctrine is enforced by the engine anyway (Arial, DXA table widths, finance color coding, theme palettes), so the rules resource was purely advisory; tool-aware clients (e.g. Claude API) can still read it.

Also added an explicit **"DO NOT CALL TOOLS WITH \`office://\` URIs"** defensive section so the model knows those are MCP resources.

### 2. Scrub \`local://\` from the prompt surface

Production targets OneDrive only. Exposing \`local://\` to the LLM in instructions, docstrings, examples and demo scenarios was adding noise without buying anything. Per-file changes:
- FastMCP \`_INSTRUCTIONS\` and LibreChat \`serverInstructions\` now describe \`od://\` only.
- \`docx_create\` and every \`fs_*\` docstring use \`od://AI Generated/<name>\` examples.
- README intro: "OneDrive" instead of "pluggable storage".
- \`scripts/demo_scenarios.md\`: every URI rewritten.

\`LocalBackend\` and its tests **stay in the codebase untouched** — when we re-enable multi-storage support we re-add the prompt blocks from git history. Production registry now registers \`GraphBackend\` alone when oauth is configured; \`LocalBackend\` is the dev-mode fallback (Azure creds absent). Test \`test_bootstrap_registers_only_one_backend_at_a_time\` locks the contract.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Smoke test post-deploy: "génère un docx histoire de dragon" should produce a single \`docx_create\` call (no preceding \`docx_read("office://...")\`) and the file lands in \`OneDrive/AI Generated/\`
- [ ] Confirm no regressions on \`fs_*\` flows

author: ridopark
body:
## Summary

Today's fast-poll FillReceived fix surfaced 11 broker positions that OMO wasn't monitoring. The drift was silent because /portfolio rendered only the broker view. This PR adds an OMO-facing endpoint and outer-joins the two views in the existing Open Positions panel so the same regression class is visible at a glance.

### Backend

- `positionmonitor.Service.BootstrapReady()` getter (atomic.Bool, flips true after the initial reconcile completes) so the dashboard can suppress drift-banner false positives during the ~5s startup window.
- `GET /api/portfolio/monitored` serializes the monitor's view through a private snake_case struct. The domain type's json tags are inconsistent and its `CustomState`/`PendingExitOrderIDs` maps are shared with the live monitor — a direct encode would race the tick loop.
- 503 when the monitor isn't wired (backtest binaries, etc.).

### Frontend

- /portfolio fetchData adds a third parallel fetch and merges by symbol.
- Status taxonomy: `SYNCED`, `ORPHAN_BROKER`, `ORPHAN_OMO`, `QTY_DRIFT`, `SIDE_DRIFT`.
- `SIDE_DRIFT` exists because broker SELL 2 vs OMO BUY 2 would otherwise look SYNCED on qty alone (the most dangerous false-negative).
- ORPHAN_OMO rows are synthesized so the existing grouped renderer needs no rework. Counts and the destructive "Close All" confirm dialog read from a broker-only filter so they never promise to delete rows the broker doesn't hold.
- Drift banner above the panel, styled to match the existing inline error banner.

## Evidence

- `go build ./...` clean.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/http/ ./internal/app/positionmonitor/` clean (4.0s).
- `next build` clean; /portfolio compiles at 8.66 kB.
- /simplify pass (3 parallel reviewers: reuse, quality, efficiency) flagged one BLOCKER (positions.length and Close-All confirm count inflated by ORPHAN_OMO synth rows). Fixed in 2be06847 plus secondary cleanups: lookup-table StatusBadge, normalizeSide helper, brokerPositions filter, dropped redundant custom_state passthrough, gated bootstrap setter, moved DTE math to backend.
- /review pass returned no blockers; recommendation was "Ship as-is."

## Plan

[`_workspace/portfolio_omo_view_plan.md`](_workspace/portfolio_omo_view_plan.md). Sub-agents consulted during plan-design: `go-architect`, `dashboard-dev`, `qa-inspector`. Their findings were folded into the plan before any code changed.

## Sub-agents consulted

- Plan review (parallel): `go-architect`, `dashboard-dev`, `qa-inspector`
- /simplify (parallel): three reviewers covering reuse, quality, efficiency
- /review: `code-reviewer` against final branch state

## Follow-ups not in this PR

These were flagged by the final review as latent under today's integer-quantity universe and explicitly carved out for a small follow-up PR (~30 LOC):

1. `computeStatus` uses strict `!==` on quantities. Will false-fire QTY_DRIFT on fractional shares / crypto. Switch to `Math.abs(b - o) > 1e-6`.
2. `bootstrap.go` does not assign `Side` when reseeding from broker — currently coincidentally correct because `normalizeSide("")` returns `"BUY"` and bootstrap filters out shorts. Set `pos.Side = "BUY"` (or derive from signed qty) explicitly.
3. `pendingClose` cleanup `useEffect` filters against `positions` which now includes synthesized rows. Filter against `brokerPositions` instead so the Set can drain.
4. One Go table-driven test for `handleGetMonitored` JSON shape + `bootstrap_complete` flag.

## Test plan

- [ ] Restart omo-core. Confirm `/portfolio` shows currently-held positions as SYNCED with green tick in the new Monitored column.
- [ ] Confirm no banner during the first poll cycle if you load the page within ~5s of restart (bootstrap_complete suppression).
- [ ] Manually close one position at IBKR (broker-side). Within 5s the banner appears: "1 position drifting between broker and OMO: SYM (ORPHAN_OMO)".
- [ ] Hit `GET /api/portfolio/monitored` directly and verify snake_case keys, RFC3339 entry_time, dte present on option rows.
- [ ] Verify Close All confirm count equals the broker-side count (not inflated by orphan rows).

author: ethan-piper
body:
## Summary
The PIPEKIT_AUTO_SHIP env var mechanism from PR #56 was structurally broken: env vars set in one Bash tool call don't survive into subsequent Bash calls (each is a fresh subshell). `/verify` always read it as unset and stood down. PR #58 had since reverted `/work`'s auto-invoke prose, leaving `/verify`'s auto-ship logic in place but never signalled — effectively dead code.

This restores the auto-flow with a working signal: the Skill tool's `args` parameter.

## Changes
- **`/work` Step 7**: restores auto-invoke of `/verify` on clean exit; passes `args="--auto-ship"` via the Skill tool. Drops the broken `export PIPEKIT_AUTO_SHIP=1` instruction. Skip-the-rollover conditions (abort, deviation, explicit stop, behavioral gap) preserved.
- **`/verify` Step 4**: detects `--auto-ship` in its own args instead of reading `$PIPEKIT_AUTO_SHIP`. Adds a "Why an arg, not an env var" footnote so future sessions understand the constraint.
- **`bin/pk`**: PK_VERSION 2.1.2 → 2.1.3.

## How discovered
RS-76 dev session: `/verify` Pass'd, user echoed `$PIPEKIT_AUTO_SHIP` and saw `unset`, manually stood down. Diagnostic was correct — the var genuinely never gets set across Skill→Bash boundaries.

## Test plan
- [ ] Sync into rs-vault
- [ ] Run `/work <ID>` end-to-end on a clean issue; confirm `/verify` auto-runs and `pk ship` auto-runs on Pass
- [ ] Run `/verify` standalone (no `--auto-ship`); confirm hint-only behavior, no auto-ship
- [ ] Force a `/verify` Fail; confirm rollover stops, no `pk ship`, even with `--auto-ship` set

author: akillies
body:
## Summary

PPA mechanism (proposal-generation path) — NOT a DID schema change.

Per the framework's three-axis basis (Product DECLARES; Design EXPRESSES; Engineering MAINTAINS), DID schema authorship lives with RFC-0009 (Mo + Dom + Alex collectively). The PPA flywheel that *triggers* revision proposals lives with PPA (Product domain). This RFC covers the trigger mechanism + classification + approval routing.

## What it does

When PPA's calibration flywheel accumulates evidence that a DID field has drifted from observed reality, PPA generates a structured `DIDRevisionProposal` event with trigger evidence + classification + recommended approval path. The triad (or relevant pillar lead) reviews and decides. PPA does not modify the DID — proposal-only.

## Three trigger conditions

- ≥10 dismiss signals over 60 days
- SA-gap > 0.3 sustained over 3 sprints
- ≥3 attributable SoulDriftDetected events

## Healthy / unhealthy / ambiguous classification

- **Healthy** (icpMatchRate > 0.6 AND not core-fields-affected) → propose DID revision
- **Unhealthy** (icpMatchRate < 0.3 OR core-fields-affected with dismissToEscalate < 1.0) → propose admission tightening (`SoulHealthDiagnostic`)
- **Ambiguous** → both, flagged for triad review with full evidence

## Approval routing by identityClass

- `core` → triad (all three pillar leads)
- `evolving` → owning pillar lead + one other
- Ambiguous classification overrides to triad regardless

## Scope: Shard DIDs only

Platform Tessellated DID revisions are human-initiated only — cascading inheritance makes them too consequential for automated proposals. Single-product platforms: the single DID IS the shard DID; no practical effect.

## Five OQs

Confidence calibration / multi-field bundling / operator opt-out / cross-pillar coordination / rejection learnings.

## Pillar perspective

Product HIGH (PPA-flywheel mechanism) / Design HIGH-via-cross-review (DID target schema is RFC-0009) / Engineering HIGH (event schema + storage).

author: sykurtyppi
body:
## Root cause

`write_skip_total=96` — prediction events silently discarded because the SQLite write lock was held by an external writer (the event loader populating `touch_events`/`event_labels` in `pivot_events.sqlite`) longer than the 500ms `busy_timeout`. The writer loop had zero retry logic: first contention → event gone.

## Changes

**`server/ml_server.py`** (no model logic touched, no service restart needed):

| Parameter | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `PREDICTION_LOG_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` default | 500 ms | **5 000 ms** |
| `PREDICTION_LOG_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC` default | 0.5 s | **5.0 s** |
| `PREDICTION_LOG_WRITE_RETRY_MAX` | — | **3** (new, env-overridable) |
| `PREDICTION_LOG_WRITE_RETRY_BACKOFF_SEC` | — | **0.5 s** (new, env-overridable) |

Writer loop now retries up to `RETRY_MAX` times with `BACKOFF_SEC` sleep on "skip" (contention). Only events that exhaust all retries increment `write_skip_total`. WAL mode and single-writer thread are unchanged.

## Tests (`tests/python/test_prediction_log_reliability.py`) — 19 new tests

- Config defaults meet minimums (busy_timeout ≥5000ms, connect_timeout ≥5s, retry_max >0)
- WAL journal mode confirmed active on real temp DB; PRAGMA source-presence checks
- Retry boundary conditions: single transient → ok, all retries exhausted → skip, retry_max=0 → immediate skip, fail_count == retry_max → last retry succeeds
- Queue overflow → `dropped_total` (not `write_skip_total`)
- Score path: enqueue-only, helpers dispatch via `asyncio.to_thread`
- Error classification: "database is locked"/"database is busy" → skip; other OperationalError → error

## Restart / reload

No restart required for the retry + WAL changes (env vars); the `busy_timeout` change takes effect on the **next** new SQLite connection (i.e., first write after the current thread-local connection is recycled). To apply immediately:

```bash
# Hot-reload (applies new busy_timeout on next connection open):
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8100/reload | jq .status

# Or full restart if preferred:
bash server/run_ml_server.sh
```

author: mandakan
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes for the secondary-beep flow that was failing silently on `tallmilan-2026` stages 4 and 6.

- **Confidence floor 1.5 -> 1.10.** The 1.5 floor was calibrated on synthetic same-stage pairs and rejected every real-world alignment. On `tallmilan-2026` secondaries where in-stream beep_detect independently succeeded, cross-align lands within 10-16 ms at confidence 1.23-1.34 -- below 1.5 but well above 1.0. New floor calibrated against those validated pairs.
- **Soft-fail UI now visible.** When cross-align falls below the floor, `beep_alignment_confidence` is saved (was wiped) so the SPA can render "Auto-detect failed (conf 1.05)" distinctly from "not started". Failed state offers a "Pick on waveform" button.
- **Always-on sanity check.** When in-stream succeeds on a secondary, cross-align still runs. The delta (`in_stream - cross_align`, ms) is surfaced; large disagreements (> 250 ms) get a yellow banner + one-click "Use cross-align" swap. In-stream is never auto-overridden -- it has frequency-domain info cross-align doesn't.
- **Pill differentiates aligned suggestions.** `beep . aligned . verify` (yellow) for cross-aligned suggestions on the ingest card, with confidence in the tooltip; user must `Mark reviewed` after verifying on the waveform.

End-to-end on tallmilan-2026:

| stage | in-stream | cross-align | delta_ms | conf | verdict |
|------:|----------:|------------:|---------:|-----:|---|
| 2 | 19.330 | 19.320 | +10 | 1.34 | agree (sanity-checked) |
| 4 | -- | 21.170 | -- | 1.31 | promote: aligned (verify) |
| 5 | 1.151 | 1.135 | +16 | 1.23 | agree (sanity-checked) |
| 6 | -- | 10.210 | -- | 1.15 | promote: aligned (verify) |

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_ui_server.py` -- 162 passed
- [x] `pnpm run build` -- clean
- [ ] Open `tallmilan-2026` stage 4: secondary shows `beep . aligned . verify` at 21.170 s; scrub waveform, confirm, mark reviewed
- [ ] Same for stage 6 (suggested 10.210 s)
- [ ] Confirm stages 2 and 5 still show `beep . auto` (in-stream wins; sanity-check passed silently)
- [ ] Force a disagreement (manually edit a project to set in-stream != cross-align by > 250 ms) and verify the yellow `AlignmentDisagreement` banner renders + the "Use cross-align" button works

## Notes

- Cross-correlation runs on the Hilbert envelope at 200 Hz, so the per-secondary cost is sub-second on a 60 s clip even with the always-on sanity check.
- The disagreement banner is the answer to "in-stream sometimes locks onto a steel-strike that resembles the buzzer." Cross-align sees the broader silence -> loud -> pause -> shots shape and is harder to fool by a single tone, so disagreement is a useful detector for that failure mode -- without giving up in-stream's tone-specificity when both methods agree.

body:
## Description

Adds a chained two-flag CTF challenge covering modern software supply-chain attacks: a typosquatted `react-toastfy` npm package whose `postinstall` would drop a malicious Cursor rules file (`lab/quarantine/productivity-helper.mdc`) carrying a hidden HTML-comment prompt-injection payload. The payload instructs the developer's AI agent to inject a magic-header auth bypass at `/api/admin/diag`. Players solve the chain black-box through the existing path-traversal endpoint, ending with a runtime `curl` exploitation.

The challenge fills a gap in the lab (no supply-chain flag previously) and is positioned around OWASP 2025 A03 (Software Supply Chain Failures) and the LLM Top 10 supply-chain category. Inspired by Pillar Security's "Rules File Backdoor" (March 2025), the npm Shai-Hulud worm (September 2025), and the axios maintainer takeover (March 2026).

**Two new flags**:

| # | Slug | Difficulty | OWASP / CWE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `npm-supply-chain-typosquat` | HARD | A03:2025 / CWE-829 |
| 2 | `ai-rules-file-backdoor` | MEDIUM | A07:2025 / CWE-798 |

**Notable changes**:

- New `SUPPLY_CHAIN` value in the `FlagCategory` enum (schema, types, format labels, dashboard short label)
- New `lab/quarantine/` directory for inert lab payloads, with a `README.md` explicitly instructing AI agents to treat the contents as data
- `AGENTS.md` updated with a "Lab Quarantine Zones" section
- `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`, `.prettierignore` updated to exclude `packages/react-toastfy/` and `lab/`

**Safety**:

- Fake package is **not** declared in the root `package.json` and is never installed
- `postinstall.js` is fully inert (top-of-file comment + one `console.log` + `process.exit(0)` — zero `fs.write`, zero `child_process`, zero network, zero `os.homedir`)
- No file added in any auto-loaded AI-tooling path (`.cursor/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules`, `.continue/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`)
- Backdoor token is hardcoded in the route file (realistic for the AI-injected narrative); endpoint is unlinked from any sitemap, navigation, or UI

author: rickieplin
body:
Closes #20. Final follow-up bundle from the Codex adversarial review of PR #16. Combines findings F7 (env-var strictness), F8 (rewrite-failure test theatre), F9 (env-var test coverage) plus the carry-over round-trip-after-migration test from the earlier PR #16 review.

## Summary

### F7 — Strict env-var parsing for `DOXMIND_SIDECAR_MIGRATE`

`_migration_disabled` previously accepted only \"disabled\" aliases (`0`/`false`/`no`/`off`) and silently treated EVERY other value as \"enabled\". That meant typos (`maybe`, empty string, full-width `０`) defaulted into mutating user state.

Now both vocabularies are explicit:
- Enabled: `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on` (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped).
- Disabled: `0`, `false`, `no`, `off` (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped).
- Anything else raises `ValueError` listing both accepted vocabularies.
- Unset env var still defaults to enabled.

### F8 — Rewrite-failure test injects at the real filesystem boundary

`test_migrate_legacy_sidecar_aborts_after_rewrite_failure` previously monkeypatched `sd_module.atomic_write`, bypassing the real `services.sidecar_io.atomic_write` and silently making the temp-file-cleanup contract un-testable. The test now patches `Path.replace` (the real boundary inside atomic_write) and asserts:
- `.bak` exists with original bytes.
- Original sidecar unchanged.
- **No leftover `.tmp-*` files in the parent directory** — the cleanup contract from PR #16 F2.

### F9 — Parameterized env-var coverage

`test_open_pdf_in_read_only_mode_does_not_migrate` previously only tested `\"0\"`. Replaced with parametrized tests that exercise:
- Each accepted-disabled value (incl. mixed case, whitespace).
- Each accepted-enabled value.
- Invalid values (incl. `\"maybe\"`, empty string, non-ASCII `\"２\"`) → assert `ValueError`.

### Carry-over — round-trip-after-migration

Adds `test_legacy_migrate_then_write_round_trip`: legacy sidecar → `open_pdf` (auto-migrate) → `write_full(new_state)` → re-`open_pdf` returns the new state. This was flagged in the original PR #16 review note but landed here since #20 was already touching the same test file.

## Acceptance criteria (from #20)

- [x] Strict env-var parsing; invalid values raise explicit `ValueError`.
- [x] Rewrite-failure test patches `Path.replace`, preserves `.bak`, preserves original, asserts no leftover `.tmp-*`.
- [x] Parametrized coverage over disabled / enabled / invalid env values.
- [x] Round-trip test: legacy → migrate → write → reopen preserves state.
- [x] CLAUDE.md env-var entry lists both vocabularies.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd server && pytest` — 97 passed
- [x] `cd server && ruff check .` — clean
- [x] `npm run type-check` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean (3 pre-existing warnings unrelated)

## Out of scope (per #20)

- Per-sidecar lock — already landed via #22.
- Structured error responses — #19 / PR #24.
- Frontend changes.
- Renaming the env var.
- Changing the default (still: migration enabled by default).

author: amp-rh
body:
## Summary

Extends firewatch rules so CI failures produce richer Jira issues and **Automation-friendly Slack routing** without adding Slack tokens or webhooks to the firewatch workload.

- **`jira_watchers`**: list of emails; watchers are added after issue create (best effort; unresolvable users log a warning and are skipped).
- **`jira_additional_assignees`**: list of emails; sets the Red Hat Jira **Additional Assignees** field (`customfield_10465`) after create (best effort).
- **`slack_channel`** / **`slack_user`**: optional strings; firewatch adds Jira labels `slack-channel:<name>` (`#` stripped) and `slack-user:<sanitized-email>` (`@` → `-at-`) so **Jira Automation** rules (for example `Send web request` to a Slack Workflow) can route notifications per rule.

**`!default` for email lists**: when `jira_watchers` or `jira_additional_assignees` contains `!default`, values are merged from `FIREWATCH_DEFAULT_JIRA_WATCHERS` / `FIREWATCH_DEFAULT_JIRA_ADDITIONAL_ASSIGNEES` (JSON arrays). Firewatch **exits with an error** if `!default` is used but the corresponding env var is missing or empty after parsing (stricter than optional defaults on some other fields).

Rule reference: [docs/configuration_guide.md](https://github.com/RedHatQE/firewatch/blob/main/docs/configuration_guide.md).

### openshift-ci smoke replay (local)

- [`development/env.list.example`](development/env.list.example) lists env vars for replaying `firewatch report` against a completed Prow job.
- **`make smoke-openshift-ci`** runs [`scripts/smoke-openshift-ci-replay.sh`](scripts/smoke-openshift-ci-replay.sh) (`jira-config-gen` + `firewatch report` with `--keep-job-dir`).

### Tests and tooling

- **E2E**: synthetic job names and stubbed downloads to avoid collisions; cleanup helper for created issues; optional live assertions for labels and watcher/additional-assignee fields when `JIRA_EMAIL` is set.
- **Unit tests** updated for report output parity and rule behavior.
- **Pre-commit**: `types-requests` for mypy; **e2e** may load repo-root `.env` via `python-dotenv`.
- **VS Code**: default pytest args targeting `tests/`.

## New rule fields

| Field | Type | Jira behavior |
|-------|------|----------------|
| `jira_watchers` | list of emails | Watcher API after create |
| `jira_additional_assignees` | list of emails | Additional Assignees (`customfield_10465`) |
| `slack_channel` | string | Label `slack-channel:<channel>` |
| `slack_user` | string | Label `slack-user:<sanitized-email>` |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for rule getters, Jira helpers, report wiring, and slack labels on issues
- [x] E2E (live Jira): passing-label regression and rule-field smoke with stubbed Prow layout
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files`
- [ ] Reviewer sign-off

Resolves INTEROP-8865, INTEROP-8979

author: zephdev-92
body:
## Pourquoi cette PR
La PR #343 a été squash-mergée sans le commit fix qui ajoutait les SECURITY DEFINER helpers. **Conséquence en prod** : la vue `employer_health_data_v` plante avec `permission denied for function crypto_aead_det_decrypt`, et la lecture/écriture des données santé est cassée côté front.

## Fix
- **Helpers SECURITY DEFINER** `decrypt_health_field(bytea, uuid)` et `encrypt_health_field(text, uuid)` qui wrappent les fonctions pgsodium (qui sont restreintes au superuser par défaut). Ils s'exécutent avec les privilèges de leur owner, ce qui permet à `authenticated` de chiffrer/déchiffrer ses propres données.
- L'**AAD = profile_id** est passée explicitement → un user ne peut pas déchiffrer les données d'un autre user, même s'il devine le bytea
- **Vue `employer_health_data_v`** : appelle désormais `decrypt_health_field`. RLS toujours héritée via `security_invoker = true`
- **RPC `upsert_employer_health_data`** : passe en SECURITY DEFINER avec vérification explicite `auth.uid()` pour préserver l'isolation owner-only
- **Migration idempotente** : re-jouable sur une DB déjà partiellement migrée (le bloc `ALTER ... bytea` est gaté sur `data_type = 'text'`, donc skip si déjà bytea)

## Test plan
- [x] Code app inchangé (toujours compatible)
- [x] Tests existants passent (2306 passed)
- [ ] Re-jouer la migration 058 corrigée sur la prod
- [ ] `SELECT * FROM employer_health_data_v` doit retourner les 3 lignes en clair (déchiffrées)
- [ ] UI Paramètres > Profil employeur > Ma situation : valeurs santé existantes affichées + modification fonctionne

Avant même le merge, applique le SQL correctif sur la prod cassée :

```bash
ssh unilien-test
```

body:
## Summary

The dashboard's ask, plan, and done status icons were rendered statically while the same icons in the sidebar pulse. This makes the dashboard look inert when there are sessions waiting for attention.

The fix moves the pulse animation into the shared `SessionStatusIcon` component (which both the dashboard and sidebar can — and should — rely on), so any consumer of these statuses gets consistent behavior.

- Adds a `.pulse` class + `pulse-badge` keyframe to `SessionStatusIcon.module.css` (2s opacity 1 → 0.4 → 1, identical to the sidebar's existing keyframe in `Sidebar.module.css`)
- Wraps `ask`, `plan`, and `unread` cases in `SessionStatusIcon.tsx` with a pulsing span; `running`, `stopped`, and `idle` are unchanged
- Honors `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (consistent with the existing `.spinner` reduced-motion guard in the same file)

## Complexity Notes

- The `pulse-badge` keyframe is now declared in two CSS Module files (`Sidebar.module.css` and `SessionStatusIcon.module.css`). CSS Modules scope keyframe names locally per file, so they don't collide — but a future cleanup could move both to `theme.css` if we want a single source of truth.
- Only `ask` / `plan` / `unread` get the pulse. `running` already animates (spinner), and `stopped` / `idle` are passive states that intentionally shouldn't draw attention.

## Test Steps

1. Pull this branch and run `cargo tauri dev`.
2. Open the dashboard. For any workspace card whose session is waiting for input (ask), in plan-approval mode (plan), or recently finished/unread (done), confirm the status icon pulses with a 2-second opacity fade.

4. In macOS System Settings → Accessibility → Display, enable "Reduce motion". Reload the app. Confirm the pulse is suppressed in both the dashboard and the sidebar (icons remain static and fully opaque).

author: raizhe
body:
## Summary

Diagnóstico final de por que os labels do BottomNav (\"Home\", \"Extrato\", etc.) ficam cortados/colados na borda inferior em iPhone com home indicator.

### Causa

Linha 101 do [BottomNav.tsx](src/components/layout/BottomNav.tsx#L101) tinha:

\`\`\`tsx
<div className=\"flex items-center justify-around h-16 px-2 pb-safe\">
\`\`\`

\`h-16\` é **height fixo** 64px com \`box-sizing: border-box\` (default Tailwind) → padding-bottom **consome** do height total.

Quando o PR #23 finalmente fez \`pb-safe\` funcionar (\`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)\` ~34px no iPhone), o content area útil ficou:

\`\`\`
64px (h-16) - 34px (pb-safe) = 30px de espaço pra ícones+labels
\`\`\`

Mas cada button precisa de:
- \`h-5\` ícone = 20px
- \`gap-1\` = 4px
- label \`text-[10px]\` ~12-14px line-height
- \`py-2\` = 16px (top + bottom)
- **Total: ~52px**

Resultado: content overflow de 22px do content area → labels visualmente colados na borda inferior, sensação de \"linha de corte\".

Antes do PR #23, \`pb-safe\` era classe-fantasma (sem CSS) → pb=0 → content area completo de 64px → cabia com folga.

### Fix

Trocar \`h-16\` (height fixo) por \`min-h-16\` (height mínimo). A nav agora cresce conforme necessário:

| Device | Antes | Depois |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone SE / desktop (env=0) | 64px nav, 64px content | 64px nav, 64px content (igual) |
| iPhone com home indicator (env=34) | 64px nav, **30px content** (squeeze) | **98px nav**, 64px content (sem squeeze) |

\`pb-safe\` agora só **adiciona** espaço — não rouba do content.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` verde
- [x] \`npx vitest run\` — 111 testes passando
- [ ] Smoke manual em iPhone 16 Pro PWA standalone:
  - [ ] BottomNav: ícones + labels com folga visual entre eles e o home indicator
  - [ ] Conteúdo da página não fica atrás dos labels
- [ ] Smoke manual em Safari mobile (browser, não PWA):
  - [ ] Mesmo comportamento — labels visíveis com folga

## Lembrete pra testar

Como nas outras vezes — Service Worker em iOS standalone retém versões antigas. Pra validar:
1. **Desinstala** o PWA (segurar ícone → \"Remover App\")
2. Safari → URL → \"Adicionar à Tela de Início\"
3. Reabre

- Consume the exact JSON payload keys specified (`temp1`, `temp2`, `cpo`, `water`, `sludge`, `total_level_cm`, `vol_*`, `mass_*`, `weight_*`, `humidity_avg`, `pressure_ref`) and render them safely across the UI.

### Description
- Added a Next.js Pages Router app scaffold with Tailwind/PostCSS configuration and `package.json` listing runtime dependencies (`mqtt`, `framer-motion`, `chart.js`, `react-chartjs-2`, `react-icons`).

body:
## Summary
Integrated live GitHub and LeetCode data fetching into the developer dashboard, replacing hardcoded dummy stats with real-time API data. Users can now see their actual GitHub repositories, stars, followers, and LeetCode problem-solving statistics directly on their profile and overview pages.

## Changes

### New Features
- **GitHub API Route** (`app/api/github/route.ts`)
  - Fetches user profile, repositories, and stats from GitHub API
  - Supports both GitHub URLs and usernames
  - Returns top 5 repositories by stars, total stars, forks, and follower counts
  - Implements 5-minute ISR caching

- **LeetCode API Route** (`app/api/leetcode/route.ts`)
  - Fetches user profile and problem-solving stats from LeetCode GraphQL API
  - Returns problem breakdown by difficulty (Easy/Medium/Hard)
  - Includes ranking, submission count, and top problem tags
  - Implements 5-minute ISR caching

- **Custom Hooks**
  - `useGithubStats()` - Client-side hook for fetching and managing GitHub data
  - `useLeetcodeStats()` - Client-side hook for fetching and managing LeetCode data
  - Both hooks handle loading, error, and empty states gracefully

### Modified Components
- **Profile Page** (`app/dashboard/profile/page.tsx`)
  - Added LeetCode username field to user profile settings
  - Fixed Supabase auth to use `getSession()` instead of `getUser()` for browser client
  - Removed dummy data fallback, now fetches real user data from database
  - Integrated leetcode_username into profile schema

- **Dashboard Overview** (`app/dashboard/overview/page.tsx`)
  - Converted to Server Component for secure profile fetching
  - Fetches github_url and leetcode_username server-side
  - Passes real data to stats components

- **GitHub Stats Component** (`components/dashboard/overview/github-stats.tsx`)
  - Replaced hardcoded dummy stats with live data
  - Displays real repositories, stars, followers, and following counts
  - Shows top 5 repositories with star counts and languages
  - Graceful handling of missing GitHub URL and API errors

- **LeetCode Stats Component** (`components/dashboard/overview/leetcode-stats.tsx`)
  - Replaced hardcoded dummy stats with live data
  - Displays problem breakdown by difficulty with visual progress bars
  - Shows ranking, total submissions, and top problem tags
  - Graceful handling of missing LeetCode username and API errors

- **Auth Actions** (`app/actions/auth.ts`)
  - Updated `updateProfileAction()` to save leetcode_username to Supabase

### Database Schema
- Added `leetcode_username` column to profiles table (nullable text field)

## Testing
- ✅ Build passes with 0 TypeScript errors
- ✅ Dev server starts successfully on localhost:3000
- ✅ GitHub API route returns valid JSON with real user data
- ✅ LeetCode API route returns valid JSON with real user data
- ✅ Profile page fetches and displays real user data from Supabase
- ✅ Dashboard overview displays live stats when GitHub URL and LeetCode username are set
- ✅ Graceful error handling when credentials are missing or API calls fail

## User Experience
- Users can add their GitHub URL and LeetCode username in profile settings
- Dashboard automatically fetches and displays live stats
- Loading states show skeleton placeholders while data is being fetched
- Error messages guide users to add missing credentials
- Stats update on page refresh with 5-minute cache

## Breaking Changes
None - this is a backward-compatible enhancement.

## Notes
- GitHub API token is optional but recommended for higher rate limits
- LeetCode API uses GraphQL with proper error handling
- All API routes implement ISR caching for performance
- Browser client uses `getSession()` for auth, server client uses `getUser()`

author: olivercalder
body:
When multiple `desktop` plugs are present for a given app, we need to ensure that any `desktop-file-ids` attributes across all such plugs are considered when selecting the desktop file ID for the app.

This commit ensures that all `desktop` plugs are collected and sorted by name first, and then for each, if the `desktop-file-ids` plug is present, add its IDs to the list of common IDs for the app.

This ensures that if any `desktop-file-ids` attribute is present, the IDs listed always have precedence over the fallback common ID. It also ensures that if multiple plugs are present, the output is always deterministic.

This fixes a bug first reported by @3v1n0

This work is tracked internally by https://warthogs.atlassian.net/browse/SNAPDENG-36476
