The block names unit of analysis, bootstrap method/seed, primary endpoints, multiplicity stance, judge state with reliability/validity/calibration/bias as explicitly unmeasured, practical-delta source, and causal scope.

- Diff (6): "Methodology unchanged across runs" framing — verdict change is attributable to the prompt change because methodology held constant.

Phase 0.2: docs/concepts.md added — eight sections (defensible verdicts, non-claims, verdict states, trust floor vs decision policy, failure-as-data, evidence and audit bundle, privacy and redaction, examples of misleading outputs whatif must never produce) plus a glossary appendix.

author: deanmarano
body:
## Summary

- Ports all 9 Rails-private overrides from \`MySQL::SchemaDumper\` into \`connection-adapters/mysql/schema-dumper.ts\`
- Closes 0→9/9 (0%→100%) for \`connection_adapters/mysql/schema_dumper.rb\`
- 23 unit tests covering each override

## Methods implemented

All override the abstract base and match Rails layout/order:

- \`prepareColumnOptions\` — adds \`unsigned\`, \`autoIncrement\`, \`size\` prefix for tiny/medium/longtext/blob, virtual column \`as\`/\`stored\`/\`type\` prefix
- \`columnSpecForPrimaryKey\` — strips \`autoIncrement\` for integer+auto_increment PKs
- \`isDefaultPrimaryKey\` — also requires \`autoIncrement\` and non-\`unsigned\`
- \`isExplicitPrimaryKeyDefault\` — integer type without auto_increment
- \`schemaType\` — \`timestamp\` sql_type → \`"timestamp"\`; \`enum\`/\`set\` → full sql_type string
- \`schemaLimit\` — suppresses limit for \`text\`/\`blob\` family
- \`schemaPrecision\` — \`time\`/\`timestamp\` precision 0 → omit; \`datetime\` precision 0 → \`"nil"\`
- \`schemaCollation\` — omits collation when it matches the cached table default (\`tableCollationCache\`, keyed by table name, populated by adapter before column iteration); always emits when cache is not loaded
- \`extractExpressionForVirtualColumn\` — reads from \`virtualExpressionCache\` (table → column → pre-serialized expression literal); returns \`undefined\` when not loaded

## State fields

Two public cache fields for adapter wiring:

- \`tableCollationCache: Record<string, string>\` — table-default collation per table
- \`virtualExpressionCache: Record<string, Record<string, string>>\` — pre-serialized generation expressions (already JSON/inspect-equivalent literals, matching Rails' \`.gsub("\\'", "'").inspect\` output) per table+column

\`connection?: object\` retained as a semantic marker that the adapter has been wired in (not used for method dispatch in this PR).

author: cryptobal
body:
## Resumen

Cambios cruzados en cuatro frentes durante una misma sesión de trabajo. Cada commit es atómico — el PR se puede revisar tema por tema.

---

### 🟢 Onboarding del cliente (modal)

- **`f73bc8a`** — Rediseño del modal con flujo de 2 pasos (formulario → compartir):
  - `ValidationsPanel`, `StepEditor`, `AddCustomTicketForm` y `PlatformConfigPanel` pasan a un look minimalista (cards colapsables, chips de prioridad/equipo, contador `n/total`, alerta inline cuando hay bloqueos).
  - Pantalla final `OnboardingSuccessShare`: hero verde + quick links a deal/tickets/maps + resumen de pendientes + mensaje WhatsApp **editable** con tres acciones (`Copiar`, `Enviar a un grupo`, `Enviar al contacto` — normaliza a +56).
  - Builder `whatsapp-summary.ts`: cliente · instalación · etapa · fecha de inicio · dirección + Google Maps · contacto · dotación (cargo, puesto, días, horario, sueldo líquido del active quote) · pendientes con equipo/prioridad/vencimiento.
  - `/api/onboarding/preview` ahora retorna `primaryContact`, `lat/lng`, `activeQuotationId` y `stageName`.
- **Fix `P2022`** en `ensureDefaultPlaybook`: guard idempotente en SQL puro (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) para entornos donde la migration `20260721000000_add_default_assignee_to_ops_ticket_types` no quedó aplicada.

### 🍞 Toasts apiladas

- **`cf1e9a3`** — `Toaster` global con `expand={true}` ya empujaba las toasts en columna, pero el fondo `opai-liquid-glass` (6% blanco + blur 24 px) las fundía visualmente. Reemplazo por `opai-toast` con fondo sólido (`hsl(var(--card))`) y blur reducido. `gap=12` y `visibleToasts=5` para mejor lectura en cascada.

### 🔐 Permisos del módulo Documentos

- **`0eeec88`** — Antes existía un único submódulo `docs.gestion` que controlaba las tres pestañas. Ahora se divide en tres independientes con sus niveles `view/edit/full`:
  - `gestion` → `/opai/documentos`
  - `operativos` → `/opai/documentos-operativos`
  - `plantillas` → `/opai/documentos/templates`
- **No requiere migración**: los roles existentes con `docs: edit` heredan por cascada los tres submódulos. Solo cambian si el admin marca uno como `none`.
- API guards (`requireDocsView`, `requireDocsEdit`, `requireDocsDelete`) aceptan submódulo opcional. Nuevo `requireDocsViewAny` para recursos compartidos (p. ej., `GET /api/docs/templates` lo necesitan tanto el editor de plantillas como la pantalla de generar documentos).
- `DocumentosSubnav`, `role-nav-builder` y `module-nav` filtran cada item por su submódulo.

### 🎫 Tickets — UX

- **`c21235c`** — Default = vista **Cards** y filtro **"Asignados a mí"**. Persistencia de la última vista elegida en `localStorage` (`ops-tickets-view-mode`).
- **`4c12ace`** — Nuevo filtro **"Asignados a mi equipo"**:
  - `getAssignedTeamsForUser(tenantId, userId)` resuelve las membresías de `AdminGroup` → conjunto de `assignedTeam` a matchear (match directo + mapeo canónico vía `TICKET_TEAM_TO_GROUP_SLUG`).
  - `?assignedTo=my_team` devuelve `assignedTo === me OR assignedTeam IN [equipos]`. Sin grupos → degrada a "asignados a mí".
  - Conteo `myTeam` en `/api/ops/tickets/counts`. Chip "Mi equipo" + opción del dropdown.
- **`4149d9c`** — Fix `P2023` (UUID inválido) cuando un filtro CRM (`dealId`/`accountId`/`contactId`) no resolvía a tickets. El `where.id = "no-match"` rompía con `OpsTicket.id @db.Uuid`. Reemplazo por short-circuit con respuesta vacía.
- **`ec64d7b`** — Coherencia visual prioridad ↔ SLA:
  - Card de instalación con fondo neutro y rail lateral por severidad. Dos micro-barras separadas (Prioridad: P1/P2/P3/P4 · SLA: vencidos vs en plazo).
  - Card de ticket con rail de 4 px usando tokens del DS (`status-danger/warn/info`).
- **`2a21674`** — Toolbar consolidado: 3 filas → 2 (chips arriba; search + filtros + selección + view-toggle abajo). Removí el `h2` interno (la PageHero ya lo dice) y oculto "Por instalación" del view-toggle cuando ya estás drilled-in.
- **`a469df8`** — Tres mejoras finales:
  - **Orden por criticidad** (default): `priority asc → slaBreached desc → slaDueAt asc → createdAt desc`. Dropdown "Más críticos / Más nuevos / SLA por vencer".
  - **Drill-in header**: card secundaria con 📍 + nombre + contadores scoped (activos · P1 · SLA vencidos · sin asignar) en lugar del breadcrumb.
  - **Cards compactas**: 3 filas (título + chips críticos · meta · SLA bar) + filas opcionales solo si aplican (hallazgo / guardia / tags).

---

## Test plan

- [ ] **Onboarding modal**: abrir un deal en estado "won", verificar el rediseño, crear los tickets, validar el mensaje WhatsApp en la pantalla de share (incluye dotación, dirección con Maps, contacto, pendientes).
- [ ] **Migración faltante**: en un tenant donde la migration de `default_assigned_to_user_id` no se aplicó, abrir el modal y confirmar que ya no falla con P2022.
- [ ] **Toasts**: disparar varias toasts seguidas (p. ej., guardar varias acciones) y confirmar que se ven separadas, no fundidas.
- [ ] **Permisos docs**: en `Configuración → Roles y permisos`, confirmar que aparecen 3 filas (`Gestión documental`, `Documentos operativos`, `Plantillas`). Setear `docs.plantillas: none` y confirmar que el botón Templates desaparece del subnav y de la sidebar.
- [ ] **Tickets**: 
  - [ ] Abrir `/ops/tickets` por primera vez (incógnito): default = cards + "Asignados a mí".
  - [ ] Cambiar a list/kanban; recargar: la elección persiste.
  - [ ] Filtrar por "Mi equipo" siendo miembro de un grupo cuyo slug coincida con un `assignedTeam` real → tickets aparecen.
  - [ ] Drill-in: entrar a una instalación desde "Por instalación" → header secundario con counters scoped.
  - [ ] Probar las 3 opciones de orden y validar que P1/SLA vencidos quedan arriba en "Más críticos".
- [ ] **Tickets API**: abrir un deal sin onboarding ni instalación → no más 500 P2023 en `/api/ops/tickets?dealId=…`.

author: subsetpark
body:
## Summary

- **Gameplan complexity**: `/write-gameplan` now requires every patch to carry a `complexity` integer (1/2/3) estimating how hard the patch is to implement correctly. The skill instructs the author to be **conservative** — when in doubt, score higher — and to read the relevant code (and external docs for unfamiliar APIs) before scoring rather than going off the title alone.
- **`--model auto`**: when this flag is passed, each backend resolves the literal `auto` to a backend-specific model based on the patch's complexity. Conservative fallback: missing/out-of-range complexity routes to the strongest tier. Per-backend ladders use current model names (mid-2026):
  - **claude** — `haiku` / `sonnet` / `opus` (stable aliases)
  - **codex** — `gpt-5.4-mini` / `gpt-5.4` / `gpt-5.5`
  - **gemini** — `gemini-2.5-flash` / `gemini-3-flash-preview` / `gemini-3-pro-preview`
  - **opencode** — `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` / `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` / `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`
  - **pi** — no canonical ladder; `auto` falls back to pi's CLI default
- **Refactor**: extracts the 412-line `run_claude_and_handle` (and its helpers `ensure_worktree`, `log_event`, `log_stream_entry`, `extract_pr_number_from_text`, `session_mode`) out of `bin/main.ml` into three new lib modules: `Session_driver`, `Worktree_setup`, `Runtime_logging`. `main.ml` shrinks 4338 → 3934 lines.
- **Naming**: renames `run_claude_and_handle` → `Session_driver.run`, `with_claude_slot` → `with_session_slot`, and rewords comments/CLI docs that referred to "Claude" generically. Remaining `claude` references are all about the Claude backend specifically (dispatch case, display name, `--model` example).

The `model` value flows as `string option` end-to-end, so the literal `"auto"` round-trips cleanly through `Project_store` (resume) and the CLI without a migration.

## Test plan

- [x] `dune build` clean (with strict warnings)
- [x] `dune runtest` — all inline + property tests pass
- [x] `dune fmt` clean
- [x] New unit tests for `Llm_backend.resolve_auto_model` and `Claude_runner.auto_model` cover the conservative fallback and case-insensitive `auto` recognition
- [ ] Smoke-test `--model auto` against a real gameplan with complexity=1/2/3 patches across at least the claude and codex backends
- [ ] Verify `--model auto` round-trips through `onton PROJECT` resume after a fresh `onton --gameplan ... --model auto` start

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Implementa os dois objetivos da Fase 8: ### Objetivo 1 — Multi-Player Selector Tabs **Servidor 1 / Servidor 2** acima do iframe no player view. - **Servidor 1**: Superflixapi (lógica que já tinha) — `?season=S&episode=E`. - **Servidor 2**: WarezCDN — `https://embed.warezcdn.com/filme/{id}` ou `/serie/{id}/{S}/{E}` (path segments, sem query string). - `buildPlayerUrl(server, ...)` é um dispatcher; cada server é um adapter no objeto `SERVERS` (fácil de adicionar Mixdrop/Embedder no futuro). - `setServer()` troca o iframe mantendo o S/E atual. Preferência persistida em `localStorage` (`yverflix:server:preference`) — usuário não precisa re-trocar a cada conteúdo. - Tabs são botões nativos com `role="tab"` + `aria-selected`. Click delegation no `$playerView` (sobrevive a re-renders). ### Objetivo 2 — Persistência "Onde Você Parou" Nova tabela `watch_history` + módulo `HistoryService` + section "Continuar Assistindo". **Migration** (`supabase/migrations/0002_watch_history.sql`): - 1 row por `(user_id, tmdb_id, media_type)` (UNIQUE) — UPSERT atualiza S/E + `updated_at`. - Index `(user_id, updated_at DESC)` cobre o SELECT do "Continuar Assistindo". - RLS permissiva (espelho da 6.2) — refinaremos quando endurecer auth. **HistoryService** (IIFE): - `touch(item, { season, episode, episodeTitle })` — upsert debounced. - `list(limit=10)` — top N por `updated_at desc`. - `invalidate()` — limpa caches no logout/troca de user. **Estratégia anti-spam no banco** (sua pergunta): 1. **Debounce 500ms por chave** (`tmdb_id+media_type`). Cada `touch` reseta o timer; cliques rápidos viram 1 upsert. Chaves diferentes têm timers independentes. 2. **Dedupe semântico** via `sigCache` em memória. Antes de cada flush, comparo `(season, episode)` com o último upsert enviado — se igual, NEM bate no banco. Caso típico: user reabre o mesmo episódio que já é o "current" → 0 round-trips. 3. **Optimistic dispatch** — `dispatchEvent('yverflix:history-changed')` é disparado ANTES do upsert resolver. UI atualiza instantâneo. Se o upsert falhar, libero o `sigCache` pra próxima retry naturalmente. 4. **UPSERT nativo** (single round-trip), com UNIQUE constraint no banco como guardião final. 5. **Last-write-wins via `updated_at`** — robust contra responses fora de ordem (raro mas possível em redes ruins). **Cenário de stress**: user abre 10 episódios em 3s → 1 upsert (debounce). Reabre o E10 5 segundos depois → 0 upserts (dedupe). De ~10 → ~1 round-trip. **ContinueWatching** (IIFE, mesmo padrão do MyList): - Section `#continue-section` ACIMA da Minha Lista. Hidden quando vazio. - Reusa `createCard` (estética idêntica ao grid/Minha Lista) + badge sobreposta `T1 · E03` no canto inf-esq do poster (só séries). - Sync via `CustomEvent('yverflix:history-changed')` — patch incremental: - **Existe** → move pro topo + atualiza badge (zero re-render). - **Não existe** → prepend + trim para max 10 cards (consistente com `list(10)`). - `reload()` é chamado em login/logout (mesmo gate do MyList: `prevUserId !== nextUserId`). ### Deep Linking - Cards de "Continuar Assistindo" carregam `data-autoplay="1"` + `data-resume-season/episode`. - `onCardClick` extrai esses opts e passa pra `ContentModal.open(item, opts)`. - Para **filmes**: `enterPlayerView(null,null)` direto (skip details). - Para **séries**: `DetailsView.mount` recebe `resumeOpts` → `SeriesEpisodes.mount` carrega a temporada salva (não S1) e auto-aciva o episódio marcado uma única vez (`resumeConsumed` evita re-fire em troca de temporada). ### ⚠️ Pré-requisito Antes de testar em produção, rode o conteúdo de [`supabase/migrations/0002_watch_history.sql`](https://github.com/ClayverViegas/YverFlix/blob/devin/1777923041-fase-8-multiplayer-history/supabase/migrations/0002_watch_history.sql) no [SQL Editor do Supabase](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/oxgibqccznmysncubkct/sql/new). Sem isso, todos os upserts batem em PGRST205 (tabela inexistente) e a section "Continuar Assistindo" fica sempre hidden. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Rodar a migration `0002_watch_history.sql`** no SQL Editor do Supabase (caminho linkado acima). - [ ] Click num conteúdo → entrar no player → verificar que aparece a section "Continuar Assistindo" no topo da home após F5. - [ ] Trocar de Servidor 1 → 2 num episódio → confirmar que o iframe re-carrega e a URL agora aponta pra `embed.warezcdn.com/serie/.../S/E` (DevTools → Network). - [ ] Click num card de série em "Continuar Assistindo" → modal abre, S/E correto fica destacado e player auto-toca o episódio salvo. - [ ] Stress: clicar em 5+ episódios rapidamente → checar logs (`[History]`) — só 1 upsert deve sair (debounce). Reabrir o último → 0 upserts (dedupe). ### Notes - Migration é idempotente (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS`) — pode rodar múltiplas vezes sem erro. - Server 2 (WarezCDN) também não tem todos os conteúdos — é normal o user trocar e o vídeo não aparecer pra alguns títulos. O selector dá o controle pra ele escolher. - HistoryService.touch é chamado em TODA entrada no player, mas o dedupe garante que reabrir o mesmo episódio (sem trocar S/E) NÃO gera upsert. - `state.currentEpisodeTitle` é capturado do cache local do SeriesEpisodes (não exige fetch extra). Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e5e72928da754ab8ac62bfb34a3eefb7 Requested by: @ClayverViegas ---

author: lokimetasmith
body:
The `monitoring` playbook was failing with a timeout error during the `Wait for MQTT service to be healthy in Consul` task. The reason is that Ansible was synchronously waiting for the `mqtt` service to be fully passing its Consul health checks before deploying the `mqtt-exporter` Nomad job.

This fix removes these explicit `ansible.builtin.uri` and `ansible.builtin.wait_for` waits. Instead, it delegates the retry and wait logic to Nomad natively, allowing it to restart the `mqtt-exporter` if `mqtt` is not yet ready, avoiding blocking the entire Ansible bootstrapping pipeline.

author: dougborg
body:
/simplify pass over PRs #492 / #493 / #496. Three cleanups, **net −63 lines**, no behavior change.

## What

1. **Drop dead \`state.result\`.** \`SetState(\"result\", RESULT)\` was added to every Confirm button's \`on_success\` chain in #496, paired with \`\"result\": None\` seeds in four \`PrefabApp\` state dicts — forward-compat for an iframe-side render that doesn't exist (no UI component reads \`state.result\` anywhere). YAGNI. Removed.

2. **Push None-handling into \`_build_confirm_action\`.** The xor-check \`(confirm_request is None) != (confirm_tool is None)\` and the conditional \`if confirm_request is not None and confirm_tool is not None: ...\` block were duplicated verbatim in \`build_receipt_ui\` and \`build_batch_recipe_update_ui\`. The helper now accepts \`Optional\` inputs and returns \`Optional[CallTool]\` (both None → None, exactly one None → ValueError). Both call sites collapse to a single delegate.

3. **Route \`build_fulfill_preview_ui\` through \`_build_confirm_action\`.** It was hand-building 30 lines of \`CallTool\` + \`on_success\`/\`on_error\` handlers exactly duplicating what #496 centralized. The justifying comment said \"args aren't a Pydantic request, they're echoed from the response dict\" — but \`FulfillOrderRequest\` is trivially constructible from \`response[\"order_id\"]\` + \`response[\"order_type\"]\`. Eliminates the duplication and the \"confession comment\".

Also trimmed narrative \`History:\` paragraphs and \"Regression for #491\" comments where they explained WHAT (visible in the code) or duplicated rationale already in the helper docstring. Kept the DataTable boundary comment in \`build_search_results_ui\` — it documents a real invariant about a different substitution mechanism (#494).

## Findings considered but skipped

The /simplify reviewers flagged a few more items that I judged not worth the API churn:

- **\`ConfirmAction(tool, request)\` dataclass replacing the kwarg pair** — modest cleanup at significant API churn cost; current pair-with-helper-validation is fine.
- **\`Literal[tool_names]\` for \`confirm_tool: str\`** — type maintenance burden each time a write tool is added; tests already pin the names.
- **Parametrize the 4 feedback-handler tests** — they read better as 4 independent tests that name the builder under test in the function name.
- **Generic tree walker replacing the 3 in tests** — three walkers with subtly different return semantics; aesthetic consolidation only.
- **\`overrides\` parameter on \`call_tool_from_request\`** — only one caller currently uses it (\`{\"preview\": False}\`), but the validation guard is small and keeping it preserves an extension point.

## Test plan

- [x] \`uv run poe agent-check\` — clean
- [x] \`uv run poe test\` — full MCP suite, 704 passed
- [x] \`grep -n state.result\` and \`grep -n SetState..result\` — no remaining dead-state references

body:
## Summary
- Catch only `KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException` in `MainDataModule.provideEncryptedSharedPrefs`. Transient `GeneralSecurityException`/`IOException` from cold-launch keystore stalls now propagate to Hilt and Crashlytics instead of silently destroying `shared_prefs/token_secure_prefs.xml` and the `vultisig_secure_prefs_key` alias.
- Drop the second-tier `InMemorySharedPreferences` fallback so a still-broken keystore surfaces as a real failure rather than a non-persistent store that loses every write at process death.
- Specialize `recoverAndRetry` to `KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException` (future widening is now a compile error). Demote recovery log from `Timber.e` to `Timber.w` and name the trigger. Pin file-then-alias delete order so a partial recovery leaves no readable ciphertext for the next launch.
- Extract `SecurePrefsRecoveryPolicy.shouldDestructivelyRecover(Throwable)` covered by 8 JUnit 5 cases (KPIE → true; GSE, IOException, InvalidKeyException, UnrecoverableKeyException, IllegalStateException, RuntimeException, KPIE-as-`cause` → false). Drop now-unused imports.

Closes #4401

## Deferred
- OEM-wrapped KPIE (Samsung/Xiaomi/Huawei nest KPIE inside `IllegalStateException`/`KeyStoreException`): policy intentionally does not unwrap `cause` — revisit when Crashlytics signal justifies it.
- `InMemorySharedPreferences` in `SecureSharedPreferences.kt` is orphaned; separate cleanup PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :data:testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.vultisig.wallet.data.utils.SecurePrefsRecoveryPolicyTest"` (8/8 pass)
- [x] `./gradlew :data:compileDebugKotlin` clean

author: roadhero
body:
## Summary

The npm-on-Windows install in \`build-electron.yml\` is intentional — pnpm's content-addressed store puts deps under \`node_modules/.pnpm/<name>@<ver>_<longhash>/...\` which blows past Windows MAX_PATH (260) for makensis.exe's NSIS include resolver. The team already tried \`--shamefully-hoist\` (4510cc5) and still got unreachable include paths.

This PR adds an inline comment so the next person who looks at the divergence doesn't try to "fix" it back to pnpm and break Windows installer builds. No behavior change.

## Why not switch to pnpm

#42's first acceptance bullet asks whether \`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\` runs successfully on \`windows-latest\`. It does — pnpm/action-setup@v3 works on Windows fine, and the install itself completes. The problem surfaces later, in the \`pnpm build\` step (\`electron-builder\`), when makensis can't open NSIS includes from the deeply-hashed pnpm store paths. So the install command's exit code is misleading; the load-bearing constraint is downstream.

## Test plan

- [x] Documentation-only change — Windows / macOS smoke jobs should still pass with no behavior change
- [ ] If Windows MAX_PATH ever stops being a constraint (e.g. long-paths enabled by default in a future runner image), revisit and consolidate to pnpm

Closes #42 by documenting the reason inline (per the issue's third acceptance bullet).

author: scottyzen
body:
# Pluginize payment gateways

## Summary
This PR refactors checkout payment handling into a gateway plugin system so each provider owns its UI/state/payment logic, while checkout coordinates selection and order submission.

## What Changed
1. Added a payment gateway plugin architecture and shared gateway lifecycle APIs (register, select, readiness, reset, process payment).
2. Moved gateway-specific logic out of checkout into provider plugins:
   1. Stripe plugin (Payment Element, saved cards, intent/metadata handling).
   2. PayPal/PPCP plugin registration.
   3. COD and Cheque plugin registration.
3. Added reusable payment rendering pieces:
   1. Gateway component host for provider-specific UI.
   2. Updated payment options UI to use plugin-provided icons and behavior.
4. Simplified checkout page responsibilities:
   1. Select active gateway.
   2. Validate readiness.
   3. Delegate payment processing.
   4. Continue with checkout submission.
5. Added Vue type shim support for plugin-based .vue imports used in TS plugin files.

## Why
1. Reduces checkout complexity and coupling.
2. Makes adding new gateways straightforward without editing core checkout logic.
3. Improves maintainability and testability by isolating provider behavior.

## Validation
1. Typecheck run for the base layer.
2. Manual checkout-path verification for Stripe/non-Stripe flows after pluginization.
3. Confirmed branch upstream/tracking issues were handled separately and are not part of this code behavior change.

author: rinaldodev
body:
## Description

Jira: [RHOAIENG-58945](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHOAIENG-58945)

Adds `MonitorOperator` to the precondition framework and migrates all `dependency.NewAction` consumers to `WithPreCondition`. Dependency monitoring now runs before reconciler actions instead of mid-pipeline.

### MonitorOperator

`MonitorOperator(config OperatorConfig, opts ...Option)` fetches an external operator CR, applies a caller-provided `ConditionFilterFunc` to its status conditions, and reports unhealthy ones.

Missing CRD always passes (operator not installed). Missing CR behavior is controlled by `OperatorConfig.RequireCR`: false (default) passes, true reports failure.

### Migrated components

KServe, Kueue, and Trainer migrated from `dependency.NewAction` to `WithPreCondition`. CRName pinned to the canonical singleton in Kueue and Trainer. `action_operator.go` deleted (no remaining consumers). The `dependency` package survives for subscription monitoring (RHOAIENG-58946).

### Behavioral changes

- Condition reason: `DependencyDegraded` → `PreConditionFailed`
- Message prefix `"Dependencies degraded: ..."` removed. Detailed condition info preserved.
- API errors surface as `ConditionUnknown` instead of being silently treated as healthy.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Unit tests pass for all affected packages. Lint clean.

CRD dependency monitoring tests rewritten as envtest-based integration tests through the real kserve controller (`kserve_controller_dependency_test.go`).

| # | Input | Path exercised |
|---|-------|----------------|
| 65 | `DELIMITER "$$"` | `DelimiterDoubleQuote → EOF` |
| 66 | `DELIMITER ''` | empty single-quoted → `DelimiterContinues → EOF` |
| 67 | `DELIMITER ""` | empty double-quoted → `DelimiterContinues → EOF` |
| 68 | `DELIMITER '$$'   ` | quoted + trailing whitespace → `DelimiterContinues → EOF` |
| 69 | `DELIMITER '$$' extra` | quoted + trailing text → `DelimiterIgnoring → EOF` |
| 70 | `DELIMITER "$$" extra` | double-quoted + trailing text → `DelimiterIgnoring → EOF` |

author: nntin
body:
The agent pipeline was fixed to stop being a hardcoded `agent → evaluator → optimizer` loop. Workflows are now defined per request, edited visually in the UI, and executed by a dynamic backend runner without requiring server changes or restarts.

- **Shared stream/workflow contract**
  - Add `WorkflowNodeConfig`, `WorkflowEdgeConfig`, and `WorkflowDefinition` to shared types.
  - Extend `StreamRequest` with optional `workflow`.
  - Widen `model_input.source` and `thinking.source` from fixed literals to arbitrary strings.
  - Add `routing` trace events and bump the stream schema to `1.7.0`.

- **Backend dynamic execution path**
  - Add `apps/backend/app/graph/dynamic_executor.py` to validate and execute arbitrary directed workflows.
  - Implement per-node execution with:
    - node-specific system prompt
    - node-specific tool allowlist
    - context assembly from user input and prior node outputs
    - inner tool-call loop until final node output
  - Implement LLM-based edge routing for nodes with multiple outgoing edges.
  - Keep `/stream` backward-compatible by dispatching to the existing LangGraph path when no workflow is provided.

- **Backend trace/event model**
  - Update backend stream event schemas for arbitrary node names.
  - Add `RoutingEvent` / `RoutingEdgeOption` so routing decisions show up in trace replay and live streaming.
  - Reuse existing stream emission infrastructure so dynamic workflows produce the same observable event model as the legacy path.

- **Frontend workflow authoring**
  - Replace global agent tool configuration with workflow state in the store.
  - Add a full-screen workflow editor modal using React Flow (`@xyflow/react`).
  - Add:
    - configurable LLM nodes
    - fixed `End` node
    - inline edge label editing
    - entry-node selection
    - per-node tools and context sources
    - reset-to-default workflow

- **Frontend runtime integration**
  - Send `workflow` in stream requests instead of `tool_config`.
  - Update chat controls to surface workflow configuration and a compact workflow summary.
  - Update trace rendering to display arbitrary node sources directly and render routing decisions.

- **Docs and compatibility**
  - Update architecture docs to describe the new dynamic execution path.
  - Preserve legacy session replay behavior by continuing to render historic `agent` / `evaluator` / `optimizer` sources correctly.

Example request shape now sent by the frontend:

```ts
const request: StreamRequest = {
  input: "Solve this and grade the answer",
  ollama_backend_id: selectedBackend,
  model: selectedModel,
  workflow: {
    nodes: [
      {
        id: "node-agent",
        name: "Agent",
        systemPrompt: "...",
        tools: ["add", "multiply"],
        contextSources: ["user_input"],
        isEntry: true,
        position: { x: 200, y: 150 },
      },
      {
        id: "node-grader",
        name: "Grader",
        systemPrompt: "...",
        tools: [],
        contextSources: ["user_input", "node-agent"],
        isEntry: false,
        position: { x: 480, y: 150 },
      },
    ],
    edges: [
      { id: "e1", source: "node-agent", target: "node-grader", label: "always" },
      { id: "e2", source: "node-grader", target: "END", label: "done" },
    ],
  },
};
```

## Summary
Complete visual and structural redesign of the portfolio website with a new dark theme, simplified typography system, and interactive mockup carousel component. Removed i18n complexity and refactored components for a cleaner, more modern aesthetic.

### Design & Styling
- **New color system**: Replaced complex Tailwind theme with simplified CSS variables (`--bg`, `--ink`, `--accent`, `--rule`) for a dark-first design
- **Typography overhaul**: Switched from Bricolage Grotesque + Newsreader to Fraunces (serif) + Inter (sans-serif) with JetBrains Mono for code
- **Layout primitives**: Added utility classes (`.wrap`, `.grid12`, `.mono`, `.eyebrow`, `.rule`) for consistent spacing and typography

- **Header redesign**: Simplified navigation with numbered links, Lisbon timezone clock, and language toggle

- **New Mockups section**: Added interactive carousel component (`Mockups.tsx`) with touch swipe support, keyboard navigation, and lightbox integration for project screenshots
- **Projects section**: Simplified data structure, removed i18n, cleaner card layout
- **Skills section**: Converted to simpler card-based layout with percentage bars
- **Experience section**: Removed timeline component, simplified role display
- **About section**: Added portrait image, restructured layout with new grid system
- **Testimonials**: Simplified quote display with initials and role
- **Contact section**: Streamlined contact information display

### Infrastructure
- **Removed i18n**: Eliminated translation system and language switching complexity
- **Removed Container component**: Replaced with `.wrap` utility class

- **Removed legacy components**: Typewriter, Timeline, and other complex UI components

- Added 17 mockup images for Padel app and Daillo iOS app showcase

- Interactive carousel uses refs and transform-based positioning for smooth centering

body:
## Summary

Closes #827 (parent epic #825).

A franchised Sovereign now supports **N parent zones**, NOT one. The operator brings 1+ parent domains at signup (`omani.works` for own use, `omani.trade` for the SME pool, etc.) and may add more post-handover via the admin console (#829, already merged).

## Changes

### A. PowerDNS multi-zone bootstrap (bp-powerdns 1.2.0)
- New `zones: []` values key
- New `templates/zone-bootstrap-job.yaml` — Helm post-install/post-upgrade hook Job that POSTs each zone to `/api/v1/servers/localhost/zones`. Idempotent on HTTP 409.
- Default empty zones renders zero resources (legacy paths unaffected).

### B. cert-manager per-zone wildcard (bp-catalyst-platform 1.4.0)
- New `parentZones: []` + `wildcardCert.{enabled,namespace,issuerName}` values
- New `templates/sovereign-wildcard-certs.yaml` — renders one `cert-manager.io/v1.Certificate` per zone (each `*.<zone>` + apex) via the `letsencrypt-dns01-prod-powerdns` ClusterIssuer
- Each cert renews independently; a stalled DNS-01 challenge on one zone never blocks another
- Skips render entirely when `parentZones` is empty so the legacy `clusters/_template/sovereign-tls/cilium-gateway-cert.yaml` keeps ownership of `sovereign-wildcard-tls` (no helm-vs-kustomize ownership flap)

### C. catalyst-api runtime add-zone integration
- New `internal/powerdns` package with typed `Client.CreateZone` / `ZoneExists` (idempotent on 409/412)
- `handler.pdmCreatePowerDNSZone` (issue #829's stub) now uses the typed client when wired via `SetPowerDNSZoneClient`. The admin-console "Add another parent domain" flow now creates real zones in the Sovereign's PowerDNS at runtime.
- Falls back to the legacy `CATALYST_PDM_ZONES_ENABLED` path so contabo + CI installs stay green.

### D. Bootstrap-kit slot integration
- `clusters/_template/bootstrap-kit/11-powerdns.yaml`: bumps to bp-powerdns 1.2.0 and threads `zones: ${PARENT_DOMAINS_YAML}` from Flux `postBuild.substitute`
- `clusters/_template/bootstrap-kit/13-bp-catalyst-platform.yaml`: bumps to bp-catalyst-platform 1.4.0 and threads `parentZones: ${PARENT_DOMAINS_YAML}` (same source string — the two slots stay in lockstep)
- New `parent_domains_yaml` Terraform variable defaulting to a single-zone array derived from `sovereign_fqdn`

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] Unit tests: `internal/powerdns` — 11 cases (201/409/412/500 + custom NS + custom serverID + ZoneExists 200/404)
- [x] Unit tests: `internal/handler` — `parent_domains_test.go` continues to pass
- [x] Helm template render: 2-zone overlay (`omani.works` + `omani.trade`) renders 2 PowerDNS zone-create API calls in the Job AND 2 `Certificate` resources
- [x] Helm template render: empty `parentZones` skips Certificate render entirely (no conflict with legacy cert)
- [x] envsubst end-to-end: `PARENT_DOMAINS_YAML='[{name: "omani.works", role: "primary"}, {name: "omani.trade", role: "sme-pool"}]'` substitutes correctly into both bootstrap-kit slots and parses as valid YAML

## Notes

- Pre-existing CI test failures unrelated to this change: `internal/provisioner` (Harbor robot token validation) and `internal/handler/TestAuthHandover_HappyPath` (handover_jwt nil pointer). Confirmed by stashing my changes and running the same tests against `main` HEAD.

## Summary
- add a same-machine local append-only bus for gh room ids at ~/.airc/bus/gh/<room_gist_id>/messages.jsonl
- GhBearer.send writes the signed envelope to the local bus before attempting GitHub, and reports delivered for local agents when GitHub is transient/auth/rate limited
- GhBearer.recv_stream polls the local bus alongside the gist and dedupes identical lines when both paths eventually contain the same message

## Why
GitHub/gist is still useful as rendezvous/control, but it cannot be the only hot message path. Today we had active gh API 403 secondary-rate-limit failures while local agents on the same machine still needed to collaborate.

## Live validation
While gh GET/PATCH for c68640ec0144b422c16b2d8c83ad5ee5 was returning HTTP 403 rate-limit errors:
- continuum sent marker localbus-continuum-to-auth-1777923537
- marker appeared in ~/.airc/bus/gh/c68640ec0144b422c16b2d8c83ad5ee5/messages.jsonl
- authenticator received and mirrored it to /Users/joelteply/Development/ideem/authenticator/.airc/messages.jsonl
- authenticator ACKed; ACK appeared in continuum local log and same local bus

## Tests
- python3 test/test_bearer.py GhBearerLocalBusTests GhBearerSendTests GhBearerRecvTests GhBearerErrorClassificationTests
- python3 test/test_bearer.py
- python3 -m py_compile lib/airc_core/bearer_gh.py test/test_bearer.py

## Scope
This is a same-user/same-machine data-plane fallback. It does not solve LAN or cross-machine transport yet, but it stops local agents from being stranded by GitHub rate limits.

### Motivation
- Prevent blind immediate application of the AI background remover by prompting the user to choose the target scope first.  
- Preserve all existing selection, chapter, thumbnail, Analyze & Align, export/atlas and background-removal algorithm behavior while surfacing an explicit scope chooser.  

### Description
- Intercept the existing `handleRemoveBackground` click to open a scope chooser dialog instead of starting processing immediately by setting `isBgScopeDialogOpen` and rendering a `Dialog` with `Cancel`.  
- Extract the existing immediate-processing logic into `processBackgroundRemoval(targetIds: string[])` and reuse the same `removalState` progress updates and frame mutation logic so progress UI remains unchanged.  
- Add two helper scope builders: `getCurrentChapterScope()` (first chapter that contains `focusedFrameId`) and `getCheckedChapterScopeIds()` (chapter-order-preserving, de-duplicated list of frame ids from `checkedChapterIds`).  
- Add `handleRemoveBackgroundWithScope(scope)` which maps the chosen scope to frame ids for: `current-frame` (`focusedFrameId`), `current-chapter` (first matching chapter), `checked-chapters` (ordered unique frames from checked chapters), and `all-frames` (`frames.map(f => f.id)`), then calls `processBackgroundRemoval`.  
- Import and use UI primitives `Dialog` and `Button` and conditionally show/disable scope options based on availability (focused frame, chapters, checked chapters, frames).  
- Keep all preserved behaviors intact: selection logic, chapter creation, All Frames behavior, thumbnail visuals, Analyze & Align, export/atlas logic, and the background removal algorithm itself.

Cierra el módulo de **inversiones**. Todos los documentos de la categoría están registrados, vinculados a sus campos en BD, con templates `.docx` listos y **probados generándose correctamente end-to-end** (template → render → PDF → firma vía Documenso).

### Documentos completados

| # | Tipo | Plantillas | Estado |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Acuerdo de Inversión Cash In | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 2 | Anexo 1 - Carta de Confirmación de Inversión Inicial | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 3 | Anexo 2 - Carta de Elección de Modalidad de Pago y Reinversión | hombre | ✅ |
| 4 | Anexo 3 - Carta de Instrucción para Inversión en Cartera Activa | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 5 | Anexo 4 - Carta de Incremento de Inversión | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 6 | Anexo 6 - Carta de Instrucción por Pago Anticipado | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 7 | Cesión de Créditos | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 8 | Contrato de Servicios Cash In - Inversor General | hombre / mujer | ✅ |
| 9 | Anexo 7 - Designación de Beneficiarios | único | ✅ |

### Cambios incluidos

- **`types/contract.ts`** — 5 nuevos `ContractType` (CARTA_INSTRUCCION_INVERSION_CARTERA_ACTIVA, CARTA_INCREMENTO_INVERSION, CARTA_INSTRUCCION_PAGO_ANTICIPADO, CONTRATO_SERVICIOS_CASH_IN_INVERSOR_GENERAL, DESIGNACION_BENEFICIARIO).
- **`ContractGeneratorService.ts`** — registros de los 5 templates con su path hombre/mujer.
- **`docusealConfig.ts`** — signer config (1 firmante "Inversionista" en cada uno; "Cedente" para cesión).
- **`signaturePatterns.ts`** — patrones para localizar la línea de firma en el PDF.
- **Anexo 7 (Designación de Beneficiarios)**: la tabla de beneficiarios fue re-armada para usar el loop nativo de docxtemplater (`{#listaBeneficiarios}...{/listaBeneficiarios}` envolviendo la fila de datos), de modo que se replique automáticamente por cada beneficiario.
- **Backend schema** — `designacion_beneficiario` agregado al `documentNameEnum` para mantener simetría con la BD.

### Notas
- `package.json` y `docker-compose.yml` quedaron afuera (ajustes locales no relacionados).
- Anexo 2 mujer todavía apunta al template de hombre (pendiente recibir variante femenina).
- Patrones de firma para los nuevos docs son placeholders ajustables si la firma queda mal posicionada en algún caso particular.

## Test plan
- [x] Generar cada uno de los 9 documentos en hombre y mujer (donde aplica).
- [x] Verificar que `listaCreditos` (cesión) y `listaBeneficiarios` (Anexo 7) replican correctamente las filas/bullets por cada item enviado.
- [x] Confirmar que los selects con opciones (modalidad, modalidadPagos, instruyeACube, formaEntrega) marcan el checkbox correcto vía la convención `<key>_<optionvalue>` con ☒/☐.
- [x] Endpoint `/docuSeal/documents?categoria=inversiones` lista los 9 documentos.

author: zkochan
body:
## Summary

- Stop adding freshly-resolved **transitive** packages to `ctx.updatedSet` in `resolveDependencies` (recursive). The set is meant to drive transitive dedupe of **user-requested** updates (the original goal of #3877), but populating it from any depth caused unrelated transitive references to flip to the newly resolved version whenever a different importer dep happened to introduce a new version of the same package.
- The flag is now only set at importer level (`currentDepth === 0`), which preserves the explicit-upgrade dedupe behavior while leaving valid transitive resolutions untouched.

Closes #11456.

## Test plan

- [x] Added a regression test in `installing/deps-installer/test/install/dedupe.ts` covering the scenario where adding an unrelated direct dep should not flip an existing transitive resolution.
- [x] All 11 dedupe tests pass.
- [x] Reproduced the original issue against the pnpm monorepo before the fix; with the fix applied, `pnpm install` no longer flips `wide-align@1.1.5`'s `string-width` from `1.0.2` to `4.2.3` when an unrelated workspace package is added.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Reduced lockfile churn by preventing unnecessary re-resolution of transitive dependencies when adding unrelated new dependencies. Existing locked transitive resolutions that still satisfy requested ranges are preserved, so adding new top-level packages no longer flips unrelated transitive versions and produces a cleaner, more stable lockfile.

author: mikan95
body:
Closes #235 

## Checklist

- [x] Target branch is `dev`
- [x] No `.env` or sensitive files committed

## What was done

### **File Changes:**
- Deleted `.env.example`, replaced by `.env.dev.example` and `.env.prod.example`
- Updated `.gitignore` to track the two new example files instead of `.env.example`
- Removed dead `JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET}` env var from `compose.dev.yaml` backend service

### **Make Setup:**
- Rewrote `make/setup.mk`: 
  - `_setup-apply` now generates both `.env.dev` and `.env.prod` from their respective examples
  - Added `_domain-dev` and `_domain-prod` targets for per-stack DOMAIN prompts
  - Removed `DEV_ONLY_ENV_VARS` (Obsolete as `BACKEND_PW`, `JWT_SECRET` are Docker secrets in both stacks)
  - Updated `REQUIRED_FILES` to require `.env.dev` and `.env.prod` instead of `.env`

### **Infra & Makefile:**

- Changed `Makefile` include from `-include .env` to `-include .env.dev`
- Added `ENV_DEV` and `ENV_PROD` variables and applied `--env-file` to every `docker compose` invocation in `Makefile` and `make/clean.mk`

### **Make Swagger:**
- Rewrote `swagger` target to grep `DOMAIN` from each env file independently


### **Behaviour Change:**

- `make setup` prompt now defaults to **yes** on empty input (`[Y/n]` instead of `[y/N]`) — pressing Enter proceeds with setup rather than cancelling it
- The **dev** and **prod** stacks now each run on different dotenv files. This allows devs to define different behaviour for each stack. 
  - **For example:**  
  Running **dev** on localhost (127.0.0.1) and **prod** on Local LAN (168.192.x.x).

## Why

A single `.env` shared between dev and prod required manually editing `DOMAIN` and re-running setup before every prod deployment. Splitting into `.env.dev` and `.env.prod` lets `make setup` configure both stacks in one pass and eliminates the risk of accidentally deploying with dev values. Each `docker compose` invocation now explicitly loads the correct file, removing reliance on Make's `export` to implicitly pass variables to Docker Compose.

## Testing

### Prod Test 1 — Fresh setup and prod stack start

**1. Full wipe and setup:**

```bash
make nuke
make setup
```

> Answer `n` to both DOMAIN prompts to use `127.0.0.1` defaults.

**2. Confirm both env files were created and both DOMAIN are set to whatever you did during the setup prompt:**

```bash
ls .env.dev .env.prod
grep DOMAIN .env.dev .env.prod
```

**3. Start the prod stack:**

```bash
make prod
```

**4. Confirm the stack is healthy:**

```bash
make ps
```

**5. As an extra measure verify URLs in `.env.prod` are all `https` and use port `8443`:**

```bash
grep -E \
"FORTYTWO_REDIRECT_URI|FRONTEND_OAUTH_SUCCESS_URL|VITE_OAUTH_42_START_URL|TWO_FACTOR_URL" \
.env.prod
```

---

### Dev Test 1 — Dev stack after nuke

**1. Remove some Required files to 'simulate a nuke':**

```bash
rm .env.dev .env.prod
```

**2. build the dev stack:**

```bash
make up
```

> `_check-required-files` must trigger `_setup-apply` automatically. Both env files and all secrets must be created before the stack starts. (you will have to go through the prompting again).

**3. Confirm stack is healthy:**

```bash
make ps
```

**4. As an extra measure verify URLs in `.env.dev` are all `http` and use port `1024`:**

```bash
grep -E \
"FORTYTWO_REDIRECT_URI|FRONTEND_OAUTH_SUCCESS_URL|VITE_OAUTH_42_START_URL|TWO_FACTOR_URL" \
.env.dev
```

---

### Swagger Test — Swagger reads correct DOMAINs

**1. Run `_setup-apply` and set domains to different IPs:**

```bash
make _setup-apply
```

> Set dev to Local LAN and prod to localhost or vice versa

**2. Check both DOMAIN are different:**

```bash
Automatically setup DOMAIN? [Y/n]
[DEV]  Set DOMAIN to local LAN? [Y/n]
       Using custom DOMAIN: '192.168.1.67' <---- This should be different to PROD domain

[PROD] Set DOMAIN to local LAN? [Y/n] no
       Using default DOMAIN: '127.0.0.1' <---- This should be different to DEV domain
```
> Or run the command below:

```bash
grep DOMAIN .env.dev .env.prod
```

**3. Run swagger:**

```bash
make swagger
```

> Dev URL must match `DOMAIN` in `.env.dev`, prod URL must match `DOMAIN` in `.env.prod`.

body:
## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why? -->

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Documentation / config only

---

## Security Checklist

> Complete this section for any PR that touches signaling or token paths:
> `domain/jwt.rs`, `domain/livekit_bridge.rs`, `domain/relay.rs`,
> `domain/sfu_relay.rs`, `handlers/ws.rs`

If this PR does **not** touch any of those files, check this box and skip the rest:
- [ ] This PR does not touch signaling or token paths — checklist not applicable

Otherwise, confirm each item below:

### Sensitive Data Logging (Req 5.1–5.4)
- [ ] No JWT strings, raw tokens, or MediaToken values are passed to log macros
- [ ] No invite code values are passed to log macros (lengths/counts are OK)
- [ ] No SDP content is passed to log macros (lengths/types are OK)
- [ ] No ICE candidate strings are passed to log macros (counts/types are OK)
- [ ] `cargo test --test no_sensitive_logs` passes locally (also enforced by CI: `backend-ci.yml`)

### Message Size Limits (Req 3.5, 3.8)
- [ ] SDP payloads are validated against `MAX_SDP_BYTES` (64 KB) before forwarding
- [ ] ICE candidate payloads are validated against `MAX_ICE_CANDIDATE_BYTES` (2 KB) before forwarding
- [ ] Oversized payloads return a descriptive error and are not forwarded

### Server-Enforced Identity (Req 2.3, 2.4)
- [ ] All post-join message dispatch uses `session.participant_id` as sender identity
- [ ] No client-supplied identity fields are trusted for routing or authorization

### Domain-Enforced Action Authorization (Req 3.1, 3.2, 3.6)
- [ ] Action messages (kick, mute) are rejected in P2P rooms
- [ ] Host-only actions check `session.role == Host` in the handler (Tier 1)
- [ ] Domain functions (`handle_kick`, etc.) independently validate role (Tier 2 / defense in depth)
- [ ] Action messages are never forwarded through the relay path

### Token Scope and Lifetime (Req 1.1–1.7)
- [ ] MediaTokens include `iss` and `aud` claims
- [ ] Token TTL is ≤ 600s (default) — no unbounded lifetimes
- [ ] `validate_media_token` checks both `iss` and `aud`
- [ ] Revoked participants are blocked from token re-issuance within the TTL window

---

## Tests

- [ ] `cargo test -p wavis-backend` passes
- [ ] New property tests added for any new correctness properties
- [ ] No tests were deleted or disabled to make the build pass

Automated promotion of `staging` (`1282c1c8`) to `main`. All required staging gates green at this SHA: CI, E2E Staging Canvas, E2E API Smoke, CodeQL.

This PR is auto-generated by `.github/workflows/auto-promote-staging.yml` whenever every required gate completes green on the same staging SHA. It exists because main's branch protection requires status checks "set by the expected GitHub apps" — direct `git push` from a workflow can't satisfy that, only PR merges through the queue can.

Merge queue lands this; no human action needed unless gates fail. Reverse-direction sync (the merge commit on main → staging) is handled by `auto-sync-main-to-staging.yml`.

author: cybertecharmor
body:
…tent installer

The installer generated random LIVEKIT_API_KEY/SECRET for meet-api but never passed them to the livekit container, which was still loading the hardcoded `keys: devkey: secret` block from livekit.yaml. Login worked (no LiveKit involved) so the breakage was invisible until the admin panel opened and every /api/rooms call hit
"Unauthorized: invalid API key". Re-running install.sh would also regenerate one side without the other, drifting the pair further.

Fix the auth path:

  - install.sh now reuses LIVEKIT_API_KEY / LIVEKIT_API_SECRET from an existing .env on rerun (idempotent), and writes a third var LIVEKIT_KEYS=<key>: <secret> into the same .env.
  - docker-compose.yml passes LIVEKIT_KEYS through to the livekit container's environment. LiveKit treats LIVEKIT_KEYS as an override of the keys: block in livekit.yaml, so meet-api and livekit now load the same pair from a single .env field.
  - livekit.yaml keeps the devkey/secret stub but documents that the env override wins.
  - .env.example documents the three vars and their interlock.

Add diagnostics so the next operator catches this in seconds:

  - info.sh gains a LiveKit auth probe that calls RoomServiceClient.listRooms() from inside the meet-api container using the EXACT credentials it has, then categorises the result:
      OK              -> auth ✓
      "invalid API key"           -> KEY MISMATCH (with which key meet-api thinks it has)
      "signature is invalid"       -> SECRET MISMATCH
      ECONNREFUSED / timeout       -> livekit unreachable
  - info.sh's bridge-IP detection now skips docker0/br-*/veth*/cni*/
    lxcbr*/virbr*/tun*/tap*. The previous logic returned 172.18.0.1
    (the Docker network gateway inside the LXC), which the host
    Caddy can't reach — operators kept pasting it into ProxyPilot
    and getting timeouts. Now returns the LXC's external interface
    (e.g. 10.185.17.131).
  - Strip-prefix section reorganised to lead with the rule
    ("only /livekit/* strips") and then the failure modes, instead
    of the other way around.
  - Common-pitfalls section calls out 5355 (mDNS/LLMNR on the LXC,
    not a MEET port) more emphatically and adds a "don't hand-edit
    the LiveKit auth vars" rule.
  - New "Compose handles" section spells out container-name format
    (external-proxy-<service>-1) and the -p flag for outside-dir use.

docs/install/external-reverse-proxy.md gains a matching troubleshooting row for the "Login works but Disconnected" symptom, rewrites the strip-prefix paragraph to make /livekit/* the special case (not the general rule), and documents the compose service-name convention.

author: garthdb
body:
## Description

The `s2-docs` plugin's CLI (`bin/s2-docs.js`) crashed on first use with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: commander` after install via `/plugin marketplace add adobe/spectrum-design-data` + `/plugin install s2-docs@spectrum-design-data` (PR #834 fix).

**Root cause:** Per Anthropic's [plugins reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#persistent-data-directory), Claude Code does **not** run `npm install` for a plugin's `dependencies` — the cache contains only the files declared in `package.json#files`, no `node_modules/`. The documented escape hatch for plugins that need runtime deps is a `SessionStart` hook that installs them into `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/`. I confirmed this experimentally: I tried switching the marketplace `source` from a relative path to an `npm` source first, but neither variant produces a `node_modules/` in the cache.

**Fix:** Drop the only runtime dep on the plugin's CLI path. `commander` was used for trivial subcommand routing; replacing it with built-in `process.argv` parsing is ~40 lines, preserves all five subcommands (`list`, `get`, `search`, `use-case`, `stats`) and matching JSON output, and eliminates the install-time install step entirely. The MCP server entry point (`src/cli.js`, used by `npx @adobe/s2-docs-mcp`) keeps its `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` dep — that path goes through `npx` which does install deps, so it was never broken.

## Related Issue

Reported by garthdb after attempting to use the skill installed via PR #834.

## Motivation and Context

Without this fix the plugin is unusable. The skill's `lookup.js` shells out to `bin/s2-docs.js`, which fails immediately on the bare `commander` import.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `claude plugin validate` → ✔ Validation passed
- `node bin/s2-docs.js stats` / `use-case "form input"` / `list --category inputs` / `get Button` / `search picker` — all return the same JSON shape as before
- `cd /tmp && claude plugin marketplace add /path/to/repo && claude plugin install s2-docs@spectrum-design-data` → cache populated at `1.0.1/`
- `node ~/.claude/plugins/cache/spectrum-design-data/s2-docs/1.0.1/skills/s2-docs/scripts/lookup.js use-case "form input"` → returns the expected component list, no missing-module error
- Cleanup: uninstalled the plugin and removed the local marketplace from user settings

## Rollout note for already-installed users

Anyone who installed the broken `1.0.0` from PR #834 needs to refresh, otherwise their cache still has the commander-importing bin:

```
/plugin marketplace update
/plugin uninstall s2-docs
/plugin install s2-docs@spectrum-design-data
```

The `plugin.json` version bump to `1.0.1` should make `/plugin update` work too once Claude Code's update detector kicks in, but a clean reinstall is the surefire path.

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

author: bmwill
body:
…ation

`MultisigCommittee` deserialization does not enforce the invariants checked by `is_valid()` (nonzero threshold, 1..=10 members, no zero weights, threshold <= sum of weights, no duplicate members). Validity is enforced downstream by the verifier in `sui-crypto` before any signature is checked, but consumers that inspect a deserialized committee — counting members, summing weights, indexing by bitmap — without first verifying signatures may operate on malformed, attacker-supplied committees and observe nonsensical results (division by zero, double-counting, panics on out-of-bounds bitmap indices). Add a "Validity" section to the type's docs that calls this out and directs consumers to call `is_valid()` before relying on any committee field. Behavior is unchanged.

author: maciekish
body:
Single self-contained script that installs and configures an AmneziaVPN
(AmneziaWG protocol) road-warrior server on Linux. Designed to coexist
with stock WireGuard or other VPNs already on the host: dedicated
nftables tables prefixed amnezia_*, a non-default UDP port suggested
from a live conflict scan, and its own /etc/amnezia/amneziawg/awg0.conf.

Covers Debian/Ubuntu (PPA), Fedora/RHEL (COPR with source-build
fallback), and Arch (AUR helper or source build), with a userspace
amneziawg-go fallback when the kernel module cannot build.

Interactive prompts for endpoint host, port, IPv6 toggle, WAN egress
interface and an obfuscation profile (off / standard / aggressive),
all overridable via AMNEZIA_* env vars and AMNEZIA_NONINTERACTIVE=1
for unattended installs. Subcommands: install, add-client,
remove-client, list-clients, show-client, status, uninstall [--purge].

Sysctl forwarding is enabled via a single dedicated drop-in. NAT/MASQ
excludes RFC1918, CGNAT, link-local, ULA, multicast and loopback so
the server's local LAN stays unreachable from VPN clients. IPv6
support auto-detected from a global v6 address. Clients are issued
with a per-peer preshared key and a QR code (qrencode) for mobile.

### Motivation
- Ensure browser builds use browser-safe storage backends (IndexedDB + LocalStorage) and do not require the Cordova SQLite driver, while preserving SQLite support on native/Capacitor runtimes.
- Make startup diagnostics visible so the app reports which storage backend was selected and warn users when importing mobile exports that reference native file URIs.
- Preserve existing export/import formats and browser download/export behavior while documenting browser persistence limitations.

### Description
- Added a runtime-aware helper `getStorageDriverOrder()` in `src/main.ts` to provide `driverOrder` that omits `localforage-cordovasqlitedriver` for web runtimes and keeps the original order for native runtimes (IndexedDB, Cordova SQLite, LocalStorage).
- Updated `UIStorage.init()` in `src/services/uiStorage.ts` to register the Cordova SQLite driver only when a native/Capacitor runtime is detected and to log the active backend after creating storage.
- Added import-time migration diagnostics in `src/services/uiStorage.ts` by introducing `collectNonWebAttachmentPaths()` and `logWebImportMigrationHints()` and calling the hint logger during `import()` to detect native-only file URIs (`file://`, `content://`, `capacitor://`).
- Documented browser-mode persistence limitations and mobile→web import caveats in `README.md` and kept export/import/ZIP handling unchanged so browser users can still back up/download data files via the existing `UIFileHelper` browser download path.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run lint`, which failed in the CI environment due to package manager engine constraints (repo expects `pnpm` and current environment uses `npm`), not code lint errors.
- Ran `pnpm lint`, which failed in this environment because `package.json` contains an invalid `packageManager` specification for the local `pnpm` execution.
- No runtime/unit tests were executed in this environment; the changes are limited to driver selection, logging, and import-time diagnostics and do not alter export formats or ZIP handling.

author: peterdrier
body:
Closes nobodies-collective/Humans#627
Closes nobodies-collective/Humans#628 (with a design pivot — see below)

## Summary

- Single "Help" floating bubble replaces the two corner FABs (red `IssuesWidget` exclamation + green `AgentWidget` sparkles).
- Click opens a small popover menu: **Talk with AI Agent** (primary), **Create issue** (secondary).
- Agent item opens the panel; consent gate handles first-time consent and lists explicit caveats: full conversation log visible to user AND admins, history retained for `AgentSettings.RetentionDays` days then deleted (value threaded through `HelpWidgetModel` so the disclosure tracks the admin-configurable setting).
- Create issue → existing Issues modal, unchanged behavior.
- Both prior view components deleted; new `HelpWidgetViewComponent` + `Views/Shared/Components/HelpWidget/Default.cshtml`.
- Layouts (`_Layout`, `_AdminLayout`) invoke `HelpWidget` instead of the old two.

## Agent access expansion (was Phase 1 admin-only)

Per direction during PR review, the Phase 1 admin-only gate has been **removed**. The agent option now shows for any authenticated, consented user when `AgentSettings.Enabled = true`. `AgentController.Ask` was already only `[Authorize]` (no role check), so the backend boundary is unchanged — only the UI gate is gone.

`docs/sections/Agent.md` updated: Phase 1 admin-only language dropped, touch-and-clean rule rewritten, `AgentSettings.PreloadConfig` default left at `Tier1` (admin-tunable at runtime; flip to `Tier2` if non-admin questions start probing sections outside the preloaded index).

## Agent handoff redesign (closes #628 with a pivot)

#628 specced renaming `route_to_feedback` → `route_to_issue` while keeping the auto-create behavior. **This PR drops auto-create entirely.** The agent never writes Issue rows itself; the tool returns a proposal `{title, category, description}` and the client opens the Issues submission modal pre-filled. The user reviews and submits via existing `/Issues/Submit`.

Streaming bug fixed alongside: `AnthropicClient.StreamAsync` was emitting tool calls on `content_block_start` (when SDK `Input` is still `{}`), so args arrived empty. Now accumulates `partial_json` deltas across `content_block_delta` events and emits on `content_block_stop`.

## Conversations: shared admin/user URL

`/Agent/History` (user-only, with delete buttons, no viewer) and `/Agent/Admin/Conversations` (admin-only) collapsed into a single `/Agent/Conversations` route that adapts to the caller. Admins see all conversations + Human column + filters. Users see only their own (no Human column). Detail view at `/Agent/Conversations/{id}` shares the same template — admin sees token counts / tool invocations / "Show what would be sent to Anthropic" / handoff banner; user sees messages + refusal reasons.

Admin transcript now also surfaces tool invocations + args (`<details>` panel per assistant message reading from `AgentMessage.FetchedDocs`) so it's possible to verify what the agent actually sent.

## Out of scope

- No changes to the agent panel UI, the streaming pipeline, or the Issues modal markup.
- The Legal `agent-chat` document content lives in the `Statutes` repo, not here — caveat copy is inline at the consent gate.
- `IAgentService.DeleteConversationAsync` stays on the interface — no UI surface today; useful for GDPR / retention paths.
- Tool RESULT capture is not stored on `AgentMessage` (only `FetchedDocs` carries tool name + args). Follow-up if you want full result visibility in admin transcript.

## Test plan

- [ ] Lower-right shows one Help bubble.
- [ ] Click → menu opens with "Talk with AI Agent" first, "Create issue" second.
- [ ] Click outside / Escape closes the menu.
- [ ] As any authenticated, consented user (admin or not): pick AI Agent → panel opens straight to composer (or consent gate first time).
- [ ] As anonymous: no bubble at all.
- [ ] Pick "Create issue" → existing modal opens with all fields, submission still works.
- [ ] Mobile width (≤576px): menu fits within viewport, items remain tappable.
- [ ] Ask a question the agent can't answer (e.g., "what's on the calendar"): assistant bubble shows "I drafted an issue, please review and submit", Issues modal pops pre-filled with `{title, category, description}` from the model.
- [ ] Submit the pre-filled issue → lands as a normal Issue row (no `Source = AgentUnresolved` legacy linkage).
- [ ] As user, navigate to `/Agent/Conversations` → only own conversations, no Human column, no admin filters, no delete button. Click View → message thread visible (no token counts, no tool invocations panel).
- [ ] As admin, same URL → all conversations, Human column leftmost, filters, detail page shows token counts + tool invocations + "Show what would be sent to Anthropic" link.

- **`src/evaluation.py`**: `find_optimal_threshold` (Youden's J sweep), `get_roc_curve_data`, `perform_welch_t_tests`, `compute_feature_correlations`; AUC-ROC and F1 dropped from `compute_performance_metrics`

- **`app.py` / `templates/index.html`**: 2D Glucose-BMI model option and its preprocessing branch; model-selector radio group and JS toggle
- **`requirements.txt`**: `scipy`, `matplotlib`, `seaborn` (no remaining consumers)

- **`config.py`**: Replaced threshold/stats/plot config blocks with a single `DECISION_THRESHOLD = 0.5`
- **`main.py`**: Pipeline reduced to data cleaning → model training → evaluation at `threshold=0.5`; prints accuracy / sensitivity / specificity / precision + confusion matrix only
- **`app.py`**: `preprocess_input` simplified to 8D path only; message logic already consistent with ≥ 50% = higher risk

author: kelsonpw
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the wizard migration plan (#527). Fixes the `--agent` API 400 bug that makes `npx @amplitude/wizard --agent` unusable inside Claude Code, Cursor, and Cline.

**Root cause:** Vertex AI's Anthropic publisher endpoint does not honor the `context-1m-2025-08-07` beta. The wizard was unconditionally setting `betas: ['context-1m-2025-08-07']` in the Claude Agent SDK options on the gateway path. Vertex returns 400, Thunder's wizard-proxy wraps that as the verbatim `"Invalid request sent to model provider"` string, and the retry loop loops forever because the next request will be identically rejected. Thunder is a transparent forwarder — the rejection is upstream (verified by reading `~/amplitude-repos/javascript/server/packages/thunder/src/wizard-proxy/router.ts`).

## Changes

- **`agent-interface.ts:2969`** — gate `betas: ['context-1m-2025-08-07']` behind `AMPLITUDE_WIZARD_GATEWAY_BETAS=1`. Default off on the gateway path, preserved on the direct-API path where the beta is honored.
- **`agent-interface.ts`** — add `GATEWAY_INVALID_REQUEST` error type + fail-fast detection of the literal Thunder wrapper string. The retry loop short-circuits because retrying is futile; the runner surfaces a remediation message pointing users at upgrading the wizard or using `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to bypass the gateway.
- **`agent-interface.ts:2944-2948`** — pin `fallbackModel` to `claude-sonnet-4-6` so the fallback path matches `selectModel`'s production alias instead of the stale dated id.
- **`agent-runner.ts`** — handle `GATEWAY_INVALID_REQUEST` with a clear user-facing error and the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` bypass hint.
- **`agent-interface.test.ts`** — 4 regression tests:
  1. Pins the wire shape: no `betas` on the gateway path by default
  2. Pins opt-in: `betas` present on the direct-API path
  3. Post-stream fail-fast classification (result with `is_error: true`)
  4. Catch-branch fail-fast classification (thrown error with the marker)

## What is NOT in this PR

The migration plan calls for stripping `$schema` / `additionalProperties` / `exclusiveMinimum` / `exclusiveMaximum` from `tools[].input_schema` to harden against the same class of Vertex rejection on tool calls. The Claude Agent SDK uses its own zod adapter that doesn't emit those keys, so the shipped wizard isn't producing them today. That sanitizer is needed in **Phase 2a** when the harness moves to Vercel AI SDK (which uses zod-to-json-schema and does emit them).

## Pre-merge verification

- [ ] Confirm the exact Vertex rejection by reading Thunder's `[WizardProxy] Upstream error` logs in Datadog for a recent failing request. The proxy logs the upstream body (truncated to 500 chars) at `thunder/src/wizard-proxy/router.ts:927` with `LOG_PREFIX = '[WizardProxy]'`. This confirms whether the cause is the beta header (this PR's primary fix), schema noise (Phase 2a), or both.
- [ ] Internal eval suite shows no regression on the direct-API path.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1 src/lib/__tests__/agent-interface.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/agent-runner.test.ts` — 282 tests pass.
- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean.
- [x] `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean.
- [ ] Smoke test: `npx @amplitude/wizard@<this-build> --agent` inside Claude Code completes without 400.
- [ ] Smoke test: same inside Cursor's integrated terminal.
- [ ] Smoke test: same inside Cline.
- [ ] Telemetry on the `--agent` 400 rate after this ships drops by ≥95%.

## Related

- Migration plan PR: #527
- See `MIGRATION_PLAN.md` §2 for the full RCA and §7 Phase 1 for scope rationale.

author: adhithyan15
body:
## Summary

Standalone program that proves the entire matrix execution layer works on a real workload: takes a PPM image, applies an Instagram-style filter expressed as a MatrixIR graph, writes a PPM image.

\`\`\`
PPM bytes
   ↓
PixelContainer
   ↓
image-gpu-core (builds matrix_ir::Graph)
   ↓
matrix-runtime planner (lowers to compute-ir ComputeGraph)
   ↓
matrix-cpu executor (evaluates)
   ↓
PixelContainer
   ↓
PPM bytes
\`\`\`

If the matrix execution layer is broken, the output image is *visibly* wrong — colours shifted, gamma off, channels swapped, alpha lost. Much stronger smoke test than asserting \`[1, 2, 3]\` round-trips through a graph.

## Filters

| Filter | CLI | MatrixIR primitives exercised |
|--------|-----|------------------------------|
| invert | \`--filter invert\` | Const, Sub, Where |
| greyscale | \`--filter greyscale\` | Cast, Reshape, MatMul |
| sepia | \`--filter sepia\` | same + custom matrix |
| brightness | \`--filter brightness --amount N\` | Cast, Add, Min, Max, Where, Broadcast |
| gamma | \`--filter gamma --gamma G\` | Cast, Pow, Broadcast |
| contrast | \`--filter contrast --scale S\` | Cast, Sub, Mul, Add, Min, Max, Where, Broadcast |
| posterize | \`--filter posterize --levels L\` | Cast, Div, Mul, Where, Broadcast |

Together these exercise every primitive the matrix execution layer supports.

## End-to-end verified

Manual test on a 4×4 gradient PPM (values 0, 16, 32, …, 240):

\`\`\`
=== Original ===
First pixel: 0   0   0
Last  pixel: 240 240 240

=== Inverted ===
First pixel: 255 255 255   (255 - 0)
Last  pixel: 15  15  15    (255 - 240)

=== Brightness +50 ===
First pixel: 50  50  50
Last  pixel: 255 255 255   (saturated)

=== Sepia ===
Greys warmed toward orange (R ≥ G ≥ B confirmed)
\`\`\`

The pipeline is real.

## Test coverage: 22 passing

- 13 library tests (parameter validation, end-to-end filter dispatches on synthetic 2×2 images)
- 9 CLI argument-parser tests

\`\`\`
cargo test
test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed
\`\`\`

## File format

Input and output are **PPM (P6)** — the simple binary format that \`image-codec-ppm\` supports. PNG decode isn't yet implemented in this repo's PNG codec; once it is, this program will gain a \`--format\` flag and accept PNG.

ImageMagick converts: \`convert photo.jpg photo.ppm\` and back.

## Architecture

Standalone workspace per programs/rust convention (matches parrot, cowsay, etc.). Library half (\`src/lib.rs\`) handles filter selection and parameter validation; binary half (\`src/main.rs\`) handles CLI parsing and file I/O. Library half is fully unit-testable without touching the filesystem.

## Dependencies

\`\`\`
\$ cargo tree
instagram-filters
├── image-codec-ppm
├── image-gpu-core
└── pixel-container
\`\`\`

Only path deps. Zero external crates.

## Trust model

\`--input\` and \`--output\` are treated as literal filesystem paths (same trust model as \`cp\`). Path traversal is allowed at the user's discretion. Input file size capped at 64 MiB before reading to bound memory.

## What's next

This completes the V1 end-to-end story: matrix execution layer → image-domain library → application program.

Possible follow-ups:
- Real GPU executor (matrix-metal, matrix-cuda) — Instagram filters automatically get faster because the planner routes large workloads to GPU
- PNG codec read support (so this program can accept JPEG-converted images directly)
- Filter chains (\`--filter "sepia | contrast --scale 1.2"\`)
- Wire to \`cli-builder\` for richer help generation
- Begin neural network layer integration

author: simnaut
body:
Closes #301.

Extends the kinematic-only joint spec catalogue beyond the constant-rate single-axis primitive that PR #289 shipped. Force-controlled joints (with reaction forces, integrated joint dynamics) remain deferred under #276 — this PR is kinematic-only enrichment.

## Summary

Three new spec variants, each shipped as a sibling spec type alongside the existing `JointKinematicsSpec` (rather than refactoring it into an enum) so existing struct-literal call sites in tests and recipes keep compiling unchanged. A new unifying `JointKinematicsModel` enum is provided for callers that need heterogeneous joint collections.

### `SinusoidalJointKinematicsSpec`

Single-axis joint whose angle is

```
θ(t) = offset_rad + amplitude_rad · sin(omega_rad_per_s · t + phase_rad)
```

The kernel computes the analytic time-derivative for the angular velocity, so `dθ/dt = amplitude · ω · cos(ω · t + phase)` and the angular velocity in this-frame coordinates is `(dθ/dt) · axis_in_parent`. Useful for periodic articulation (pointing dither, antenna scan, gimbal sweep, slosh-style oscillation).

### `ClosureJointKinematicsSpec`

Single-axis joint pinned to a fixed rotation with no time dependence (`θ(t) = fixed_angle_rad`, `ω = 0`). The kinematic-only degenerate case useful for closing kinematic loops where one joint's pose is constrained at declaration time rather than driven through `θ(t)`.

### `MultiDofJointKinematicsSpec`

Up to `MAX_MULTI_DOF_AXES` (= 6) DOF chain. Each stage is a `SingleDofKinematics` variant (`ConstantRate` / `Sinusoidal` / `Closure`) declared in the *intermediate frame* produced by the preceding stages, matching the standard kinematic-chain convention. The kernel folds stages with `RefFrameState::incr_right` so the composed `(rotation, angular velocity)` is bit-identical to walking the equivalent N-entity frame-tree chain. Stages must be a contiguous prefix of the fixed-size axes array — the kernel asserts this; a "hole" in the middle panics with a diagnostic.

The fixed-size axes array (`[Option<SingleDofKinematics>; MAX_MULTI_DOF_AXES]`) keeps the spec `Copy`, which keeps `JointKinematicsModel` `Copy` and avoids per-tick allocation in the propagation path. Chains longer than 6 DOFs can be expressed as multiple chained joint frame entities (one frame per DOF) — also the JEOD-faithful pattern, since JEOD has no native multi-DOF joint primitive.

### `JointKinematicsModel`

Unifying enum over the four variants (`ConstantRate` / `Sinusoidal` / `Closure` / `MultiDof`). `evaluate_model(&model, t)` dispatches each variant to the matching per-spec kernel.

## Three-layer split

- **`jeod_dynamics::kinematic_joint`** — pure-math kernels. Each new evaluator validates `axis_in_parent` is unit-norm (within `AXIS_NORM_TOL`) and every spec scalar is finite, panicking with a fix-this-by message on violation.
- **`jeod_sim`** — re-exports the new spec types, kernel evaluators, and `MAX_MULTI_DOF_AXES` so the Bevy adapter and any other `jeod_sim` consumer (mission crates, `jeod_runner`, ...) reach the kernel through the single API surface.
- **`bevy_jeod`** — `SinusoidalJointKinematicsC` / `ClosureJointKinematicsC` / `MultiDofJointKinematicsC` Components (each with the same `#[require(FrameTransC, FrameRotC, FrameAngVelC)]` triplet contract as `JointKinematicsC`) and three sibling driver systems scheduled in `JeodSet::EphemerisUpdate` alongside `joint_kinematics_system`. The four kinematic-spec components are semantic alternatives — each entity carries at most one — so the four driver systems write disjoint storage and commute under EphemerisUpdate's parallelism.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --tests --examples -- -D warnings -D deprecated`
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'not test(tier3_)'` — 1060/1060 pass
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'test(bevy_parity_)'` — 21/21 pass
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- [x] `bash scripts/check_no_escape_hatches.sh`
- [x] `cargo test --test invariant_coverage`

New tests:

- 19 Tier-1 kernel tests in `kinematic_joint::tests` — closed-form values at known times (sinusoidal `t = 0` snapshot, sinusoidal quarter-period peak, closure constant over time, multi-DOF same-axis stages summing to aggregate, multi-DOF empty chain → identity, multi-DOF 1-stage matching constant-rate kernel, multi-DOF 2-stage matching manual `incr_right`), fail-loud on non-unit axes / non-finite scalars / hole-in-middle / over-`MAX_MULTI_DOF_AXES` slice length, and `JointKinematicsModel::evaluate_model` dispatch correctness.
- 7 Bevy integration tests in `tests/joint_kinematics.rs` ticking the `FixedUpdate` schedule end-to-end and pinning the per-component output bit-for-bit to direct kernel calls at the same elapsed time. Includes a sibling-driver test that spawns one entity per variant and asserts the four drivers tag disjoint entity sets without cross-write.
- `tests/bevy_reflect_smoke.rs` and `register_jeod_component_types` updated to cover the three new components.
