## Summary

Mirrors the existing `/venues/in/[region]` hyperlocal pattern for the vendor side of the catalog. Generates **104 new statically-rendered SEO surfaces** with templated copy, breadcrumbs, JSON-LD, and graceful empty states.

## Routes added

| Pattern | Pages | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `/vendors/category/[category]` | 14 | every DB category |
| `/vendors/in/[region]` | 6 | reuses venue regions |
| `/vendors/in/[region]/[category]` | 84 | full intersection (6×14) |

## Structural decisions worth flagging

- **Empty intersections render, never 404.** Per audit spec, e.g. `/vendors/in/naples/lighting` (no matches today) shows a card with four cross-links: "View all Lighting Designers statewide", "All vendors in Naples", "Browse the full directory", "Get matched via multi-quote". The 84-page grid stays coherent even with sparse cells. Verified in smoke testing.
- **`generateStaticParams` covers the full allowlist.** All 6×14 = 84 region×category combos are statically generated, even empty ones. URLs outside the allowlist (e.g. `/vendors/in/timbuktu`, `/vendors/category/baker-foo`) 404 via `notFound()` guards. Verified.
- **Sitemap only emits non-empty entries.** 55 of 104 routes have ≥1 vendor today; the rest stay out of `sitemap.xml` until they have content. Auto-catches up on each deploy.
- **Regions reused from `src/lib/hyperlocal.ts`** — vendors and venues share the same FL city → region map. New `src/lib/hyperlocalVendors.ts` holds the 14-category taxonomy + filter helpers and re-exports `REGIONS`/`RegionDef`.
- **Vendor card extracted to `<VendorListingCard />`** so all four surfaces (the existing `/vendors` listing plus the three new SEO patterns) share one JSX source of truth — no drift.
- **Each page emits BreadcrumbList + CollectionPage JSON-LD** via a new `vendorCollectionPageLD` helper.
- **Per-category intro copy** for all 14 categories — no boilerplate. Each opens with a one-line take on what makes that category matter.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean — all 104 paths static-generated successfully
- [x] `/vendors/category/florist` — title, breadcrumb, JSON-LD CollectionPage, H1 ✓
- [x] `/vendors/in/miami` — same ✓
- [x] `/vendors/in/miami/florist` — same ✓
- [x] `/vendors/in/naples/lighting` (genuinely empty: 0 lighting vendors in Naples) — empty state with 4 cross-link suggestions rendered ✓
- [x] `/vendors/in/florida-keys/lighting` (1 match: Kiss Me Entertainment in Key West) — listing renders with that vendor ✓
- [x] `/vendors/in/timbuktu` — 404 ✓
- [x] `/vendors/category/baker-foo` — 404 ✓
- [x] Sitemap includes 55 vendor SEO URLs (non-empty combos only) ✓

## Out of scope

- Pagination — caps out at ~7 vendors per category × region today, fits a single screen
- Vendor detail pages — untouched
- Watercolor placeholders — untouched
- Existing `/venues/*` hyperlocal pattern — untouched

## Resumo

- **`scripts/auto-implement-sped.ps1`** — orquestrador de automação que implementa registros SPED pendentes em loop sem intervenção manual
- **`.claude/commands/implementar-registro.md`** — skill do Claude Code com os 10 passos de implementação (PDF → código → testes → build → commit → PR)

## Como funciona o script

Para cada registro pendente no bloco alvo:
1. `git checkout dev && git pull`
2. Invoca `claude --print /implementar-registro --dangerously-skip-permissions`
3. Detecta o novo PR criado (snapshot diff antes/depois)
4. Poll `gh pr checks --json name,state,bucket` a cada 30s
5. Quando `bucket=pass`: `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch`
6. `git pull` + `git branch -d <branch-local>`
7. Repete para o próximo registro

Para imediatamente se CI falhar, exibindo URL do PR para revisão manual.

## Uso

```powershell
# Listar pendentes sem implementar
.\scripts\auto-implement-sped.ps1 -Bloco 0 -DryRun

# Automação completa do Bloco 0
.\scripts\auto-implement-sped.ps1 -Bloco 0

# Todos os blocos com Opus
.\scripts\auto-implement-sped.ps1 -Model opus

# Limitar a N PRs por sessão
.\scripts\auto-implement-sped.ps1 -Bloco 0 -MaxPRs 5
```

## Notas

- `settings.local.json` **não** commitado (caminhos locais hardcoded)
- Requer `gh` e `claude` CLIs autenticados no PATH

body:
## Summary
Five distinct improvements bundled, each its own commit:

1. **Ad-hoc codesign for unsigned builds** — root-cause fix for the \"Enable notifications\" silently no-opping (your screenshot in this thread)
2. **Daemon version bump** — \`imuDaemonVersion\` 0.2.0 → 0.3.0 (audit item #96)
3. **Contacts permission UI in Settings** with sample-lookup validation
4. **\"Compact all\" + per-row size + summary stats** in History
5. **WAL rolling snapshot buffer docs** — closes #76

## Why ad-hoc codesign matters
The linker-signed Mach-O that \`swift build\` emits has \`Info.plist=not bound\` and \`Sealed Resources=none\`. macOS treats that as an unstable code identity and refuses to register the bundle for **Notifications/Contacts/etc.**, so \`requestAuthorization()\` returns without prompting. Verified pre-fix on the running app:

\`\`\`
Identifier=IMUMenuBar
flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)
Info.plist=not bound
Sealed Resources=none
\`\`\`

Post-fix (after the new ad-hoc \`codesign --force --sign -\` step):

\`\`\`
Identifier=com.imessage-unsent.app
flags=0x2(adhoc)
Info.plist entries=13
Sealed Resources version=2 rules=13 files=1
\`\`\`

That difference is what TCC keys off of.

## What's new in the History view

**Summary bar** between the header and list shows: total count, total disk usage, recovered count, compacted count, not-recoverable count.

**Per-row metadata** now includes archive size (e.g. \"2.4 MB\") + a \"Compacted\" chip when applicable.

**\"Compact all\" button** in the header iterates compactable archives, calls the daemon's compact op for each, reports \"Compacted N — reclaimed X.X MB\".

## Contacts UI
- New \`ContactsPermissionModel\` mirrors \`NotificationPermissionModel\` shape (#99): \`@Published\` status + \`isRequesting\` + \`promptSuppressed\` + \`lastTestResult\`.
- Settings → Contacts:

  - Suppressed-prompt detection → pivots to \"Open System Settings\" with orange caption

- ✅ \`make gui-build\` clean

- ✅ \`codesign -dvv\` on the produced bundle confirms the new sealed Info.plist + bundle id

body:
### Description of your changes

When an override snapshot fails to apply on a selected resource, the binding's `Overridden=False` condition message now identifies **which** override snapshot and **which** target object failed, instead of surfacing only the underlying patch error.

Before:
> `Failed to apply the override rules on the resources: failed to process the request due to a client error: add operation does not apply: doc is missing key: /invalid`

After:
> `Failed to apply the override rules on the resources: ClusterResourceOverrideSnapshot "cro-2" failed to apply on Namespace "app": add operation does not apply: doc is missing key: /invalid`

**Implementation:** the wrap is done once at the outer `applyOverrides` call site so the existing controller-level message trim at `controller.go:188-194` works correctly without doubled sentinel prefixes. `applyOverrideRules` and `applyJSONPatchOverride` no longer call `controller.NewUserError` themselves — they return raw errors, and `applyOverrides` does the sentinel-tagging once with the snapshot + target context. `errors.Is(err, controller.ErrUserError)` still holds end-to-end.

Boy Scout cleanups limited to the files touched by this fix:
- `override.go` — `isClusterScopeResource` → `isClusterScopedResource`; capitalised log messages; `cluster.ObjectMeta.Labels` → `cluster.Labels`; doc comments on three unexported functions; redundant `// do nothing` dropped.
- `override_test.go` — `unmarshl` → `unmarshal` (3 sites); `clusterole` → `clusterRole`; corrected the wrong function name in a test failure diagnostic (`TestReplaceClusterLabelKeyVariables` was logging `applyJSONPatchOverride()`); `expected/expectErr` → `want/wantErr` per project style; test renamed `TestApplyOverrides_namespacedScopeResource` → `_namespaceScopedResource`; explanatory comment added for the inverted-looking `IsClusterScopedResource: false` `FakeManager` flag.
- `controller_integration_test.go` — double-space typos in `By(...)` strings.

I have:

- [ ] Associated this change with a known KubeFleet Issue (Bug, Feature, etc).
- [x] Run `make reviewable` to ensure this PR is ready for review.

### How has this code been tested

- `make test` passes (`pkg/controllers/workgenerator` runs 86 Ginkgo specs plus unit tests; `pkg/utils/condition` and `pkg/controllers/placement` unaffected and green).
- **Unit coverage:**
  - `TestApplyOverrides_clusterScopedResource` and `TestApplyOverrides_namespaceScopedResource` gained a `wantErrSubstr` field. Four failure cases now assert on the new message format (snapshot identity + target identity), including two cases that previously had no `wantErrSubstr` and would have surfaced an empty snapshot name post-change.
  - New case for the `IsClusterMatched` error path through `applyOverrideRules` (an invalid `MatchExpressions` `Operator` makes `metav1.LabelSelectorAsSelector` fail). This path was previously unexercised in `override_test.go`.
- **Integration coverage:**
  - The existing `Bound ClusterResourceBinding … invalid override` context now asserts via `MatchRegexp` on the new message structure.
  - New sibling context `Bound ClusterResourceBinding … invalid resource override` mirrors the CRO failure path for `ResourceOverrideSnapshot`. New fixture `invalidResourceOverrideSnapshot` (`ro-2`) added in `suite_test.go`.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- **Single-call wrap is intentional.** `applyOverrideRules` and `applyJSONPatchOverride` no longer call `controller.NewUserError`. Re-wrapping an already-tagged error created a doubled `"failed to process the request due to a client error: "` prefix that the trim at `controller.go:188-194` couldn't strip cleanly. Doing the wrap once at `applyOverrides` keeps the `%w: <suffix>` shape the trim expects.
- **Trim untouched.** The pre-existing trim at `controller.go:188-194` and its `//TODO: check if it's user error and set a different failed reason` are unchanged; cleaning that up is a separate refactor.
- **Scope discipline.** Two follow-on improvements were considered and explicitly deferred to keep this PR focused:
  - Firing a Kubernetes `Event` on `Overridden=False` so `kubectl describe binding` shows the same enriched message.
  - Enriching the CRP/RP `Overridden=False` rollup condition message with the failing cluster names instead of just a count.

body:
## Summary

Fix: `uipath-maestro-flow` skill was not presenting user choices as dropdowns at decision points despite SKILL.md rule #5 mandating the `AskUserQuestion` pattern.

**Root cause:** `AskUserQuestion` was missing from the `allowed-tools` frontmatter list in `SKILL.md`. Claude Code enforces `allowed-tools` as a hard gate — when a skill is active, any tool not on the list is unavailable, regardless of what prompts instruct. So the rule was unreachable. Every peer skill that uses dropdowns (`uipath-maestro-case`, `uipath-coded-apps`, `uipath-agents`, `uipath-planner`, `uipath-review`, `uipath-feedback`) lists it explicitly; this skill did not.

## Changes

### Primary fix — unblock the tool

- `SKILL.md` — add `AskUserQuestion` to `allowed-tools`.

### Convert finite-choice user prompts to dropdowns

Eight decision points were phrased as free-form chat prompts. Each now uses `AskUserQuestion` with a "Something else" escape hatch:

| File | Decision point |
|---|---|
| `references/author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md` (×2) | Multiple connection matches; missing required fields with finite value sets |
| `references/author/references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md` | Missing required event-parameter fields with finite value sets |
| `references/author/references/plugins/http/impl.md` | Empty connections list — Create / Manual mode / Skip / Something else |
| `references/author/references/editing-operations.md` | Rung-5 scripted-mutation gate — Edit / Write / Approve script / Cancel / Something else |
| `references/operate/references/ship.md` | Publish target ambiguous — Studio Web / Orchestrator / Something else |
| `references/operate/references/run.md` | Run mode — Debug / Process run / Job inspection / Something else |
| `references/operate/references/manage.md` | Instance action — Pause / Resume / Cancel / Retry / Something else |
| `references/diagnose/references/troubleshooting-guide.md` | Next action — Re-author / Retry / Cancel / Escalate / Something else |

### Reinforcement at script-mutation gate call sites

The rung-5 gate is referenced from multiple journey docs. Added inline `via AskUserQuestion` mentions so an agent reading the call site doesn't have to follow the link to learn how to ask:

- `references/author/references/brownfield.md`
- `references/author/references/greenfield.md`
- `references/author/references/editing-operations.md` (lines 7 and 21, in addition to the canonical rung-5 spec at line 13)

### Diagnose CAPABILITY inheritance

- `references/diagnose/CAPABILITY.md` — added `AskUserQuestion dropdown pattern` to the inherited-rules callout for parity with Author and Operate.

## Deliberately not converted

- **`flow debug` consent gate** — destructive-action consent should require typed acknowledgement, not a click. Same reasoning as force-push confirmations. Free-form prompt stays.
- **Plugin "two kinds — choose based on…" guidance** (HITL/agent/inline-agent planning docs) — agent-internal heuristics with explicit prefer-X defaults, not user-facing prompts.
- **"Open Questions" sections in planning docs** — by design, these are written-document artifacts in the architectural plan the user reviews offline, not interactive prompts.

## Coverage

Files referencing `AskUserQuestion`: **6 → 15** skill files.

author: kaeawc
body:
## Summary
pgmem-go is in-memory and doesn't carry actual index machinery, so CREATE / DROP INDEX accept the syntax migration tools and sqlc-init emit but do nothing at exec time. The IR fields (Name, Table, Concurrently, IfNotExists / IfExists) let a future indexed-scan piece grow the behaviour without an IR rev.

## Parsed shapes
- \`CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX [CONCURRENTLY] [IF NOT EXISTS] [name] ON table [USING method] (col [, …]) [WHERE …]\`
- \`DROP INDEX [CONCURRENTLY] [IF EXISTS] name [, …]\`

Anonymous index (no name), partial-index predicates, the USING method clause, and the column / expression list all parse and are discarded. \`parseCreate\` / \`parseDrop\` dispatch on the second token so TABLE / VIEW / INDEX live side by side.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)
- Real indexed scans
- \`ALTER INDEX\`, \`REINDEX\`, \`CREATE INDEX … INCLUDE\`

- [x] \`go test -race ./...\`
- [x] \`golangci-lint run ./...\`

body:
## Summary

- Rewrite `SCENE_ANALYSIS_INSTRUCTIONS` as a procedural prompt with explicit `ROLE / SCOPE / INPUTS / PROCEDURE / HARD CONSTRAINTS` sections so the agent systematically uses the data the `views_manifest.json` actually provides — `stableId` as the join key with `scene.json`, `bboxPx` for image-localized attention, `depthHint` for occlusion disambiguation, and per-view `cameraForward/Up/Right` for an explicit image-axis ↔ world-axis mapping that grounds axis inference.
- Preserve PR #25's descriptive-only scope: no FuncSpec classification, no `roles`, no `interaction_params.type`. The new prompt names FuncSpec types only in the SCOPE negative list and explicitly forbids them in `HARD CONSTRAINTS`.
- Reflect the mandatory contract in code: `input_items.build_input_items` now raises `ValueError` when the manifest text or required images are missing, instead of silently dropping them.
- Remove the now-redundant `IMAGE_ANALYSIS_TASK` prefix (`backend/pipeline/settings.py`) and its callsite in `backend/jobs/runner.py`. Update the small `SCENE_FEEDBACK_INSTRUCTIONS` test prompt to match the new contract (no \"optional\").

## Why

The previous prompt described `VIEWS_MANIFEST_JSON` and images as *optional*, even though `runner.py` enforces both as required files. More importantly, it never told the LLM *how* to use the manifest: the rich per-object/per-view localization data (pixel rectangles, depth, camera matrices) was passed as a JSON dump but unexplained, so the model treated images as anonymous visual context and fell back to naive bounding-box heuristics for axis inference. The new procedural structure walks the model through cross-referencing, image localization, and a deterministic axis-mapping step before any inference.

## Reviewer notes

- The restructured prompt is longer overall, but the increase is structural (numbered steps, input schema, hard constraints) rather than additional content.
- The `roles` / `funcspec_type` separation introduced in PR #25 is preserved end-to-end. The 6 regression tests added there (`test_excludes_roles_and_funcspec_type` across all trim levels, plus the `assert \"roles\" not in summary` check in `test_scene_understanding.py`) all stay green.
- `SEND_IMAGES_TO_AGENT` is intentionally left in place as a test/debug toggle — it now only matters when `include_images=False` is passed explicitly.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest` — all 146 tests pass (vs. 140 pre-PR-#25; the 6 new regression tests are unaffected).
- [x] `python -c \"from constants.agent_instructions import SCENE_ANALYSIS_INSTRUCTIONS\"` — module loads.
- [x] Negative paths: empty `views_manifest_text` and empty `images` (with `include_images=True`) both raise `ValueError`.
- [x] `grep -r IMAGE_ANALYSIS_TASK` — no residual importers.
- [ ] End-to-end run against the Cubes example scene — verify `scene_understanding.objects[].stable_id` matches manifest entries and no `roles` / `interaction_params.type` leak into the output.

author: brukhabtu
body:
## Summary

Implements **TASK-17**: split `binder/binder.py` (1187 lines, one class) into topical modules of free functions taking a `BinderState` dataclass. The `Binder` class is kept as a thin facade so existing call sites work unchanged; **TASK-18** removes the facade.

## Layout

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| `binder.py` | **155** | `bind()` entry point + `visit_node` dispatch + `Binder` facade |
| `state.py` | 39 | `BinderState` dataclass (all shared state for one bind() run) |
| `helpers.py` | 141 | Pure utilities: location/span, hash, target/docstring extraction, ref-kind, symbol-id, relative-import resolution |
| `imports.py` | 120 | `import` / `import_from` / `global` / `nonlocal` |
| `references.py` | 287 | `identifier` / `call` / `attribute_call` / `attribute` + receiver chain |
| `assignments.py` | 260 | `=` / `+=` / walrus / `for` / `with` / `except` + variable declarations |
| `scopes.py` | 333 | `function` / `class` / `decorated` / `lambda` / `comprehension` + parameters |
| `scope_stack.py` | 178 | unchanged |

`binder.py`: **1187 → 155** lines. Total LOC roughly preserved (just relocated).

## Architectural rationale

The `Binder` is a transient one-shot AST visitor whose state never outlives a single `bind()` call. It fails the "what does this carry between calls?" test for class-vs-function design — the state exists for one transformation, then is discarded. Modern Python static analysis tools (`mypy`, `pyright` internals, `astroid`) model this as functions over a state dataclass.

Mixin-style inheritance was considered and rejected as a 2010-era pattern that doesn't fit Python (implicit shared attrs, MRO complexity, pretends to be polymorphism it isn't).

Internal mutation of `BinderState` is acceptable because the state has bounded lifetime within one `bind()` call and never escapes the binder package. The composed `bind()` function is pure from outside.

## Mutual recursion

`visit_node` calls visitors; visitors recurse via `visit_node`. Handled via late imports inside the functions that recurse — avoids circular imports at module load time without forcing every signature to take `visit_node` as a parameter.

## Test plan

- [x] All 287 tests pass without modification
- [x] Re-indexed pypeeker's own `src/`; self-validation tests still pass (same FileIndex shape, same observations on real code)
- [x] Public API unchanged: `Binder(adapter, file_path, source).bind(root) -> FileIndex` works exactly as before
- [x] New entry point: `bind(adapter, file_path, source, root) -> FileIndex` works as a module-level function (used by the facade)

## What this PR does *not* do

- Does not remove the `Binder` class — that's TASK-18, which also migrates `cli.py`, `applier.py`, and `tests/conftest.py` to call `bind()` directly.
- Does not change behavior, the FileIndex shape, or any test expectations.

### Motivation
- Prevent downstream (CE2/CE4) from blocking on CE1 implementation by freezing the minimal CE1 I/F contract and error semantics contract-only. 
- Ensure deterministic behavior and fail-safe boundaries (preview gate, hash determinism, SafeMode) while keeping implementation details out of the contract.

### Description
- Appended a `Stream C update (2026-05-04)` section to `01_Plans/issues/issue-CE1-context-query-bundle-foundation.md` that records a 6-phase workflow (`Read Sync`, `ADR`, `Plan`, `Execute`, `Verify`, `Proceed`) and enforces docs-only / contract-only scope. 
- Fixed CE1 v1 contract semantics by making `ContextQueryV1`/`ContextBundleV1` closed-world and rejecting unknown keys with `400 unknown_contract_key`, requiring `previewConfirmed=false -> 422 preview_required`, and enforcing deterministic hashes where `queryCanonicalHash`/`bundleHash` are canonical JSON + `sha256(lowercase-hex)` and mismatches yield `409 nondeterministic_bundle` (3/3 match requirement). 
- Declared handoff keys (`queryCanonicalHash`, `bundleHash`, `sourceBundleHash`, `equivalenceKey`) and mandated mock-first decoupling so CE2/CE4 can proceed without CE1 implementation, with no handler/UI/DB/worker implementation details included. 
- Reaffirmed SafeMode boundary by referencing `CE0-SAFEMODE-IF` read-only and prohibiting preview bypass / SafeMode relaxation in the CE1 contract text.

body:
## What changed

- Refactored ingestion scrapers into smaller shared modules for company metadata, detail merging, HTTP fetching, salary normalization, seniority inference, skill extraction, remote detection, and text cleanup.
- Introduced shared scraper behavior through a reusable `JobSource` trait.
- Updated existing scrapers such as `work_ua`, `robota_ua`, `djinni`, and `dou_ua` to use the new modular scraper helpers.
- Added resilient HTTP fetching with retry/backoff handling for rate limits and server errors.
- Improved job detail enrichment flow so listing data can be merged with detail-page data in a consistent way.
- Improved scraper output reporting by tracking attempted, failed, and successfully normalized jobs.
- Optimized profile-ranked job loading by fetching job views in batch instead of one-by-one.
- Added small API runtime hardening changes, including reusable ML health client behavior and conservative auth route rate limiting.

## Why

The scraper layer was becoming too large and duplicated across sources. This change moves shared logic into focused modules so new sources can be added with less copy-paste and existing scrapers become easier to maintain.

It also improves ingestion reliability by making HTTP failures, detail-page failures, and partial normalization easier to handle and observe.

author: mashkovd
body:
## Summary

Follow-up **PR-B** to PR #16 (bare upstream merge to v2026.5.2).

The 2026.5.2 upstream sync added several auto-triggered workflows pinned to Blacksmith runners. On the mctlhq fork those jobs sit QUEUED forever and leave every PR stuck in the UNSTABLE merge state — exactly what's happening on PR #16 right now.

This PR mirrors the existing pattern from `558dbe113e ci: skip upstream Blacksmith pipelines on the mctlhq fork` (which guarded `ci.yml`, `install-smoke.yml`, `labeler.yml`).

## Changes

Added `if: github.repository == 'openclaw/openclaw'` to entry jobs only — downstream jobs already gate via `needs:` and auto-skip:

| Workflow | Entry job(s) guarded | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `codeql.yml` | `security-high` | pull_request, schedule |
| `codeql-critical-quality.yml` | `quality-shards`, `ui-control-plane`, `web-media-runtime-boundary` | pull_request, schedule |
| `live-media-runner-image.yml` | `build` | push to main |
| `openclaw-performance.yml` | `kova` | schedule |
| `opengrep-precise.yml` | `scan` | pull_request |
| `qa-live-transports-convex.yml` | `authorize_actor` | schedule |
| `stale.yml` | `stale`, `backfill-stale-closures`, `lock-closed-issues` | schedule |

## Why these and not others

`workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` only workflows from the same merge — `npm-telegram-beta-e2e.yml`, `openclaw-live-and-e2e-checks-reusable.yml`, `openclaw-release-checks.yml`, `opengrep-precise-full.yml`, `package-acceptance.yml`, `plugin-prerelease.yml` — don't need guards. They never auto-fire on the fork.

## Validation

Locally on this branch (post-PR #16 merge):
- `pnpm tsgo` ✅
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` ✅
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` ✅
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` ✅
- `pnpm lint` ✅
- `pnpm check:workflows` ✅
- YAML syntax check on all 7 modified files ✅

CI on this PR itself should now actually complete (not all QUEUED) — that's the verification.

## Next step

Once green, tag merge commit as `v2026.5.2-mctl.1` (per fork release flow) → `Docker Release` workflow publishes `ghcr.io/mctlhq/mctl-openclaw:2026.5.2-mctl.1` → bump `mctl-gitops` admins canary.

### Motivation
- Corregir el flujo de Remitos para que registre solo: proveedor, productos existentes y cantidades, sin tocar precios ni crear productos desde el remito.
- Evitar que campos de precio/costo/IVA/flete/ganancia se usen o se calculen durante la carga de remitos, dejando esa responsabilidad al módulo Productos/Precios.
- Permitir búsqueda de proveedor por nombre o CUIT y una alta rápida de proveedor durante la carga del remito.

### Description
- Frontend: actualicé `app/index.html` para agregar buscador de proveedor por nombre/CUIT y botón de alta rápida, y cambié la tabla de remito a columnas: producto, cantidad que entra, stock actual, stock nuevo y acción.
- Frontend: reescribí `app/main.js` para que el buscador de remitos busque producto por nombre, eliminar la creación/edición de precios desde el remito, eliminar asociación/creación de producto desde remito y mantener `remitoDetalles` con solo `productoId`, `productoNombre`, `cantidad` y `stockActual`.
- Frontend: añadí `renderProveedoresRemito()` para filtrar proveedores por nombre/CUIT y un handler de alta rápida de proveedor que solicita datos mínimos (nombre obligatorio, teléfono/CUIT/observaciones opcionales) y selecciona el proveedor creado.
- Backend: modifiqué `POST /remitos-proveedor` en `server.js` para validar y crear remito + detalles, sumar stock a cada producto y crear movimientos de stock tipo `ENTRADA` con motivo `Remito proveedor N°...`, sin modificar precios ni recalcular costos; además se eliminó el uso del tipo de cambio en este flujo.

Wires `assertNoRecurrentSynapseOnForwardOnly(...)` as a post-condition at every combiner producer site so that any future corruption throws a `TopologyError` naming the producing pipeline rather than surfacing as a downstream `[loadFrom] Stripping recurrent synapse` warning. Closes #2515. ## Evidence Backend-only change — no UI to screenshot. Verified via: - Unit tests for `normaliseCreatureExport` (4 tests) covering round-trip exports, idempotent re-normalisation, output-id remapping, and UUID-keyed wire inputs. All assert the forward-only invariant (`from < to` against `buildIdToIndexMap`). - Lifecycle integration tests covering every branch of `applyChangeToCreature` (8 tests): `add-synapses` (legal + adversarial), `add-neurons`, `change-squash`, `remove-synapse`, `remove-neuron`, and `coordinated-structural` (legal + adversarial). - All 525 discovery tests and 158 lifecycle/ErrorGuidedStructuralEvolution tests still pass. - `./quality.sh --lint-only` and `./quality.sh --check-only` are clean. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Discovery candidate] --> B[applyChangeToCreature] B --> C[normaliseCreatureExport] C --> D[apply* combiner] D --> E[validateAndFixCreatureSync] E --> F[assertNoRecurrentSynapse
OnForwardOnly] F -->|fails| G[TopologyError
names producer] F -->|ok| H[return candidate] ``` Producer tags wired in: | Site | Source tag in `TopologyError` | | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | | `applyAddSynapses` | `discovery:applyAddSynapses` | | `applyAddNeurons` | `discovery:applyAddNeurons` | | `applyChangeSquash` | `discovery:applyChangeSquash` | | `applyRemoveSynapse` | `discovery:applyRemoveSynapse` | | `applyRemoveNeuron` | `discovery:applyRemoveNeuron()` | | `applyCoordinatedStructuralCandidate` | `discovery:applyCoordinatedStructuralCandidate` | ## Test Plan - `test/architecture/NormaliseCreatureExportForwardOnly.ts` — 4 tests. - `test/lifecycle/ForwardOnlyApplyChangeLifecycle.ts` — 8 tests. - Existing tests unchanged: `ForwardOnlyAssertion`, `ForwardOnlyLifecycle`, `CandidateApplicationOps`, `DiscoveryCandidatesForwardOnlyVersionBump`, all green. Diagnostic note: `docs/issue-2515-forward-only-apply-audit.md` summarises the audit, the producer tags, and the path that was confirmed (no current introduction site found — the post-conditions are the load-bearing defence-in-depth that names the producer if a regression ever lands). --- 🤖 Processed by: stservice

## Souhrn (noční dávka, 9 feature commitů + 2 chore)

Doplnění toho, co README slibovala ale chybělo, plus production-grade SaaS featury.

### Velké přídavky
1. **Dietary značky + alergeny** (`f14e6e3`) — `is_vegetarian/_vegan/_gluten_free/_lactose_free/_spicy/_featured` + EU alergeny 1–14. Frontend je už používal, backend nevracel → menu rendrovalo prázdná místa. Teď to funguje napříč.
2. **Profil restaurace** (`e13e27f`) — logo, telefon, adresa, otevírací doba, web. Zobrazí se v hlavičce veřejného menu.
3. **Print stylesheet + health endpoint** (`923dff6`) — `Ctrl+P` na `/menu/:slug` produkuje čistý A4 list. `/api/health` vrací 503 na DB fail.
4. **Password reset** (`13cfaa8`) — `/forgot` (anti-enum, 5/h rate-limit), `/reset` (1h token, single-use).
5. **Export/import menu** (`673e769`) — JSON dump (schema_version: 1) + import s `replace?` flagem.
6. **Bulk + duplicate** (`91c45a5`) — duplikace položky, bulk-availability na celou kategorii.
7. **PWA** (`c2748a5`) — service worker + manifest. Veřejné menu funguje offline (stale-while-revalidate).
8. **Admin item search** (`fe7507e`) — vyhledávací box napříč CZ/EN názvy a popisy.

### Bezpečnost / ops
- Rate-limiting /api/auth/login (10/15min), /register (5/h), /forgot (5/h)
- CORS allowlist přes CORS_ORIGINS env var
- app.set('trust proxy', 1)
- Validace registrace (email regex, heslo ≥6, jméno 1-120)
- /api/health 503 na DB fail

### Bugfixy
- db.js oříznutý export `module.exports.toN` → toNum se nikdy neexportoval
- trial_expires_at se nikdy nenastavovalo při registraci → trial-expiring email se nikdy neposlal
- SlugEditor hardcoded loca.lt → window.location.origin
- og:image via.placeholder.com (offline od 2024) → placehold.co + skip data: URLs
- Cena 199 → 299 Kč napříč

## Test plan
- [ ] backend test.js pokrývá všechny nové endpointy
- [ ] vite build
- [ ] Smoke: register → seed-demo → veřejné menu zobrazí badges
- [ ] Settings: profil + logo
- [ ] Forgot/reset flow
- [ ] Print preview Ctrl+P
- [ ] PWA: SW se zaregistruje, offline test

## Otevřené (následující várka)
- DB backup strategie (cron + S3)
- Strukturované logování
- Zod / Joi validace zbylých endpointů
- Real item-view tracking
- PWA install prompt

## Summary

Bumps `github.com/getlantern/broflake` to the post-#360 pseudo-version (no tag — broflake's `go.mod` already uses pseudo-versions, so a hash-based bump is what we want).

## What this picks up

- [getlantern/unbounded#360](https://github.com/getlantern/unbounded/pull/360) — `clientcore`: classify QUIC connection errors for triage. Adds `err_class` and `lifetime_s` structured-log fields to every "QUIC connection ended" record. Maps quic-go errors into `idle_timeout`, `handshake_timeout`, `application_close_remote`, `application_close_local`, `transport_error`, `stateless_reset`, `context_canceled`, etc.
- [getlantern/unbounded#359](https://github.com/getlantern/unbounded/pull/359) — `egress`: integration test for connection migration. Test-only; no runtime change.

## Why

Two PRs ago the laptop's `lantern.log` had the same opaque `"QUIC connection error (<err>), closing!"` line for every failure mode. After this bump ships on a Lantern client, the per-connection record will look like:

```
level=DEBUG pkg=broflake msg="QUIC connection ended"
  err=...
  err_class=idle_timeout|application_close_remote|context_canceled|...
  lifetime_s=42.3
```

Grep + `sort | uniq -c` on `err_class` gives a histogram. After ~24-48h of usage, that histogram tells us whether `idle_timeout` dominates (→ confirms the consumer-side QUIC-state GC theory for the prod migration failures Nelson reported, fix is bumping `MaxIdleTimeout` in `common/QUICCfg`) or whether something else is the dominant failure mode (different fix).

## Test plan

- [x] `go mod tidy` clean
- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean (the existing pre-existing `unsafe.Pointer` warning in `protocol/amnezia/endpoint.go:50` is unchanged)
- [ ] After this lands and is bumped through radiance + lantern, grep the laptop's `lantern.log` for `QUIC connection ended` and break down by `err_class` over a couple days

## Summary
- Adds daemon-side handling for MachineOperation CRs, including the in-node `NodeReboot` operation and `AgentUpgrade` operation type plumbing.
- Registers a local Machine CR from the agent daemon when one does not already exist, then runs a controller-runtime loop scoped to the local Node/Machine.
- Updates bootstrapper RBAC and generated CRDs so bootstrap-token-authenticated agents can watch local state and update operation status.
- Extends agent E2E coverage to create a `NodeReboot` MachineOperation, verify the node reboot event/boot ID change, and assert operation completion state.

## Validation
- `go test ./cmd/agent/internal/daemon`
- `python3 -m py_compile hack/agent/e2e-kind/e2e.py`
- PR CI passed, including `agent-e2e`, `Verify Generated Files`, `Test`, `Lint`, `Build`, and `smoke`.
- Manually validated on Azure VM `unbounded-agent-vm`: node joined Ready, daemon registered Machine CR, `NodeReboot` MachineOperation completed with `NodeReboot completed`, and the node returned Ready.

## Notes
- The daemon currently assumes the Kubernetes Node name matches the host hostname; the code keeps a TODO to make node naming deterministic and pass it into kubelet config later.
- `AgentUpgrade` is added as an operation kind, but this PR only implements executable daemon behavior for `NodeReboot`.

## Summary
This PR resolves **56 security vulnerabilities**, reducing them from 56 to 20 (64% reduction) and eliminating all critical severity issues.

## Security Improvements
- ✅ Reduced total vulnerabilities: **56 → 20** (64% reduction)
- ✅ **Eliminated all critical severity vulnerabilities**
- ✅ Fixed all high severity issues except 2 (from fetch-mock dependency)
- ⚠️ Remaining: 18 moderate, 2 high (all in dev dependencies)

## Critical Security Fixes

### Production Dependencies
- **axios**: `0.27.2 → 1.16.0`
  - Fixes: CSRF, SSRF, DoS, header injection vulnerabilities
  - CVEs: Multiple high-severity issues resolved
  
- **react-router-dom**: `6.16.0 → 6.30.3`
  - Fixes: XSS vulnerability via open redirects
  - CVE: GHSA-2w69-qvjg-hvjx

- **lodash**: `4.17.21 → 4.18.1`
  - Fixes: Prototype pollution vulnerabilities
  
- **postcss**: `8.3.3 → 8.5.14`
  - Fixes: XSS vulnerabilities

### Red Hat Cloud Services Dependencies
- `@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components`: `6.1.1 → 7.4.1`
- `@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-notifications`: `6.1.14 → 6.6.1`
- `@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-utilities`: `6.0.0 → 7.0.9`
- `@redhat-cloud-services/rbac-client`: `1.2.2 → 4.2.5`

### Testing Dependencies
- **cypress**: `14.5.4 → 15.10.0`
- **@cypress/code-coverage**: `3.14.7 → 4.0.3`
- **jest-environment-jsdom**: `29.7.0 → 30.3.0`
- **fetch-mock**: Kept at `9.10.7` (v12 has breaking API changes)

## Code Changes

### RBAC Client API Migration
Updated code to use the new `@redhat-cloud-services/rbac-client` v4 API:
- **Before**: Class-based `new AccessApi().getPrincipalAccess(app)`
- **After**: Function-based `getPrincipalAccess({ application: app })`

**Files modified**:
- `src/utils/insights-common-typescript/RbacUtils.ts`
- `src/components/NotificationsDrawer/DrawerSingleton.tsx`

## Testing
- ✅ All 274 tests passing
- ✅ Lint checks passing
- ✅ Pre-push hooks passing

## Remaining Vulnerabilities (20 total)
- **18 moderate**: uuid package (v14.0.0) in dev dependencies
  - Affects: cypress, webpack-dev-server, nyc, sockjs
  - Impact: Development/testing only, does not affect production builds
  
- **2 high**: fetch-mock 9.x (path-to-regexp dependency)
  - Note: fetch-mock 12.x has breaking API changes requiring test refactoring
  - Impact: Development/testing only

## Future Work
- Migrate fetch-mock tests to v12 API to resolve remaining high severity issues
- Update container base image Node version from 16 to 18 or 20 LTS

## Deployment Notes
- No breaking changes for end users
- All tests passing
- Safe to merge and deploy
